2D rigid body physics. (Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change, the original src/experimental/physics2d/)
- Rigid bodies (static, kinematic, dynamic), shapes (circle, capsule, segment, convex polygon, chain), joints (distance, revolute, weld, wheel), collision filters, sensors,
  contact and sensor events, ray and shape queries, fixed steps and substeps, island sleeping, and the RigidBody2D component that connects nodes to bodies.
- The basis is the features of Box2D 3 (Erin Catto's talks and public writing) and Unity 2D physics (Rigidbody2D, Collider2D). It was written from published methods without porting anyone's code.
- Same API and same math as the Experimental namespace physics of the original vanilla.js. The math is f64 in both engines and the trigonometric functions are hand-written,
  so creating in the same order and calling the same step gives results identical to the bit. (the test comparison_matches_vanilla_js compares against a dump written by the original)
- Differences from the original: vectors are the f64 PhysicsVector2. (the Rust engine Vector2 is f32) User values are u64.
2D 그리기 대상. (원본 캔버스와 그 2D 컨텍스트): 2D drawing target. (the original canvas and its 2D context)
2D 그리기 대상. (원본과 게임이 document.createEleme:
2D drawing target. (in place of the browser canvas that the original and games use through document.createElement("canvas") and getContext("2d"))
- The original engine bakes text, shading and shadows onto offscreen canvases (getBakeCanvas and getAtlasCanvas return those canvases),
  and games create their own canvases, draw paths, gradients, shadows, clips, images and text, then hand them to the engine as images. (glossy UI shells, logo atlases, sprite cropping, pixel measuring)
- In the Rust version, a single Canvas2D is both the canvas and its 2D context. Function names are the CanvasRenderingContext2D names converted to Rust conventions.
  (fillRect → fill_rect, fillStyle = → set_fill_style, getImageData → get_image_data) The same goes for Path2D, CanvasGradient, CanvasPattern and ImageData.
  What is drawn is turned into an engine Image with to_image and used in places such as Graphic and UIImageView. (returns the same Image if nothing changed)
- On the web, it draws directly to a browser canvas (a canvas element not attached to the document) and its 2D context, as in the original.
- Desktop has no browser, so the engine does the same work. It paints with tiny-skia, a Rust port of the Skia CPU rasterizer that Chrome uses.
  (the same version resvg already uses, no extra crates to download) Path points are transformed by the transform at the time they are added, as in the original, and gradients and patterns follow the transform at paint time.
  Path arc, ellipse, arcTo and roundRect store the same conic curves as Chrome, using the math of Blink canvas_path.cc and Skia SkPathBuilder,
  and at paint time they are split into quadratic curves within 0.25 device pixels, like the Skia CPU raster. (SkAutoConicToQuads, the old chop version Chrome uses)
  An engine Image whose CPU pixels were released on GPU upload is drawn by reading back its texture. (same as when Chrome draws a GPU-resident image onto a CPU canvas)
  Shadows paint the shape separately, blur it (sigma = shadowBlur / 2, three box blurs) and lay it down offset by shadowOffset, which is not transformed.
  copy, source-in, source-out, destination-in and destination-atop also clear outside the shape, as in the original. (the shape is painted separately and composited over the whole clipped region)
  Text is painted from coverage taken from the engine glyph cache (the same face selection, shaping, fallback fonts and color emoji as the Text component).
- Differences from the original:
  - Properties are setters and getters. Colors are CanvasStyle, which takes a Color or CSS color string, a gradient or a pattern.
  - roundRect radii are a list of numbers (f32) or elliptical corners ((x, y), CanvasRadius::Elliptical, the original DOMPointInit).
  - Desktop pixels use the same Skia math as Chrome but not the same version, so edge antialiasing and blur may differ slightly.

2D 물리 월드.\n- 초안: 0.4.0 뒤 기능, API 가 바뀔 수:
2D physics world.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change. Same API and same math as the original src/experimental/physics2d/physicsworld2d.js.
- Holds rigid bodies (static, kinematic, dynamic), shapes (circle, capsule, segment, convex polygon, chain) and joints (distance, revolute, weld, wheel), and runs steps.
  The features are based on Box2D 3 (Erin Catto) and Unity 2D physics (Rigidbody2D, Collider2D).
- The broad phase is a dynamic AABB tree (DynamicTree), the narrow phase is separating axes and edge clipping, and the solver is a soft step (substeps, warm starting, soft constraints, relaxation, restitution),
  grouping touching bodies into islands and putting a whole island to sleep when it stays still.
- Determinism: all math is f64 and the trigonometric functions are hand-written. Creating in the same order and calling the same step gives results identical to the bit with the same world in the original vanilla.js.
  (pair finding creates contacts in key order, hash tables are used only for lookup, and iteration is always in slot order)
- Differences from the original: queries (cast_ray, overlap_*) take &mut self because they apply teleports first. Bodies and shapes are changed with get_body_mut or `world[body_id]`.
  The fixed step accumulation of advance keeps the same math as the original FixedStepper in f64 inside the world. (the Rust FixedStepper is f32, so step times would differ from the original)
- Not there yet: continuous collision (TOI, which keeps fast bullets from tunneling through thin walls), one-sided chains, prismatic, motor and mouse joints, changing body types, multithreading.
2D 물리의 f64 벡터.\n- 초안: 0.4.0 뒤 기능, API 가:
f64 vector of 2D physics.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- The physics of the original vanilla.js computes in JavaScript numbers (f64) and exchanges the engine Vector2. The Rust engine's Vector2 is f32, so
  the physics API exchanges this f64 vector to make the physics results of the two engines match to the bit. (in place of the original's Vector2)
- It converts directly from Vector2 (f32) (From), and for drawing it is converted with to_vector2.
2D 물리의 결정론 수학.\n- 초안: 0.4.0 뒤 기능, API 가:
Deterministic math for 2D physics.
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change. Same math in the same order as the original src/experimental/physics2d/physicsmath2d.js, so the results of the two engines match to the bit.
- Builds cosine, sine and arctangent from only addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and square root. (all operations IEEE 754 requires to be correctly rounded)
  Rust's f64::sin calls the operating system's math library, so its last digits differ per platform and from the browser's Math.sin, and the physics diverges.
  Box2D wrote b2ComputeCosSin and b2Atan2 itself for the same reason. (box2d.org/posts/2024/08/determinism)

2D 뼈대 애니메이션의 곡선, 시간줄, 자세, 클립. (원본 experi:
Curves, timelines, poses and clips of 2D skeletal animation. (the original experimental/skeleton2d/skeleton2danimation.js)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- A curve is the interpolation from each key to the next. There are three: linear, stepped, and cubic Bezier ([x1, y1, x2, y2] like CSS cubic-bezier, end points (0, 0), (1, 1)).

2D 뼈대 애니메이터 컴포넌트. (원본 experimental/skele:
2D skeleton animator component. (the original experimental/skeleton2d/skeleton2danimator.js, attached to a node to run and draw a skeleton)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Holds a Skeleton2D (pose) and a Skeleton2DAnimationState (tracks), advances time and writes the pose in tick, and computes world matrices and IK and draws in draw.
  Since it computes in draw, bones the scene's tick moved after the component tick (like IK targets) also apply in that frame.
- Images are found by the frame names of attachments. set_atlas finds and stores the frames of all skins from an engine SpriteAtlas, and set_frame can add them one at a time.
- For each slot in draw order, triangles are written into the Graphic vertex slots (get_vertex_data, x, y, u, v) and drawn with draw_vertices. The slot color is multiplied into the image.
  Slots with images on the same page are drawn at once by the engine's batching. Graphic was not modified.
- The skeleton origin is the node's pivot position. (the node position if the content size is 0)
- It is separate from SpriteAnimator (frame animation). That one changes the Sprite image of the same node; this one draws by itself.
- With gizmos on (set_gizmo_visible), bones are drawn as lines.
- Differences from the original: data is received as `Rc<Skeleton2DData>`. Frames are held as copies of Frame. To advance time outside the component, call update instead of tick.
2D 뼈대 인스턴스. (원본 experimental/skeleton2d/:
2D skeleton instance. (the original experimental/skeleton2d/skeleton2d.js, the current pose, world matrices and attachment vertices of the bones, slots and IK built from one data)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Bone local values (translation, rotation, scale, shear) are written by clips or code. update_world_transform computes the world matrices from the parents down and applies IK.
- IK does not change local values, only the 'applied rotation' (get_applied_rotation). The next computation starts again from the local values, so nothing accumulates.
- One-bone IK rotates the bone so its x axis faces the target. Two-bone IK rotates the parent by the law of cosines to place the elbow and rotates the child to face the target.
  If out of reach, it straightens. It blends with the original rotation by the mix (mix). If the grandparent bone is flipped (negative determinant), the bend direction is flipped. (same as DragonBones)
- Differences from the original: bone, slot and IK instances hold copies of their data. The chosen skin is held by index. Applying IK is called by constraint index.
2D 뼈대 자료. (원본 experimental/skeleton2d/sk:
2D skeleton data. (the original experimental/skeleton2d/skeleton2ddata.js, setup data for bones, slots, IK, skins and attachments, clips, shared by many instances)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Coordinates have y growing downward like the engine. Rotation and shear are in degrees, and positive is clockwise on screen.
- Bone local matrix: x axis = (cos(rotation + shear x), sin(rotation + shear x)) x scale x, y axis = (-sin(rotation + shear y), cos(rotation + shear y)) x scale y.
  The world matrix is the parent world matrix x the local matrix. (translation, rotation, scale and shear are all inherited)
- Bones must be ordered with parents first. (the reader checks this)
- Two formats are read: the engine's own JSON (create_from_json) and DragonBones 5.x JSON (create_from_dragon_bones).
  The Spine format is not read, because the Spine Runtimes License requires a Spine Editor license for every user of a product that includes the runtime.
- Differences from the original: the parent index is `Option<usize>` (the original -1 is None), slot blending is BlendMode, attachments are the two-variant enum Skeleton2DAttachment,
  and clips are held as `Rc<Skeleton2DAnimation>` so track entries share them.

  ```text
    camera.set_view_size(view_size);                    // every frame or on resize
    camera.follow(&[hero_position], 6.0, time_delta);  // follow (optional)

    camera.begin(graphic); ...render world... camera.end(graphic);   // push_state + apply_transform / pop_state
  ```

- Column-major as in the original. Element positions are elements[column * 4 + row], uploaded as is to glUniformMatrix4fv without transposing.

  get_elements() gives a read reference, and write_to_array / write_to_slice copy into uniform arrays.

- Chrome rounds the ascent and descent from Skia (fAscent, fDescent) separately (FontMetrics::AscentDescentWithHacks), and the line height is lroundf(ascent) + lroundf(descent) + lroundf(line gap fLeading).
- The tables Skia reads differ by operating system.
  - Linux (SkFontHost_FreeType.cpp): the typo values if USE_TYPO_METRICS in OS/2 is set, otherwise FreeType's hhea values (typo if hhea is 0, the win values if that is also 0).
    ttf-parser's ascender, descender, line_gap read them in this order.
  - macOS (CoreText): the hhea values, ignoring USE_TYPO_METRICS. (confirmed in headless Chrome on macOS: a font with that bit set keeps the same line height)
  - Windows (DirectWrite's DWRITE_FONT_METRICS): the typo values if USE_TYPO_METRICS, otherwise the win values with a line gap equal to how much the hhea line height exceeds the win height.
    (DirectWrite does not disclose which table it picks, so the calculation known from font vertical metrics guides is used)
- Chrome on macOS adds 15% of (ascent + descent), rounded, to the ascent of Times, Helvetica and Courier. (a value matched to Safari's SimpleFontDataMac)

DragonBones 5.x JSON 으로 짓기.\n- 뼈(transfo:
Builds from DragonBones 5.x JSON.
- Reads bones (x, y, skX, skY, scX, scY of transform, length), slots (displayIndex, product of color, blendMode), skin image and mesh (weights from slotPose, bonePose),
  IK (bone, target, chain 0 or 1, bendPositive, weight), and clips (translateFrame, rotate and skew of rotateFrame, scaleFrame, displayFrame, colorFrame, zOrder, events).
- Rotation is skY, and shear y is skX - skY. Frame counts become seconds through frameRate. Rotation keys are unwrapped into continuous values following clockwise.
- No tweenEasing means stepped, 0 means linear, others become a Bezier of the same shape, and curve is read as a Bezier only when it is a single [x1, y1, x2, y2]. (multi-segment curves are linear)
- Not read: turning off bone inheritRotation and inheritScale, color offsets (aO and so on), armature, boundingBox, path attachments, ffd, IK timelines, sounds and actions.

FBX 로더. (원본 experimental/graphics/fbxloa:
FBX loader. (the original experimental/graphics/fbxloader.js)
- Binary FBX → GL independent intermediate representation (FbxSceneData). After low level node/property parsing, it interprets the object/connection graph
  and extracts the node hierarchy / skinned meshes / materials / embedded textures / skeletal animation. The result is consumed as GL resources by SkinnedModel.
- Like the original, it is a pure parser. It knows nothing of GL or shading and also runs on wasm32. Compressed arrays (deflate, zlib header) are decompressed with flate2 (pure Rust).
- Differences from the original:
  - The original is async. (because it decompresses compressed arrays with the browser's DecompressionStream) The Rust version finishes on the spot with flate2.
    The Promise of the original loadFromUrl(url) is a load handle (FbxLoadHandle) like ImageAsset. load_from_url(engine, asset path) asks for the bytes through the engine's asset loading
    (desktop reads from the asset folder candidates, the web fetches from asset_base_url), and once received, get_scene_data returns the parsed result.
    The handle can be awaited as is. (inside an engine task, FbxLoader::load_from_url(engine, path).await yields the parsed result like the original await FbxLoader.loadFromUrl(url))
  - 64 bit integers: the original holds single values like object ids as BigInt when they exceed 2^53. The Rust version uses i64. Arrays (key times) are Number in the original.
  - The original uses ordered Maps. The Rust version gives the same iteration order with FbxObjectMap, which keeps insertion order.
  - objectById, which the original builds but does not use, and getDataView / getFileBytes / getTextDecoder were not carried over.

- Font name, list file and folder, last group, weights and wait time are set with configure_ui_font. (initially GameUI, ./assets/fonts/fonts.json, latin, 500 and 700)
- The lists are fonts.json (index { fonts: [{ group, manifest }] }) and fonts-<group>.json (subsets { faces: [{ file, weight, style, unicodeRange }] }).
- Draws all on-screen languages under one font name. Font files are not merged; a font face is made for each subset and registered with that subset's character range.
  So only the subsets containing characters used on screen are fetched. (Korean, Chinese and Japanese fonts have hundreds of subsets)
  Characters shared by several fonts, such as Han characters, are drawn by the font registered later. The selected language's group is placed right before Latin (second from the end)
  so that Japanese gets Japanese-font Han characters and Traditional Chinese gets Traditional-font ones. Latin is always last, so digits and Latin letters use the Latin font in every language.
- Every subset is registered with only the two weights in configure_ui_font's weights (initially 500, 700). Variable-weight subsets are registered twice (500 and 700), and 400-only subsets as 500.
- Subsets for the text in use are fetched in advance. (load_ui_font_text) When a subset arrives, the engine (EngineConfiguration.rebake_text_on_font_load) discards and rebakes only the text baked with that subset's characters.
  Characters not fetched in advance also get their subset fetched by update when measured or drawn with that font. (in the original, the browser fetches a registered FontFace when drawing characters in its range)
  Before it arrives, it is drawn with another font like the original canvas, and once it arrives it is rebaked (when rebake_text_on_font_load is on).
- At first only the lists for the selected language and Latin are fetched, and the remaining groups are fetched a little after play starts (remaining_delay_milliseconds).
  Initial subsets are waited for only up to wait_milliseconds. (is_ui_font_ready is true once that time passes or everything arrives)

UI 노드. (원본 ui/uinode.js 의 UINode)\n- 영역을:
UI node. (UINode of the original ui/uinode.js)
- Represents its area with 8 solver variables (left, right, top, bottom, width, height, derived center_x, center_y), and the user adds constraints to a LayoutSolver
  to determine those values. It registers the 4 intrinsic constraints (right == left + width, bottom == top + height, center_x == left + width / 2, center_y == top + height / 2) itself.
- User constraints are registered with add_constraint. The solver is attached with set_solver. (UISceneBase attaches the scene's solver to the UINodes in the tree by itself)
- intrinsic content size, content hugging, compression resistance, layout margins, layout margins guide are the same concepts as UIKit's APIs of the same names.
- Solver variables (left, top) are absolute positions in the coordinate system where the UI tree root is placed. If the parent is also a UINode, the child is placed offset by (left - parent left, top - parent top).
  Rotation, scale and opacity use the node's own as is.
- Usage:
  ```text
    let node_id = node_tree.create_child(parent_id, "title");
    node_tree.add_component(node_id, UINode::new());
    node_tree.with_component_mut::<UINode, _>(node_id, |ui_node, _tree| {
        ui_node.add_constraint(&ui_node.left_anchor().equal_to(screen_node.left_anchor().add(16))).unwrap();
    });
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - In the original it is a separate node inheriting TransformNode and moves to the solver values in pushTransform. In the Rust version the only node is WorldNode, so
    it is a component attached to WorldNode, and moves the solver values to the node's position (local_position, with pivot and anchor at the top left) and content_size.
    The moves happen in the component tick and in apply_layout_in_tree (called by UISceneBase right after solving). The original reads them on every draw.
  - The original getIntrinsicContentSize gathers the values of the node's components that have that function (Text, RichText). The Rust version gathers Component::get_intrinsic_content_size.
    The original UILabel calls the node's invalidateIntrinsicContentSize when the text changes. Components in the Rust version cannot call the node's other components, so
    UINode reads the components' values again every tick (and on UISceneBase's solver attaching) and invalidates by itself if they changed.
  - Where the original throws exceptions (duplicate constraints in the solver, unsatisfiable required constraints), it returns `Result<(), LayoutError>`.
    (add_constraint, remove_constraint, set_solver, set_layout_margins, invalidate_intrinsic_content_size)
  - Anchors are functions (left_anchor) instead of the original's getter properties (leftAnchor). The axis argument is the LayoutConstraintAxis enum instead of a string, so there is no "unsupported axis" exception.
  - The layout margins guide is a UINode not in the tree, as in the original. In the Rust version this UINode holds it in a Box.

UI 라벨. (원본 ui/uilabel.js 의 UILabel)\n- 표:
UI label. (UILabel of the original ui/uilabel.js)
- A display-only widget. Draws text aligned within the host's content_size area. Setters pass through to the text component as in the original.
- The original attaches Text and RichText to the host with require() and holds their references. The Rust version embeds one RichText, and RichText embeds Text.
  (the same form as Sprite embedding Paint) This is so a label.set_text call from scene code outside tick takes effect immediately.
  A sibling Text would be reachable only inside tick and lag one frame. So `get_component::<Text>()` on a label node is None.
  The embedded Text is taken out with get_text_component / get_text_component_mut, and RichText with get_rich_text_component / get_rich_text_component_mut.
- The original applies setters to both Text and RichText and picks which one to turn on with use_rich_text. The Rust version has a single set, so there is nothing to keep in sync.
  With use_rich_text(true) it draws with RichText (parsing markup), otherwise with the embedded Text. append_segment / clear_segments pass through to RichText.
- The original setFont(FontFace) was changed to set_font_family (a registered font name).
- Text direction (set_text_direction) and the visible character count (set_visible_character_count) pass through to the text component as in the original.
- Not ported from the original: invalidateIntrinsicContentSize (UINode path only).
- The background color (UIView) is drawn before the text. (in the original too, UILabel is attached ahead of the Text and RichText it requires, so the background is drawn first)

UI 문서. (vanilla.js ui/uidocument.js 의 UI:
UI document. (UIDocument of vanilla.js ui/uidocument.js)
- Exports and reads a node tree as a JSON document (.scene.json). The vanilla.js visual editor (tools/visualeditor) saves scenes in this form, and
  games read the same file and build nodes and components in a NodeTree. Trees built in Rust are exported in the same form too.
- A document is { "version": 1, "root": node }, and a node has type, name, active, position, scale, rotation, opacity, pivot, anchor,
  contentSize, interactable, components, children. If there is a widget (a component that creates a content node), only the children inside content are kept separately as contentChildren.
  Unknown keys added by the editor, like frameSize, are ignored. Key order and indentation (tabs) are written the same as the original JSON.stringify. (serde_json preserve_order)
- Differences from the original:
  - The original is a static class and module global tables. The Rust version creates and uses a UIDocument value that holds the tables. (no global state, like the engine) new registers the engine components.
  - As in the original, types without write and read functions (propertyHandler of the original COMPONENT_PROPERTY_TABLE) are written and read through reflection. (saveByReflection, loadByReflection)
    The original scans an object's get, is, set functions at run time, while the Rust version uses the list built at compile time by the `#[reflect]` macro. (core/reflection.rs)
    The only types handled through reflection are components with `#[reflect]` attached. (attached to every engine component) In the original, every object is reflected.
    Outline, SoftShade, ShadowText, UIProgressRing, which the original table saves through reflection, are also written and read through reflection. Same keys as the original reflection result (capitalized: Color, LineWidth,
    GizmoVisible, Enable, ComponentType, etc.) and order. FontFace of the original ShadowText is a font object, so it is not written. The Rust version's font name text (get_font_family)
    is kept in the property list but left out of saving with `#[reflect(unsaved)]`.
  - Reflection setters that take the tree (like SnapCurrentIndex of UISnapScrollView) are also called on the spot while reading, as in the original. The component being read is briefly taken out of the tree and the read context is handed the tree.
  - For components with &mut self getters, to_json_text_mut, serialize_node_mut read and write them through the &mut branch. (original getters have no &self, &mut self distinction)
  - Type registration: register_component_type(name, builder function) is the original registerComponentType. (written and read through reflection) Types with their own write and read functions
    are registered with register_component_type_with_handler, and widgets (components that create a content node) with register_widget_type, register_widget_type_with_handler.
  - Unregistered types are skipped with a warning when reading, as in the original. When writing, they are written through reflection as in the original, and type is the type name. (original constructor.name)
    Components without reflection (game components without `#[reflect]`) cannot be written, so they are left out with a warning.
  - Even for types with write and read functions, reflection properties that point to nodes are added and read separately as { "$nodeRef": path }, as in the original. (saveNodeReferences, loadNodeReferences)
  - ShadowImage is also added at the end of the original table in the same form (the reflection save form after imagePath), so both engines are the same.
  - The original UIImageView attaches a Sprite to the host on attach, so the document has a Sprite after UIImageView. The Rust version embeds the Sprite, so it writes the embedded Sprite there as a Sprite and
    when reading, reads the following Sprite into the embedded Sprite. (set_component_companions, in the original, reading again attaches a duplicate Sprite)
  - Original node types (WorldNode subclasses, registerNodeType) are components attached to nodes in the Rust version. Registered with register_node_type, they are written and read in the same form as the original document:
    the type of a node with that component attached is that name, and it is not listed in the component list.
    - Types that actually build children and components on attach like the original node constructor (UIWindow, UIConfirmWindow, UIDialog, UIDropdown, UIToast, UISpinner, UIContextMenu, etc.)
      have what they built written as is.
    - For self-drawing types (UIInputField, UIScrollBar), UIDocumentNode writes the original constructor's share in the original form, and reads that share back as settings.
    - The original turns the node off when hiding, but for types that only hide because tick must keep running in the Rust version (UIToast), UIDocumentNode converts active to the original meaning when writing and reading.
  - When reading, components and children already on the node (built when a node type or widget was attached, or attached together through require) are matched from the front of the document by order and type (name for children), and if they match,
    the document values are put into them without rebuilding. In the original, reading again duplicates what the constructor made and what is in the document. The Rust version does not duplicate, and writing again gives the same document.
  - The original editor (tools/uieditor) registers every Component and WorldNode subclass the engine exports and writes them to documents. Like the original runtime, they are not in the default table, and
    a game registers the same types (35 components, 12 node types) with a single line, register_editor_types. (one line per type also works)
  - Nodes in the Rust version are just WorldNode. The type of a node without a component registered as a node type is always written as "WorldNode", and unregistered types are read as WorldNode.
  - The original getComponentType (name → constructor) cannot return a constructor as a value (the node tree attaches by concrete type), so create_component(tree, node, name)
    builds the component of that name, attaches it to the node, and returns the component order index. (in place of taking a constructor and calling addComponent in the original)
  - The image path (imagePath) is resolved with the image resolver (set_image_resolver) as in the original. Without a resolver, it is looked up in the asset store the document holds.
    load_images requests the document's imagePath values as ImageAsset (the scene can hand over the received load handles with track_load_handle),
    and images not loaded yet are attached by bind_pending_images once fully loaded. (Rust assets finish loading some time after the request)
  - The base root of node references ($nodeRef) is the root of to_json_text, from_json_text. When serialize_node, deserialize_node are called directly, that node is the root.
    (in the original, calling only serializeNode does not write references, and calling only deserializeNode does not connect them)
  - Numbers are written as the shortest decimal of f32. (0.22 as 0.22, integers without a decimal point) Trailing digits of the original f64 (like 0.1 + 0.2) are reduced to f32.
- Sprite nineSlice is read by reversing the form the original writes ([left, top, left + right, top + bottom], Rect's left, top, right, bottom), as in the original.

UI scale. (vanilla.js ui/uiscale.js, UIScale)
- The fixed side of the view (height for portrait, width for landscape) always has the same length, so on a small screen (a portal's PC iframe, etc.)
  one view unit becomes much smaller than 1 CSS pixel on screen and text becomes unreadable. In that case it computes a scale that enlarges only the UI layer on screen. (the game's graphics stay as they are)
- If one unit is smaller than minimum_css_scale CSS pixels, it enlarges by that much. (1 ~ maximum_scale)
  - On a short screen, it does not enlarge so far that the enlarged UI layer's height falls below minimum_layer_height. (0 means not checked)
  - On a portrait screen (width at most portrait_ratio times the height), it enlarges without an upper limit so that one unit becomes minimum_css_scale CSS pixels.
- Differences from the original:
  - There is no global engine, so it takes the CSS pixels of one unit (ViewManager::get_css_pixel_scale) as an argument. (the original reads it from the engine if options.cssPixelScale is absent)
  - The options object is the UIScaleOptions struct.
- Usage: let ui_scale = UIScale::read(view_width, view_height, view_manager.get_css_pixel_scale(), &UIScaleOptions::default());

UI widgets. (the WorldNode line of the original src/ui)
- As in the original, most widgets are components, not nodes. Attached to a node, they use their own node (the host) as the widget.
- Widgets that create child nodes (content, scroll bars) or companion components (Mask) are attached with node_tree.add_component(node_id, ...).
  If attached with WorldNode::add_component, attach_to_tree is not called, so there is no content node and touch is not enabled.
- The original UIScrollBar is a node inheriting WorldNode. The Rust version is a UIScrollBar component attached to a single node.
- UIInputField receives key, IME and hidden web DOM input events from the engine text input queue (core/textinput.rs).
- Widgets that inherit WorldNode in the original (UIDropdown, UIDialog, UIToast, UISpinner, UIContextMenu) are also components attached to a host node.
  When attached, they set up the host and create child nodes like the original constructors. Each widget's create(node_tree, parent_id, options) takes the place of new + add_child.
- The UINode, auto layout (autolayout) and UIScene lines were also ported. (UIDocument was ported with a type name table instead of reflection)

가상 패드.\n- 원본 misc/virtualpad.js 를 옮긴 것이다:
Virtual pad.
- A port of the original misc/virtualpad.js. Computes and draws the movement of an on-screen joystick's pad (outer circle) and knob (inner circle).
- Unlike the original, it is a plain value, not a component. The owner calls touch_press / touch_move / touch_release and tick, draw.
- While the knob moves, the knob move event reports the direction (a unit vector mapped to 0 ~ 1, 0 ~ 1) and the pull strength (0 ~ 1).
  On release, the knob returns to the pad center at 1600 pixels per second while reporting, and once back reports (0.5, 0.5), 0 once.
- Differences from the original:
  The state name move is a Rust keyword, so it is moved. The original state value strings ("wait", "pressed", "move", "released") are obtained with get_name.
  The event callback is FnMut(Vector2, f32).

강체 컴포넌트. (노드를 2D 물리 몸에 잇는다)\n- 초안: 0.4.0:
Rigid body component. (connects a node to a 2D physics body)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change. Same API as the original src/experimental/physics2d/rigidbody2d.js.
- Once it takes charge of one body of the world with set_body(world, body_id), every tick it puts the body's position and angle into the node's local position and rotation (degrees). (like Unity Rigidbody2D moving the Transform)
  The body moves the node; the node does not move the body. To move the node, call the body's set_transform.
- World coordinates are assumed to equal the coordinates of the node's parent. Put physics nodes under a parent that represents one world space.
- With interpolation on (default), it blends between the previous and current step using the world's last advance fraction.
- Differences from the original: the world is received as `Rc<RefCell<PhysicsWorld2D>>` so the scene and the component can share it.
  The original setBody puts the attached node at the body position right away; Rust does it when attached to the node (attach) and in tick.

개발자 도구. (원본 misc/devtools.js 의 DEVTools):
Developer tools. (DEVTools of the original misc/devtools.js)
- F2 shows and hides it. The panel appears docked at the bottom right in the window's inner logical coordinates (canvas native), regardless of the view scale mode.
- Four tabs: Statistics (engine, screen, time info), Node Hierarchy (tree on the left + inspector on the right), Local Storage (view, add, edit, delete keys and values),
  Settings (dim background, all gizmos, aspect ratio guide, FPS display. Saved to local storage "hierarchy.settings" as the same JSON as the original)
- Drag the title bar to move it, drag the edges and corners to resize, and drag the center divider to change the left and right ratio.
- Tree: expand and collapse, active (A) and gizmo (G) columns, selection, drag scrolling. Inspector: click a component header to expand and collapse its properties. (expanded by default)
- In the Rust version the scene holds DevTools and calls it per function:
    dev_tools.tick(engine, node_tree, unscaled_time_delta) in tick, dev_tools.draw(engine, node_tree, graphic) in post_draw.
    If is_visible() && is_pointer_inside_panel(engine), the scene does not pass that input to the nodes. (original GameScene.isDevToolsCapturingInput)
- Differences from the original:
  - There is no global engine, so there is no original setEngine. tick, draw, is_pointer_inside_panel take the engine.
  - Nodes are referred to by NodeId. The root list is set_root_nodes(`Vec<NodeId>`), expanded nodes are a NodeId set, and collapsed components are a (NodeId, component order) set.
    Deleted nodes drop out of the tree and the inspector, and if the selected node is deleted, the selection returns to none.
  - Graphic is held by EngineRunner, not the engine, so it cannot be touched in tick. setForceGizmosVisible, which the original calls in tick and on press,
    only records the desired value and applies it to Graphic at the start of the next draw. (the false applied by the original setEngine is also applied on the first draw)
  - WorldNode is the only node type, so the tree's Type column and the inspector's type are always "WorldNode".
  - The inspector's component properties call and show every get*, is* getter of that component, like the original getComponentProperties.
    The original scans the prototype at run time, while the Rust version uses the list built at compile time by the `#[reflect]` macro. (core/reflection.rs, attached to every engine component)
    Getters that take the tree (which in the original grab a neighbor component directly) are called with the tree passed in during drawing, and for components with &mut self getters, tick reads the values while holding the tree and shows them.
    Names follow the original formatMethodName (getTextColor → textColor, kept as is if starting with is), and values follow the original formatPropertyValue format.

- exponential: 0 if the reference is 0, otherwise clamps the distance to at least the reference and gives (distance / reference) ^ -max(rolloff, 0).

Common base scene for games.

게임 공통 베이스 씬. (원본 game/gamescene.js 의 Gam:
Common base scene for games. (GameScene in the original game/gamescene.js)
- Loading screen (center image + gauge at the bottom + touch to skip, minimum display time).
- Touch input goes through TouchRecognizer. (gestures that scroll even when dragging a button inside a scroll view)
- Safe area node "safeArea" + safe area rectangle computation.
- When the view size changes, layout is called again at the next tick.
- Fills the whole canvas with the background color. (pre_draw)
- In the Rust version, instead of inheritance the scene contains a GameSceneBase, implements the GameScene trait (where the original overrides), and gets a Scene with one game_scene! line:
  ```text
    struct TitleScene { game_scene_base: GameSceneBase, logo_asset: ImageAsset }
    impl GameScene for TitleScene {
        fn get_game_scene_base(&self) -> &GameSceneBase { &self.game_scene_base }
        fn get_game_scene_base_mut(&mut self) -> &mut GameSceneBase { &mut self.game_scene_base }
        fn load_assets(&mut self, engine: &mut Engine) {                       // where the original overrides loadAssets (after the base requests the loading image)
            self.logo_asset.load(engine, "logo.png");
            self.game_scene_base.get_scene_base_mut().track_asset(&self.logo_asset);
        }
        fn initialize(&mut self, engine: &mut Engine) {                          // after the base initialize
            let safe_area_id = self.game_scene_base.get_safe_area_node_id().unwrap();   // attach content under here
        }
        fn layout(&mut self, engine: &mut Engine) { /* read game_scene_base.get_safe_area_rect() and place content */ }
    }
    vanilla::game_scene!(TitleScene);
  ```
  For each Scene function, the base is called first and then the GameScene function of the same name. (an override that calls super first in the original)
  Only post_draw calls the scene's first and draws the base (fade curtain, developer tools) on top. layout is called after the base recomputes the safe area.
  (on resize, and when tick sees a view size change. Also once on the first tick)
  Calling GameSceneBase functions directly from Scene functions still works. In that case the scene looks at the bool returned by tick and calls its own layout, and also calls post_draw directly.
- Differences from the original:
  - The original load (async) "waits for load_assets, then waits for the minimum time / a touch", which has been moved to the Rust asset flow.
    In create it hands over one "loading gate" read handle, and draw_on_load opens the gate when the minimum time has passed or the screen is pressed.
    The engine calls initialize only after all handed over assets (including the gate) finish, so the result is the same as the original. (all assets read + (minimum time or touch))
  - Time is measured with the real elapsed time since engine start (get_realtime_since_startup) instead of the original Date.now().
  - Screen presses are checked with the input manager's is_touch_pressed instead of the original window pointerdown.
  - The original makes TouchRecognizer in initialize. The Rust version makes it at creation. Touches are passed by tick instead of through functions like the original touchPress.
    (SceneBase's touch raycaster and first touch callback are not used)
  - Safe area: the web reads CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) as in the original. Desktop is 0 like Chrome desktop,
    and it can be set with set_safe_area_insets. (once set, that value is used on the web too)
  - set_view_scale_mode also takes the engine. (there is no global engine) Given the engine, it recomputes the view area right away as in the original.
  - Developer tools (DevTools) are made in initialize if EngineConfiguration::use_dev_tools is on. (same as the original) tick passes F2 and touches, and post_draw draws them.
- Changing the loading screen: set_loading_colors changes only the colors, set_loading_drawer changes the whole drawing on top of the background. (the original setLoadingColors, setLoadingDrawer)
  The set function is kept in an `Rc<RefCell>`. get_loading_drawer returns that Rc, and the caller borrows it with borrow_mut to call it.
  By default the gauge shows the elapsed minimum display time (get_loading_progress), and if progress is reported with set_loading_progress or track_asset_loader,
  it smoothly follows that progress. (LoadingProgress, get_loading_progress_state)
  - The original getLoadingProgress (returns LoadingProgress) is get_loading_progress_state, because the Rust version already has the same name (elapsed time ratio).
  - The original fills the progress to 1 when load_assets finishes (if it was ever reported). The Rust version fills it to 1 in draw_on_load when all assets handed to the scene except the loading gate finish.
    (complete_loading_progress_if_assets_finished, a scene that works across frames hands over a read handle and opens it when done)
  - For an AssetLoader handed over with track_asset_loader, draw_on_load calls update every frame.
  - The fourth value (outside color) of the original setLoadingColors is set separately with set_loading_outside_color, because Rust has no default arguments.
- Screen frame (the same features as fadeScreen, isUserInterfaceAt, setPlayInputHandler and setPlayAreaReference of vanilla.js GameScene):
  - Screen fade: in the original, if onDark returns a Promise, it stays dark until it finishes. The same form in the Rust version is fade_screen_async(on_dark).
    At the tick it becomes fully dark, it hands on_dark's future over as a scene task and runs it right there up to the first await as in the original (reaching the scene and engine through SceneContext),
    and when the future finishes it brightens. A scene implementing GameScene calls it with GameScene::fade_screen_async, and game_scene! takes care of starting it.
    A scene implementing Scene directly calls it with `GameSceneBase::fade_screen_async::<scene type>`, and after the base tick takes it out with take_screen_fade_dark_starter and starts it.
    (if not taken out, the base hands it over at the next polling turn in post_draw or the next tick)
    The synchronous form fade_screen(on_dark) calls on_dark(tree, engine) when fully dark, and if on_dark returns a ScreenFadeHold, it stays dark until that handle's release is called.
    (brightens right away if None) The callback form fade_screen_with_hold(on_dark) has on_dark keep the handle and release it when the work is done. (in place of the Promise's resolve)
    The curtain is drawn by post_draw. While the curtain is up, presses and the wheel are not accepted.
  - Input the UI did not take: calls the handler (set_play_input_handler) as in the original. press, move, release and wheel of the original handler object are variants of PlayInput.
    The handler cannot borrow the scene, so scene state is shared through `Rc<RefCell>`. For the scene to take them directly in tick, collect them with set_play_input_enabled(true) and take them with take_play_inputs.
    (coordinates relative to the top left of the safe area)
  - Wheel: as in the original, if it points inside the window layer (UIWindowLayer), the topmost window takes it first (UIWindowLayer::scroll_window_at), otherwise the scroll box at that position takes it.
  - If the safe area is not set with set_safe_area_insets, it reads ViewManager::get_safe_area_insets. (follows the forced value, URL, env and sides to ignore)

게임 영역 기준 설정. (세이프 에어리어를 뺀 게임 영역의 고정 쪽 길이:
Sets the play area reference. (stretches the reference resolution so the fixed side length of the play area without the safe area is always fixed_length)
- Canvas length : length without the safe area = reference resolution length : fixed_length.
- If is_landscape, the width is the fixed side, otherwise the height. The view scale mode is set to match. (width fixed StretchWidthExpandHeight, height fixed StretchHeightExpandWidth)
- Safe area sides to ignore are passed with ViewManager::set_ignored_safe_area_sides. A fixed_length of 0 turns it off.
- Given the engine, it applies right away. The scene calls apply_play_area_reference at the start of resize.
게임 영역 기준을 기준 해상도에 걸기. (캔버스와 인셋 크기에서만 셈해: Applies the play area reference to the reference resolution. (computed only from the canvas and inset sizes, so calling it any number of times gives the same result. If changed, recomputes the view area and returns true)
게임 영역 기준의 기준 해상도 길이 셈. (정적, 인셋은 뷰 좌표, in:
Computes the reference resolution length for the play area reference. (static, insets in view coordinates, inset_scale is the view coordinates → canvas units scale, 0 if it cannot be computed)
- It is fixed_length × canvas length / (canvas length - inset sum × inset_scale).

Gamepad manager.
- InputManager holds one and polls it in tick. Scenes read it with engine.get_input_manager().get_gamepad_manager().
게임패드 관리자.\n- 원본 core/gamepadmanager.js 를:
Gamepad manager.
- A port of the original core/gamepadmanager.js. The public names (GamepadButtonCode, GamepadAnalogStickCode, GamepadTriggerCode,
  connect, disconnect, set_callback, update_all_gamepads, is_button_pressed, get_button_value, get_axis_value,
  get_all_connected_gamepads, get_connected_gamepad_count, get_connected_gamepad) and the update rules are the same as the original.
  (values are rounded to two decimal places, axes are taken only when they change by more than 0.01, analog values are reported only when greater than 0, log messages)
- The original reads navigator.getGamepads(). The web (wasm32) reads navigator.getGamepads() directly like the original and takes all buttons and axes the browser gives,
  and takes connection and disconnection through gamepadconnected / gamepaddisconnected like the original engine.js.
  On desktop, gilrs reads OS input (Windows.Gaming.Input on Windows), converts it to a Gamepad list in the same W3C Standard Gamepad form as the original
  (buttons 0~16, axes 0~3, axis Y is positive downward), then runs the same rules.
- Differences from the original:
  - The gilrs default filters (deadzone, jitter filtering) are turned off. Raw values are taken like a browser, and the game applies the deadzone like the original.
  - An analog button (trigger) counts as pressed when its value exceeds 30/255, as in Chromium. (gilrs default presses at 0.75 and releases at 0.65)
  - A D-pad coming in as an axis (hat switch) is converted to buttons 12~15. (what the browser does)
  - On desktop, buttons that gilrs could not map to standard buttons (buttons missing from the mapping, gilrs C, Z) are appended after the 17 standard buttons, and axes missing from the mapping
    after the 4 standard axes, in the order they first move. gilrs does not give the device's button list and reports only buttons that have moved at least once, so such a button appears only after it is first pressed.
    When the number of buttons or axes grows, that pad's state slots grow too.
  - PlayStation pads (Sony 054c DualShock 4 05c4, 09cc, 0ba0 and DualSense 0ce6, 0df2, 0e5f) have 18 buttons like Chrome (MapperDualshock4, MapperDualSense in device/gamepad),
    and raw button 13 (HID button 14) is TOUCHPAD (17). It is always there even before being pressed, and other buttons (the DualSense mic button) and axes are not appended.
    gilrs only maps touchpad:b13 of the SDL mapping to an unnamed button (Button::Unknown, the same name as misc1), so the raw code of that button is found per platform.
    (usage 14 on the macOS IOKit button page, button 13 on Windows Windows.Gaming.Input, BTN_GAMEPAD + 13 on Linux hid-generic)
    The Linux hid-sony (from kernel 4.10) and hid-playstation (from 5.12) drivers expose the touchpad as a separate device and add 0x8000 to bcdHID.
    In that case it has 17 buttons like Chrome (MapperPs4Ps5). (the 13th and 14th bytes of the gilrs uuid are that version number)
    macOS GameController also has GCDualSenseGamepad.touchpadButton, but GameController does not give the pad's vendor and product numbers so it cannot be paired with a gilrs pad, and it is not used.
  - Gamepad.index on desktop is the gilrs GamepadId number. (from 0 in the order first connected, used like the browser index) On the web it is the browser index.
  - Gamepad.id on the web is the browser id as is, and on desktop it is built in Chrome form "name (STANDARD GAMEPAD Vendor: 054c Product: 0ce6)".
  - get_all_connected_gamepads / get_connected_gamepad return the copy read at the last update (tick). (the original reads anew on every call)
  - The button value of the callback is 1.0 (pressed) / 0.0 (released) instead of bool.
  - gilrs (the connection listeners on the web) is created on the first update. (engines and tests that never update do not open devices)
  - Added: set_log_enabled (turns logs on and off),
    update_all_gamepads_with_list (a way to feed a list without gilrs. For tests or other input sources)
  - Battery info is not in the original, so it is not ported.
  - The log printed whenever buttons and axes change is turned on with set_input_log_enabled like the original, and is off by default. set_log_enabled is the master switch for all logs including connection and disconnection.
  - GamepadKind, read_gamepad_kind: tells the kind (Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo, other) from the pad name. get_active_gamepad_id is the pad that pressed a button or tilted an axis far at the last update.
  - vibrate(strong_magnitude, weak_magnitude, seconds): vibrates all connected pads.
    On desktop it vibrates with gilrs force feedback (Linux evdev, Windows XInput and Windows.Gaming.Input), and on macOS, where gilrs does not support rumble,
    the platform layer (platform/desktop/gamepadhaptics.rs) vibrates the controller paired with the gilrs pad using GameController and CoreHaptics. (on macOS, a duration or strength of 0 stops the previous vibration)
    So gilrs is created with rumble enabled. (one gilrs rumble thread runs on desktop) On the web, like the original, it applies dual-rumble to the vibrationActuator of navigator.getGamepads().
    If called before the first update (tick), gilrs does not exist yet so nothing vibrates on desktop.

공간 소리. (원본 src/experimental/spatialaudio:
Spatial audio. (the original src/experimental/spatialaudio/)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- 3D sound exactly like WebAudio PannerNode and AudioListener. The web uses the browser PannerNode as is,
  and the desktop inserts a PannerNode porting the math of Chrome's PannerHandler into the engine mixer. (matches Chrome 158 OfflineAudioContext sample for sample)
- SpatialAudioPlayer: a player with a PannerNode inserted after the GainNode of AudioPlayer. Can output to an AudioBus (such as the SoundSystem effect bus).
  Panning model (equal power, HRTF), distance model (linear, inverse, exponential), reference and maximum distance, rolloff, cone (inner and outer angles and outer gain), position and orientation.
- SpatialAudioListener: the one listener of the context. (position, forward, up)
- AudioSource2D, AudioListener2D: components that follow the global position of a 2D node. They convert screen coordinates (+Y down) to WebAudio coordinates (+Y up).
- The math functions (calculate_distance_gain, calculate_cone_gain, calculate_azimuth_elevation, calculate_equal_power_gains, calculate_distance_cone_gain)
  use the same math as Chrome, so they are used to estimate volume before it is heard (culling sounds too far to hear) or in tests.
- There is no Doppler. WebAudio removed it from the specification. (web-platform-tests webaudio/historical.html expects AudioListener's dopplerFactor, speedOfSound, setVelocity and
  PannerNode's setVelocity to be absent) If needed, the game imitates it with the playback rate.
- HRTF: the browser on the web, and the engine mixer on the desktop, produce it with the same math as Chrome's HRTFPanner and the IRCAM data Chrome ships (Composite.flac).
  On the desktop, the data for that sample rate is built on a separate thread the first time it is chosen, and until it is built the sound passes through without panning, like a Chrome realtime context.
  The origin of the data and the IRCAM notice are in src/platform/audio/hrtf/resources/README.md of the engine repository.

Graphics quality governor. (GraphicsQualityGovernor of vanilla.js misc/graphicsqualitygovernor.js)
- Decides whether to use the light path from the setting and frame measurement, and picks the render pixel ratio limit.
- Order for deciding the light path (is_lite): override (like ?light in the address) → setting low (always light), high (never) → auto.
  In auto, it is light if light from the start (set_auto_lite_default, like touch devices) or when FrameProbe measured a slow device.
- Calling update(frame seconds, maximum frame rate) every frame measures with FrameProbe only in auto. Returns true on the frame the light path changes.
- Render pixel ratio limit: given with set_render_pixel_ratio_limits(normal, light), and apply_render_pixel_ratio(view_manager) applies it only when it changes. (0 means no limit)
- What to reduce on the light path (shadows, outlines, effects, draw counts) is decided by the game reading is_lite.
- Address: apply_search_text takes query text ("?light", "?a=1&light=0"). Reads it like the original URLSearchParams.
  (drops one leading ?, splits by & skipping empty pieces, splits name and value at the first =, decodes + as a space and %XX as bytes read as UTF-8. If a name appears more than once, the first value)
  apply_page_query reads the page address query on the web. Desktop has no page address, so it does nothing. (browser only)

Graphics quality decision. (GraphicsQualityGovernor of vanilla.js misc/graphicsqualitygovernor.js)
- Decides whether to use the lite path from settings and frame measurement, and picks the render pixel ratio limit.
- Order of deciding the lite path (is_lite): override (like ?light in the address) → setting low (always lite), high (never) → auto.
  In auto, it is the lite path if lite from the start (set_auto_lite_default, such as touch devices) or when FrameProbe measured a slow device.
- Calling update(frame seconds, max frames) every frame measures with FrameProbe only in auto. Returns true on the frame the lite path changed.
- Render pixel ratio limit: give it with set_render_pixel_ratio_limits(normal, lite path), and apply_render_pixel_ratio(view_manager) applies it only when it changes. (0 means no limit)
- What to reduce on the lite path (shadows, outlines, effects, draw counts) is decided by the game reading is_lite.
- Address: apply_search_text takes query text ("?light", "?a=1&light=0"). Reads it like the original URLSearchParams.
  (strips one leading ?, splits by &, skips empty pieces, splits the name and value at the first =, + is a space, %XX is decoded as bytes and read as UTF-8. If the same name appears several times, the first value)
  apply_page_query reads the query of the page address on the web. Desktop has no page address, so it reads the environment variable `VANILLA_<name>` (upper snake case, light → `VANILLA_LIGHT`).
그래픽.\n- GL 컨텍스트로 출력하는 렌더러. 원본(WebGL2)과 같:
Graphics.
- A renderer that draws to a GL context. Uses the same shaders and the same state model as the original (WebGL2).
- Reproduces the coordinate system (top-left origin, pixel units) and state model (transform/alpha stack) of the Canvas2D days as is.
- All draws converge on one point, draw_vertices(). Solid shapes also use a 1x1 white texture to unify with the texture path.
- Clipping is based on the stencil buffer. Text is baked into string textures and drawn.
- Batching (on by default): consecutive draws with the same texture have their vertices transformed on the CPU, gathered, and drawn at once.
  With the same batch shader as the original, color and tint go with each vertex, so tinted draws are batched too. Clip region recording is not batched.
  Blends, clips, particle draws and the end of the frame flush what has been gathered first (flush_batch). The original also turns it on by default. (setSpriteBatchingEnabled)
- Offscreen culling (on by default): NodeTree asks is_local_rect_visible before drawing a node. The original also turns it on by default and WorldNode asks with the same function. (setCullingEnabled)
- Shader override (set_shader_program_override): effects such as ShaderSprite draw with their own program instead of the default one. No batching while overridden.
  resolve_shader_program keeps the override programs by name and fixes their attribute locations to match the default program so they share the default vertex array.
- Remembers the last bound shader program and the texture of texture unit 0, and skips GL calls that bind the same thing again. (same as the original)
  When GL can be touched from outside (when handing out the context with get_gl, restore_render_state, frame start and end), it forgets them and binds again next time.
- The mipmap level bias (set_image_mipmap_bias) is applied through the textureLodBias uniform of the default, batch and particle shaders. An override shader receives it if it has that uniform. (same as the original)
- Text direction (set_text_direction, the original setTextDirection) is held in the state, and baked strings are shaped in that paragraph direction. (bidirectional ordering and shaping in textshaping.rs)
- 26 blend modes (same as the original): 13 use fixed blending, and 13 grab what is under the draw area from the current framebuffer with blit_framebuffer and mix it in a shader following the W3C formulas.
  Multiply uses fixed blending on the default framebuffer and shader mixing when drawing to a render target. (fixed blending differs from the W3C formula when the backdrop is translucent, same as the original)
  The shader text does not differ from the original by a single character. Override shaders are drawn first into an overlay slot (always RGBA16F on desktop, RGBA16F on the web when EXT_color_buffer_float is available like the original) and then mixed over.
- Alpha is not written when drawing to the default framebuffer (apply_color_mask). In the original and on the web the canvas is alpha: false so screen alpha is always 1, but the desktop default framebuffer has alpha,
  so modes using DST_ALPHA and shader mixing after a mode that lowers alpha differed from the web. Alpha is written to render targets.

그리드 길찾기. (A*)\n- 원본 misc/pathfinder.js 를:
Grid pathfinding. (A*)
- A port of the original misc/pathfinder.js. 4-directional movement, Manhattan distance heuristic, and a binary min heap managing the open list.
- A cell is blocked if is_blocked_handler(column, row) is true.
- The result is the list of cells up to the goal cell, excluding the start cell. None if there is no path.
- Differences from the original:
  { column, row } is GridCell, and null is None.
  The heap is ported as is from the original code, so when several paths have the same cost it picks the same path as the original. (the standard BinaryHeap picks in a different order)

그리드 유틸.\n- 원본 misc/grid.js 를 옮긴 것이다. 연결성:
Grid utility.
- A port of the original misc/grid.js. Gathers things rebuilt in every grid game, like connectivity checks (flood fill) and tile collision checks.
- Whether a cell is passable is decided by the is_passable_handler(column, row) callback. All functions are static.
- Differences from the original:
  The original { column, row } object is returned as GridCell, and the { x, y } of to_world_center as Vector2.
  Cell indexes are i32 so negative cells (outside the top left of the world) can be represented.
  Coordinates are taken as f32, but cell math is done in f64 like the original (JS number). (the 0.000001 subtraction in test_rect_overlap vanishes in f32)

Single-line text with a shadow. (ShadowText in vanilla.js core/component/shadowtext.js)
- Laying a shadow with two text nodes (the same text in black below, the text on top) makes the two show through separately, so when the node is faded the shadow beneath shows through the faded text.
  This component bakes the look of the text placed over the shadow into one image and draws that single sheet, so the node's opacity applies to the text and shadow as one sheet.
- Horizontal alignment is left, center or right within the node, and vertically it is the node's center.
- If the text exceeds the node width, it shrinks from the initial size down to the minimum ratio (set_fit_minimum_ratio) to fit.
- The shadow can be blurred with three box blurs (close to Gaussian). The baked image edge is widened by the blur amount.
- Rebakes when the bake scale, text, style, text direction or node width changes, or when a new font is loaded. If a bake of the same look already exists, it is shared. (sharedbakecache.rs)
- The text direction (set_text_direction, the original setTextDirection, initially Ltr) drives bidirectional ordering and shaping, and resolves alignment Start / End.
- Off-screen culling is judged by the rectangle where the last baked sheet is placed (including overflowing text and the shadow margin). It is not culled if it has not been baked yet since a setter changed it, or if the node width or bake scale has changed.
- Italic, underline, strikethrough (set_italic, set_underline, set_strikethrough): the line position and thickness are the same as Text's middle baseline, and the lines are baked together with the text so the shadow lies beneath them too.
  It is single-line text shrunk to fit, so there is no wrap mode.
- On the web, as in the original, it sets the shadow (shadowColor, shadowBlur, shadowOffsetY) on a canvas and bakes with fillText in the text color. (bake_shadow_text in platform/web/systemfont.rs, the margin and position calculations match the original)
  Desktop gets the shape with the text cache's rasterize_text and computes the shadow with three box blurs.
- Color glyphs (emoji) are placed in their own colors multiplied only by the text color's alpha, and the shadow is cast by the emoji shapes too. (the original fillStyle and canvas shadow)
- Differences from the original: the original setFontFace(FontFace) is set_font_family (a loaded font name), and the shadow color and opacity (setShadow's color string and opacity) are taken as one Color (alpha is the opacity).
  The original getBakeCanvas is get_bake_image, which returns the baked Image instead of the baked canvas.

- In the original, the browser's Canvas2D does all of this. (CSS font selection, the bidirectional algorithm, HarfBuzz shaping, Skia rasterization)
  The Rust version follows the same steps with crates:
  - Font faces (FontFaceDescriptors): like CSS @font-face, several faces with different weight, style and character ranges (unicode-range) sit under one name.
    Selection follows the CSS Fonts order (style → weight), and faces with the same weight and style split the drawing by character range. Faces loaded later come first.
  - Bidirectional ordering: unicode-bidi (UAX #9). The paragraph direction is given by the baking side. (the original canvas.direction)
  - Shaping: rustybuzz (a port of HarfBuzz). Places Arabic joining, ligatures, kerning and combining mark positions like the browser does.
    Like Chrome's HarfBuzzFace::GetScaledFont, the position scale is the font size in 16.16 fixed point. rustybuzz 0.20.1 has no scale, so the repository keeps a copy in third_party/rustybuzz
    with hb_font_set_scale added (Face::set_scale). Font unit values are rounded at that scale with em_scale and variable GPOS deltas with em_scalef,
    and axis values are normalized like HarfBuzz hb_ot_var_normalize_coords. The third_party/ttf-parser kept beside it fixes the device table base of pair kerning (PairPos format 1).
  - Rasterization: fontdue's glyph index rasterization. If there is no bold face, fake bold is applied per glyph, and if there is no italic face, fake italic.
    Color glyphs (sbix, CBDT, COLR) are drawn in their own colors by colorglyph.rs. Like Chrome, fake italic is applied to them and fake bold is not.
- Emoji presentation: VS16 (FE0F), Emoji_Presentation characters, skin tone modifiers, flags, keycaps and tag sequences pick a face with color glyphs first. Everything else (including VS15) picks a non-color face first.
  Chrome draws ❤️ (FE0F) with a color emoji font even if the specified font has a monochrome ❤, and a plain ❤ with the specified font. (checked with Canvas2D in Chrome on Mac)
- Fake italic and fake bold use the same values Chromium gives Skia:
  a skew of 1/4 (setSkewX(-SK_Scalar1 / 4) in font_platform_data.cc), and bold widens the outline by stroking it with a thickness of 1/24 (9px or less) ~ 1/32 (36px or more) of the font size.
  (kStdFakeBoldInterpKeys / Values in Skia SkTextFormatParams.h) Neither changes the advance.
  Fake bold is used when the requested weight is 600 or more and the chosen face is below 600. (Blink kBoldThreshold)
- LoadedFont holds the font bytes together with the rustybuzz face. (self_cell, the face borrows the bytes) When the registration is removed and nothing uses it anymore, the bytes are freed too.
  Several faces from the same file (the weights in a TTC, weight instances of a variable font) share the bytes (Rc).
- Font collections like TTC are read by choosing a face index (face_index). (find_collection_face_index chooses by weight and style)
- Variable fonts (the wght axis in fvar) make weight instances from axis values. (variation_list of create_from_shared_bytes) rustybuzz reads the axis values for shaping,
  but fontdue cannot read axis values for rasterization and cannot draw the outlines of variable fonts like Mac SFNS, so variable fonts get axis-applied outlines from skrifa and are drawn with colorglyph's area accumulation rasterizer.
  (Chrome also draws variable font weights from axis values)
- Optical size (the opsz axis) and the tracking table (trak): Chrome sets a font's opsz axis to the font size. (the initial value auto of font-optical-sizing, FontPlatformDataFromCTFont in Mac
  font_platform_data_mac.mm, font_custom_platform_data.cc for web fonts on every OS. Not applied to Windows and Linux system fonts)
  Shaping gives HarfBuzz the font size as ptem to add the AAT trak table's tracking. (GetScaledFont in harfbuzz_face.cc, on Mac the advances of fonts with trak and without sbix
  are computed with HarfBuzz instead of CoreText) The Rust version also applies opsz and adds trak at the baking size (the original enlarges the px in the font string by the bake scale).
  trak is added here, not by rustybuzz, the way HarfBuzz 15 (hb-aat-layout-trak-table.hh) does. Between sizes it interpolates linearly without rounding, outside the first and last entries of the table
  it uses the end values, and it is added only to the advance of the first glyph of a cluster. Not applied to fonts without a STAT table.
  (rustybuzz 0.20 rounds to integer font units, extrapolates outside the table, adds half to x_offset too, and does not look at STAT)
  The Mac system UI font (SFNS, opsz 17 ~ 96, initially 28) matches Chrome at 16px with opsz 17 and trak -40 units. (color emoji keep the CoreText advance as is)
- Per-word shaping: Chrome's canvas (SegmentWord in platform/fonts/plain_text_node.cc) splits text into words and shapes them separately. There is no kerning or ligature across spaces.
  Spaces (U+0020), tabs and ZWSP are one each, and CJK characters and emoji are separate per character. (find_chrome_word_end) The canvas turns tabs, line feeds, form feeds and carriage returns into spaces.
- Mac: glyphs are drawn with CoreText like the original Chrome on Mac. (platform/desktop/coretextglyph.rs) Non-color glyphs are A8 masks with the same settings as Chrome Canvas2D (font smoothing,
  undoing the CoreGraphics gamma, gamma pre-correction by the text color luminance, 1/4 pixel subpixel positions), and color emoji fonts (sbix) read from files are CoreText color drawings. (rasterize_glyph_at)
  The advance of color emoji is multiplied by the ratio CoreText enlarges drawing at small sizes and rounded to integer pixels. (20 at 16px, 16 at 13px, same as Chrome measureText)

- Fake italic and fake bold use the same values Chromium gives Skia:
  a skew of 1/4 (setSkewX(-SK_Scalar1 / 4) in font_platform_data.cc), and bold widens the outline by stroking it with a thickness of 1/24 (9px or less) ~ 1/32 (36px or more) of the font size.
  (kStdFakeBoldInterpKeys / Values in Skia SkTextFormatParams.h) Neither changes the advance.
  Fake bold is used when the requested weight is 600 or more and the chosen face is below 600. (Blink kBoldThreshold)
- LoadedFont holds the font bytes together with the rustybuzz face. (self_cell, the face borrows the bytes) When the registration is removed and nothing uses it anymore, the bytes are freed too.
  Several faces from the same file (the weights in a TTC, weight instances of a variable font) share the bytes (Rc).
- Font collections like TTC are read by choosing a face index (face_index). (find_collection_face_index chooses by weight and style)
- Variable fonts (the wght axis in fvar) make weight instances from axis values. (variation_list of create_from_shared_bytes) rustybuzz reads the axis values for shaping,
  but fontdue cannot read axis values for rasterization and cannot draw the outlines of variable fonts like Mac SFNS, so variable fonts get axis-applied outlines from skrifa and are drawn with colorglyph's area accumulation rasterizer.
  (Chrome also draws variable font weights from axis values)
- Optical size (the opsz axis) and the tracking table (trak): Chrome sets a font's opsz axis to the font size. (the initial value auto of font-optical-sizing, FontPlatformDataFromCTFont in Mac
  font_platform_data_mac.mm, font_custom_platform_data.cc for web fonts on every OS. Not applied to Windows and Linux system fonts)
  Shaping gives HarfBuzz the font size as ptem to add the AAT trak table's tracking. (GetScaledFont in harfbuzz_face.cc, on Mac the advances of fonts with trak and without sbix
  are computed with HarfBuzz instead of CoreText) The Rust version also applies opsz and adds trak at the baking size (the original enlarges the px in the font string by the bake scale).
  trak is added here, not by rustybuzz, the way HarfBuzz 15 (hb-aat-layout-trak-table.hh) does. Between sizes it interpolates linearly without rounding, outside the first and last entries of the table
  it uses the end values, and it is added only to the advance of the first glyph of a cluster. Not applied to fonts without a STAT table.
  (rustybuzz 0.20 rounds to integer font units, extrapolates outside the table, adds half to x_offset too, and does not look at STAT)
  The Mac system UI font (SFNS, opsz 17 ~ 96, initially 28) matches Chrome at 16px with opsz 17 and trak -40 units. (color emoji keep the CoreText advance as is)
- Per-word shaping: Chrome's canvas (SegmentWord in platform/fonts/plain_text_node.cc) splits text into words and shapes them separately. There is no kerning or ligature across spaces.
  Spaces (U+0020), tabs and ZWSP are one each, and CJK characters and emoji are separate per character. (find_chrome_word_end) The canvas turns tabs, line feeds, form feeds and carriage returns into spaces.
- Mac: color emoji fonts (sbix) read from files and fonts without outline tables (hvgl in PingFang) are drawn with CoreText. (platform/desktop/coretextglyph.rs, Chrome on Mac in the original also draws with CoreText)
  The advance of color emoji is multiplied by the ratio CoreText enlarges drawing at small sizes and rounded to integer pixels. (20 at 16px, 16 at 13px, same as Chrome measureText)

노드 레이아웃.\n- 원본 misc/nodelayout.js 를 옮긴 것:
Node layout.
- A port of the original misc/nodelayout.js. A fluent builder that lays out a node hierarchy declaratively without local variables.
- Sets position and size with number pairs (x, y) instead of Vector2.
- Usage:
  ```text
    let panel_id = NodeLayout::create()
        .pivot(Pivot::MIDDLE_CENTER)
        .content_size(680.0, 900.0)
        .component_with(Paint::new(), |paint| { paint.set_color(Color::create(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 1.0)); })
        .children([
            NodeLayout::create()
                .content_size(120.0, 70.0)
                .component_with(Text::new(), |text| { text.set_text("OK"); }),
        ])
        .build(node_tree, Some(parent_id));
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  In the Rust version nodes only live inside the tree (NodeTree), so the builder collects settings in order and creates the node at build(node_tree, parent_id), applying them in that order.
  So components are also attached at build with node_tree.add_component. (components that create child nodes when attach_to_tree is called work too)
  There is no node class, so it is create() instead of create(nodeClass).
  component(type, callback) is split into component(value) and component_with(value, callback). (Rust has no optional arguments)
  The variadic arguments of children(...layouts) are taken as a single array or Vec.
  anchored_position is applied at build relative to the parent's content_size. In the original it was called before the parent was attached, so it was effectively the same as local_position.
  mask_enabled(false) removes all of the node's Masks, not only the first mask as in the original.

Node layout.
- A port of the original misc/nodelayout.js. A fluent builder that lays out node hierarchies declaratively without local variables.
- Positions and sizes are set with number pairs (x, y) without Vector2.
- Usage:
  ```text
    let panel_id = NodeLayout::create()
        .pivot(Pivot::MIDDLE_CENTER)
        .content_size(680.0, 900.0)
        .component_with(Paint::new(), |paint| { paint.set_color(Color::create(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 1.0)); })
        .children([
            NodeLayout::create()
                .content_size(120.0, 70.0)
                .component_with(Text::new(), |text| { text.set_text("OK"); }),
        ])
        .build(node_tree, Some(parent_id));
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  In the Rust version nodes live only inside the tree (NodeTree), so the builder collects settings in order and, at build(node_tree, parent_id), creates the nodes and applies them in that order.
  So components are also attached with node_tree.add_component at build. (components whose attach_to_tree creates child nodes work too)
  There is no node class, so it is create() instead of create(nodeClass).
  component(type, callback) is split into component(value) and component_with(value, callback). (Rust has no optional arguments)
  The variadic arguments of children(...layouts) are taken as one array or Vec.
  Like the original, anchored_position is applied at build after attaching to the parent, relative to the anchor point of the parent content_size. (the anchor is the one at the time the setting is applied, a local_position set later wins)
  Like the original, mask_enabled(false) removes all Masks of that node, not only the first mask.

노드 트리.\n- 씬의 노드를 저장소 하나(slotmap)에 담고, 부모:
Node tree.
- Holds the scene's nodes in one storage (slotmap) and links parents and children by handle (NodeId).
- Game code carries NodeIds around and takes nodes out with get_node / get_node_mut (or `tree[node_id]`).
  For the NodeId of a deleted node, get_node returns None. (in place of the original isDestroyed)
- In the original, a parent holds child objects in children[] and a child points back with parent.
  In Rust that form (`Rc<RefCell>`) brings runtime borrow checking costs and reference cycles, so it was changed to handles.
- When running tick / touch, only the one component being called is briefly taken out of its node (an empty placeholder is left in its place) and a ComponentContext (own node + whole tree + engine) is passed.
  So a component can find, change and create other nodes, and also find other components of the same node (siblings) with get_node_mut().`get_component_mut::<T>()`.
- Nodes deleted while running are left inactive in place and actually deleted after the run finishes.
- Sibling order (the original Node.setSiblingIndex, getSiblingIndex, getSiblings) and hierarchy checks (isActiveInHierarchy, TransformNode.isVisibleInHierarchy)
  need to look at the parent, so NodeTree does them taking a node handle. The original -1 and null are None.
  The original isVisible means active with opacity greater than 0. The Rust version also has a separate visibility flag (set_visible) that turns off drawing, and checks that too.
- The hierarchy functions of the original Node keep the same names. Where node objects are passed it is NodeId, and names ending in _id (_ids) are the counterparts that return handles.
  (getParent → get_parent_id, getChildren → get_child_ids, getSiblings → get_sibling_ids) Detaching from the parent (remove_child) does not delete the node.
- The original WorldNode.getPosition, setPosition, getWorldCorners, getWorldBounds are also done taking a node handle. The global position is, like the original, the position of the pivot point
  computed relative to the parent pivot, and the four corners are computed from that global position, global size and global rotation.

Hit area widening. (UIHitArea of vanilla.js ui/uihitarea.js)
- Leaves the visible button as is and places a transparent hit area as the sibling right behind the button, widening its width and height to at least the minimum size. (easier to press with a finger)
- The node drawn later receives the press, so the button receives presses over the button and the hit area receives only the widened margin around it.
- Pressing the hit area fires the button's click notifications (Clicked, Click) as is. If the button is turned off or not pressable, the hit area follows.
- It follows the button's position, size, and pivot every frame, so it stays aligned even when the screen moves the button.
- When a clipping node is set, the widened margin is clipped so it does not go outside that node's rectangle. (the button's own area stays as is, so areas outside the window or scroll area are not pressed)
- Usage: UIHitArea::attach(node_tree, button_id, minimum_size) (call after the button is attached to its parent)
