다단 블룸 이펙트. (원본 experimental/graphics/mul:
Multi-level bloom effect. (the original experimental/graphics/multilevelbloomeffect.js)
- Extracts the bright part at half size, blurs it while halving the size, then adds it back to the level above while doubling the size. The first level (half the scene size) is the result. (get_result_texture)
- Extraction: from the average of four source samples, the part whose brightness (the largest of the three channels) exceeds the threshold. Within the knee width around the threshold it comes in smoothly. (set_threshold(threshold, knee))
- Downsampling is a dual filter mixing the center four and the four corners (one diagonal step), and upsampling is a nine-tap tent. The shaders match the original character for character.
- With use_float_color the targets are RGBA16F, so bright values above 1 are blurred as they are. (for HDR scenes, with RGBA8 they are clipped at 1)
- Usage: resize(gl, scene width, height) → render(gl, scene texture) → get_result_texture() is multiplied by the strength and added in the composite pass.
- Side effects: disables the depth test and blending, makes TEXTURE0 active, and changes the framebuffer binding. The blend function is restored to the previous one.

다이나믹 폰트. (원본 misc/dynamicfont.js 의 Dynam:
Dynamic font. (DynamicFont, GlyphInfo of the original misc/dynamicfont.js)
- Bakes a chosen set of characters in one font and one size into a glyph atlas (a single image), and draws text by cutting glyphs from the atlas.
  Every character uses the same image, so Graphic draws them in a single batch. (unlike Text, which bakes a texture per string, batching is not broken)
  Use it where characters change often and the same characters are drawn many times, like scores, damage numbers, and clocks.
- The atlas places glyphs in rows within 1024 pixels of width, with a 2 pixel gap between glyphs. (same as the original)
- Characters are counted in grapheme clusters (final consonants, combining marks, emoji sequences). Characters not in the atlas leave a gap of half the font size and move on. (same as the original)
- Characters are baked in white, and color glyphs (emoji) in their own colors. (the original fillTexts in white and the browser draws emoji in their own colors)
- Differences from the original:
  The original setFontAsset(FontAsset) is set_font_family(name of the loaded font). (pass FontAsset.get_family)
  The original getAtlasCanvas is get_atlas_image (`Rc<Image>`). On desktop, glyphs are baked with the font faces of the glyph cache (including shaping, fake bold and italic),
  and cannot be baked if no face covers the character. On the web, they are baked with the browser Canvas2D as in the original.
  build_atlas and draw_text take a Graphic. (the fonts live in Graphic's glyph cache)

Dynamic font. (DynamicFont, GlyphInfo of the original misc/dynamicfont.js)
- Bakes the chosen characters in one font and one size into a glyph atlas (one image), and draws text by cutting glyphs out of the atlas.
  Every character uses the same image, so Graphic draws it in one batch. (unlike Text, which bakes a texture per string, batching is not broken)
  Used where characters change often and the same characters are drawn many times, like scores, damage numbers and clocks.
- The atlas lays glyphs out in rows within 1024 pixels wide, with a 2 pixel gap between glyphs. (same as the original)
- Characters are counted in grapheme clusters (Hangul final consonants, combining marks, emoji sequences). Characters not in the atlas leave a gap of half the font size and are skipped. (same as the original)
- Characters are baked in white, and color glyphs (emoji) in their own colors. (the original calls fillText in white and the browser draws emoji in their own colors)
- Differences from the original:
  The original setFontAsset(FontAsset) is set_font_family(registered font name). (pass FontAsset.get_family)
  The original getAtlasCanvas is get_atlas_image (`Rc<Image>`). Desktop bakes glyphs with the font faces of the text cache (shaping, synthetic bold and italic included),
  and a character not covered by any face cannot be baked. (the other characters are baked) The web bakes with the browser Canvas2D like the original.
  build_atlas and draw_text take Graphic. (fonts are in Graphic's text cache)

Button motion. (ButtonMotion, ButtonMotionStyle, attachButtonMotion, setButtonMotionArea, shakeButton of vanilla.js ui/buttonmotion.js)
- Attached to a button node after UIButton, it reads that button's state every frame and scales the node up and down around its center.
  It grows on hover, shrinks while pressed, bounces on release, and shakes left and right when shake is called while it cannot be pressed.
- Colors are not touched. (the background and text colors of text buttons are set by the screen's code, and image buttons are handled by UIButton's tint)
- Devices whose primary input is a finger do not use hover. (so it does not look hovered from the finger position left after release)
- When there is no motion, the node's position and size are not touched, so it does not clash with other effects that scale the same node.
- The style is set per button with set_style, or if left empty follows the closest node above with a ButtonMotionArea, otherwise Normal.
- In the Inset style, while hovered, brightens the color of the button's background Paint and draws a white rim inside. (buttons without a background Paint or that are invisible are not brightened)
  To have the decoration on a button brighten in its own way, hook a function with set_lit_handler. (the button's pressed color is then left transparent)
  The hooked function is kept in an `Rc<RefCell>`. get_lit_handler returns that Rc, and the caller borrows it with borrow_mut to call it.
- Differences from the original: the centering math reads the pivot (the original only handles a top-left pivot), and the marker that sets the style is the ButtonMotionArea component (the original uses a WeakMap).
  The brightened background and white rim are not child nodes. (the original uses the two bottommost children, and if the text is a component of the same node as in the Rust example, children would cover the text)

대사 진행기와 대본 파서.\n- 원본 misc/dialogue.js 를:
Dialogue runner and script parser.
- A port of the original misc/dialogue.js. (DialogueRunner, DialogueScriptParser)
- DialogueRunner: steps through a script made of lines, choices, labels, and jumps in order. The state machine that visual novels / RPG dialogues / tutorials each built on their own.
  ```text
    runner.set_script(entries); runner.start(None);
    runner.get_current()   → DialogueCurrent::Line / choice / finished
    runner.advance() on a line, runner.choose(index) on a choice.
  ```
- DialogueScriptParser: turns one-line command text into a script.
  ```text
    /label label_name
    /jump label_name
    /speaker speaker_name              (default speaker for the following /say)
    /say line text
    /option option text -> label_name       (consecutive /option lines are grouped into one choice)
    /end
  ```
  Lines not starting with "/" are treated as /say of the preceding speaker. "//" is a comment.
- Differences from the original:
  Script entries are the DialogueEntry enum instead of objects with several fields. One entry cannot be both a label and a line.
  get_current returns the DialogueCurrent enum instead of a { kind, ... } object, and a choice's options are a list of option texts (`Vec<String>`).

  - Every frame reads the previous frame's field state, and turns IME on and positions the candidate window only when the focused field uses platform input (use_dominput).

Desktop audio backend. (Windows, Mac, Linux, the engine mixer on top of cpal output)
- In place of AudioContext: opens the default output device with cpal and runs a mixer at its sample rate (mixer.rs). If there is no device it reports once and does not open again.
  There is no browser autoplay policy, so the user gesture is treated as present from the start. sample_rate(), current_time() have the same names as the web AudioContext.
- The node graph is the same as the original WebAudio and the math matches Chrome. (header comment of mixer.rs)
  One AudioPlayer = source + GainNode (+ StereoPannerNode when a nonzero pan is first set), to that bus if an output (AudioOutputNode) is given, otherwise to the output.
  One AudioBus = a GainNode connected to the output. (AudioGainNode, the original getGainNode) Players made on a bus hold a bus handle,
  so as in the original WebAudio the bus stays alive while connected players exist. The node is removed once all handles are gone.
- Context suspend (SoundSystem calls it while muted): the mixer stops rendering, so the sound and clock stop in place. (the original AudioContext.suspend) resume starts it again.
- The context clock (get_audio_context_time) is the rendered time. (the original currentTime, rises by 128 / sample rate seconds every 128-frame quantum)
- A management thread holds the stream. When the device is removed (or, except on Mac, when the default device changes), it reopens the default device with the same mixer. (the original Chrome also follows the default device)
- In place of AudioBuffer: holds decoded sound in an Arc. Cloning is cheap. decode decodes it the same way as the original Chrome decodeAudioData.
  (Opus and Vorbis in webm, ogg, mp3, wav, flac, AAC in m4a and aac. Trimming of both ends, 44100Hz, downmixed to 1 or 2 channels by the WebAudio speaker rules)
- Volume, pan and stop change right from the next render quantum. Playback rate applies from the next playback. (same as the original)
- Volume is the AudioParam of the GainNode. Setting the volume is assigning the original gain.value, and SoundSystem sets automation (setValueAtTime calls) and stop(when) as in the original.
  The current gain.value (get_gain_value) is the intrinsic value the sound thread computes every quantum.
- BeepPlayer's tones build OscillatorNode → GainNode (envelope automation) → output on the mixer like the original playTone. (the math matches Chrome, oscillator.rs)
  The waveform's band-limited tables (PeriodicWave) are built once per sample rate, as in the original context.
데스크탑 웹이면 true. (모바일이거나, 맥인데 navigator.ma: true if desktop web. (false if mobile, or a Mac with navigator.maxTouchPoints of 2 or more; always true for desktop builds)
데스크탑 웹인지. (마우스 휠, 키보드 안내처럼 데스크탑에서만 보일 것을:
Whether it is desktop web. (used to pick out things shown only on desktop, such as mouse wheel and keyboard hints)
- Not if mobile. Safari on iPad reports itself as Mac like a desktop, so a Mac with multiple touch points counts as an iPad.
데스크탑 플랫폼. (윈도우, 맥, 리눅스)\n- 창(winit)과 GL:
Desktop platform. (Windows, Mac, Linux)
- Creates the window (winit) and a GL 3.3 core context (glutin), and runs one engine frame per window redraw request.
- Converts window events into the input manager's form. (keys use the same names as W3C KeyboardEvent.code, any mouse button is a touch as in the original, can be changed to left only)
- The engine core (EngineRunner) does not know about the window. Frames are called here, and the screen is presented after drawing.
- Text input (key characters, editing keys, IME composition) and the clipboard are handled by desktop/textinput.rs. The right button is a context menu request for input fields.
- Gamepad vibration on Mac is handled by desktop/gamepadhaptics.rs. (GameController and CoreHaptics, on other OSes gilrs vibrates)
- The last used device is recorded on every key, mouse and finger event. Keys to prevent (set_prevented_keys) and blocking the right-click menu are not used, since a window has no browser default actions to block.
  (same result as blocking them in Chrome. On Windows winit does not pass WM_SYSKEYUP of a menuless window to DefWindowProc, so Alt and F10 do not enter the system menu either)
- Page events: the window is occluded (Occluded, reported by Mac and X11), minimized (size 0 or is_minimized, which is how Windows reports it), the app is suspended (suspended, mobile),
  the Wayland frame callback has not come for over 3 seconds (occlusion on Chrome Linux Wayland, desktop/waylandframecallback.rs)
  If any one of these holds, Hidden; once all clear, Visible and on_page_visibility_restored. Focus is Focused / Blurred, mouse button and finger presses are PointerDown.
  Wayland's xdg_toplevel suspended state is held by winit and not reported, so it cannot be received.
- Wayland vertical sync: sets the EGL swap interval to 0 and waits up to 1/20 second for the previous frame callback before presenting. (with interval 1, Mesa stalls inside the swap on an occluded window)
- Canvas size (auto_resize_on_window_resize): the window is like a page whose canvas fills the window. When on, it fits visualViewport (the window minus the bottom covered by the on-screen keyboard) as in the original
  and applies ignore_virtual_keyboard_resize and the canvas aspect ratio limit. When off, it is the window size as is.
- On-screen keyboard: on Windows, like Chrome, focusing a platform input field with a finger shows the touch keyboard (InputPane) and removes the covered area from visualViewport. (desktop/windowsinputpane.rs)
  Mac and Linux do not shrink the viewport, like Chrome.
- Preserving the drawing buffer (preserve_drawing_buffer): captures the finished frame and redraws it at the start of the next frame. (desktop/preserveddrawingbuffer.rs)
- Page process restore (on_page_process_restored, the original resume after a Chromium freeze and bfcache): resumed after suspended, and waking from system sleep.
  Windows subclasses the window to receive PBT_APMRESUMEAUTOMATIC of WM_POWERBROADCAST. (desktop/windowsplatform.rs, the Windows monotonic clock keeps running during sleep so the clock cannot tell)
  Mac and Linux treat it as woken if between two frames the wall clock (SystemTime) advanced more than SYSTEM_SLEEP_GAP_SECONDS beyond the monotonic clock (Instant).
  (Rust Instant is CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW on Mac and CLOCK_MONOTONIC on Linux, so it stops during sleep. Rust notes that it does not guarantee this)
- Whether the primary input is a finger (is_coarse_pointer): Windows ports Chromium's (pointer: coarse) check and is true in tablet mode or on a touch device without a mouse.
  Mac is false, since Chromium always treats it as a mouse too. Linux and other Unixes, like Chromium, read touchscreens and
  mice and touchpads from the display server (Wayland wl_seat capabilities, X11 XInput device list) and are true if there is only a touchscreen. (desktop/linuxplatform.rs, the value read is used for 2 seconds)
- Key names: winit's SuperLeft, SuperRight become W3C's MetaLeft, MetaRight, and winit's Meta becomes W3C's Super.
- Image cursors (PointerCursor.register_image_cursor): reads the image file and makes a winit CustomCursor. On Mac the image size is the point size as is, so the 1x image is used;
  Windows and Linux use physical pixels, so the image and hotspot are scaled to the window scale (using the 2x image if present). While creating, or if creation fails, the CSS cursor given with it is used.
- Render scale upper limit (ViewManager.set_max_render_pixel_ratio): draws at the size reduced to that scale and stretches to the window size at the end of the frame. (desktop/renderscaler.rs)
  Input coordinates are converted to logical coordinates with the window's scale, so they do not depend on the render size.
- Canvas aspect ratio limit (EngineConfiguration.max_canvas_aspect_ratio): if the window is more elongated than that, the canvas (drawing area) is shrunk as in the original and centered in the window, and the rest is black.
  The canvas top-left is subtracted from input coordinates, and read_canvas_client_position returns that position.
- Query values of the page address (read_page_query_value) are read from the environment variable VANILLA_ followed by the name in upper snake case. (safeArea → VANILLA_SAFE_AREA)
- Capture mode (VANILLA_CAPTURE_PATH) runs with the window hidden. A hidden window has no redraw requests or vertical sync, so frames run right away in about_to_wait and pace themselves to the refresh rate.
  Occlusion notifications are not received. On Mac it does not take the Dock icon or focus either. To see the window, VANILLA_CAPTURE_SHOW_WINDOW=1.

Draggable component. (UIDraggable of the original ui/uidraggable.js)
- Attached to a node, it can be pressed and dragged. On release it notifies with the end event, and with set_snap_back_enabled(true) it slides back to where it was before being grabbed.
- The movement adds the view coordinate difference as is to the local coordinates. (sensitivity differs if an ancestor node has a scale. same as the original)

- Usage:
  ```text
    let draggable = node_tree.add_component(card_id, UIDraggable::new()).expect("draggable");
    draggable.set_snap_back_enabled(true);
    draggable.set_drag_end_event(Box::new(|draggable, context, view_position| { if is_drop_spot { draggable.settle_here(context.get_node_tree_mut()); } }));
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - Events take the drag component and the context. (move / end also the view coordinates) Original callbacks take only the component (and the view coordinates).
  - settle_here / snap_home need to read and write the node position, so they take the tree. (context.get_node_tree_mut() inside the end event)

Dropdown. (UIDropdown of the original ui/uidropdown.js, a combo box)
- The closed header button shows the current value, and pressing it expands a list of options downward. Pressing a row selects it and collapses.
- On expand, the list is moved to the last child of the tree root so it is not covered by sibling nodes drawn later. (moved back under the header button on collapse)
- The popup list node is excluded from the header button's tint targets. (exclude_node_from_tint, otherwise after selecting, the header button reapplies the old row colors it stored when pressed every tick and
  covers the selection highlight) After changing the highlight, the row buttons are made to store their original tint colors again. (on the spot in the original, on the next tick in the Rust version)
- The original is a node that inherits WorldNode. The Rust version is a component attached to a node (host), and on attach, like the original constructor, it
  sets up the host (top-left pivot, size, interactable), puts Paint + UIButton + UILabel (header text) on the host, and creates the arrow node and the popup list node as children.
  UIDropdown::create(node_tree, parent_id, options) takes the place of the original new UIDropdown(options) + add_child.
- Usage:
  ```text
    let dropdown_id = UIDropdown::create(node_tree, panel_id, UIDropdownOptions { width: 180.0, ..UIDropdownOptions::default() });
    node_tree.with_component_mut::<UIDropdown, _>(dropdown_id, |dropdown, tree| dropdown.set_option_list(tree, &["Dark", "Light", "System"]));
    node_tree[dropdown_id].get_component_mut::<UIDropdown>().unwrap().set_changed_event(Box::new(|dropdown, context| { dropdown.get_selected_text(); }));
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - Functions that change the tree (set_option_list, set_open, set_selected_index) take the tree. Scene code calls them with node_tree.with_component_mut.
    select_index takes the context to pass it to the changed event. (row buttons call it with ComponentContext::with_component_mut)
  - The changed event takes the dropdown and the context. The options object is the UIDropdownOptions struct.
  - Row highlights are updated through the list of created row nodes instead of the popup list's child order. (when rebuilt during tick, deleted rows briefly remain as children)
  - The arrow characters are small triangles (▾ ▴, U+25BE / U+25B4) as in the original. Characters missing from the default fonts (Malgun Gothic, Segoe UI, Arial) are
    drawn with a system fallback font like Chrome does. (core/textshaping.rs)
  - Node names are "DropdownArrow", "DropdownPopup", "DropdownOption{index}" as in the original. The host name is chosen by the creator. ("UIDropdown" for create)

  ```text
    let floating_text_id = FloatingText::create(node_tree, root_id);
    FloatingText::spawn(node_tree, floating_text_id, "-120", position, FloatingTextOptions { color: Color::create(1.0, 0.4, 0.4, 1.0), ..FloatingTextOptions::default() });
  ```

  The original is a node that inherits WorldNode. The Rust version is a component attached to a node, and create makes the node and attaches it.

Render target. (the original experimental/graphics/rendertarget.js)
- Offscreen framebuffer + color texture [+ depth renderbuffer / depth texture]. The basic unit of a post-processing chain.
- Options can enable multiple color attachments (MRT) / half-float color (HDR) / depth texture / multisampling / depth bits.
  The original options object { colorAttachmentCount, useFloatColor, useDepthTexture, sampleCount, depthBits } became RenderTargetOptions.
- When sample_count is 2 or more, drawing goes to multisample (MSAA) renderbuffers and resolve() resolves them into the color textures (and the depth texture).
  If it exceeds what the device supports (MAX_SAMPLES, and on the web also the sample counts supported per format), it is reduced to the largest supported value below it, and if that is unsupported or the framebuffer is incomplete, it is built without multisampling. (get_sample_count)
  Desktop GL 3.3 has no function to query the supported sample counts per format (glGetInternalformativ, GL 4.2), so only MAX_SAMPLES is checked. (3.3 supports up to MAX_SAMPLES for float and non-integer color formats)
  With multisampling, get_framebuffer is the multisample framebuffer drawn to, and get_resolve_framebuffer is the framebuffer with the textures attached. Call resolve() before reading the textures.
- depth_bits is the bit count of the depth renderbuffer (16 or 24). The depth texture is always 24-bit. With multisampling and a depth texture, the multisample depth is also built as 24-bit and resolved as is.

로컬 스토리지.\n- 원본 misc/localstorage.js 를 옮긴:
Local storage.
- A port of the original misc/localstorage.js. A set of static functions that persistently store string values under string keys.
- Where it is stored:
  Web (wasm32): window.localStorage as in the original. (separate per origin, keys used as is)
  Desktop: a single localstorage.json in the app folder. (a JSON object of key → string value, saved immediately on every write)
    Windows   %APPDATA%\{app name}\localstorage.json
    Mac       $HOME/Library/Application Support/{app name}/localstorage.json
    Linux     $XDG_DATA_HOME/{app name}/localstorage.json (if missing, $HOME/.local/share/{app name}/...)
    If the environment variables cannot be read, it goes under the temp folder (std::env::temp_dir).
  The app name defaults to the executable name. Change it with set_application_name or set_application_name_from_engine(EngineConfiguration.title).
  The folder can also be set directly with set_storage_directory. (tests, portable games)
- Differences from the original:
  Numbers are f64 like the original (JS number). Conversion to text is exactly the original String(number). (shortest notation, exponents like 1e+21 for 1e21 and above and 1e-7 and below, NaN, Infinity, -0 → "0")
    Reading is exactly the original Number(text). (trims JS whitespace, empty text is 0, 0x, 0o, 0b notation, "1.", ".5", exponents, Infinity, anything else is NaN)
  Desktop storage is held per thread and then written to the file. (the engine runs on one thread)
- Swapping the storage: passing a LocalStorageBackend to set_backend uses it instead of the default storage above. (such as a platform SDK's storage)
  The trait takes the place of the original setBackend object ({ getItem, setItem, removeItem, getKeys, clear }). Exceptions in the original are reported as Err.
  The passed storage is put in `Rc<RefCell>`. get_backend returns that Rc, and the caller borrows it with borrow / borrow_mut.
- Does not crash when blocked: if there is no storage (a blocked localStorage on the web) or writing fails (full, folder cannot be created, Err from the swapped storage),
  values are kept in memory instead for as long as this run lives. (is_memory_fallback, gone after a restart)
- Reads (get_string, get_boolean, get_number, get_json) do not write the default value for missing keys. (same as the original)
- Unpaired surrogates: the original localStorage holds JS strings (UTF-16), so it stores values containing unpaired surrogates (such as cut emoji) and
  JSON that writes them as \ud83d. Rust String cannot hold such text, so they appear as the replacement character (U+FFFD) on the Rust side,
  and writing a read value back unmodified (set_item, set_string, set_json) writes the original UTF-16 units as they were. (misc/storagetext.rs)
  If the original units are needed, get_item_code_units and set_item_code_units read and write the JS string as is.
  Keys are the same. Two keys that differ only by unpaired surrogates (different keys in the original) look like the same text as Rust strings but are stored separately in the storage.
  get_keys_code_units returns all keys in their original units, and get_item_by_key_code_units, set_item_by_key_code_units,
  remove_item_by_key_code_units and contains_key_code_units distinguish both key and value by original units. (exactly the original localStorage functions)
  A Rust string key points to the key with exactly that text if it exists, otherwise to the first unpaired surrogate key that appears as that text. (keys received from get_keys can be used)
  The web writes JS strings as is to the browser localStorage, and the desktop file writes such values and keys as \udXXX like the original JSON.stringify.
  A swapped storage (LocalStorageBackend) exchanges Rust strings, so values are exactly the text that storage holds. (keys are also given as the displayed text)

로컬라이제이션.\n- 원본 misc/localization.js 를 옮긴:
Localization.
- A port of the original misc/localization.js. Gathers automatic language detection, translation tables, {0}{1} placeholder substitution, and fallback in one place.
- Keys can be the source text as is. If a key is not in the table, the source text (the key) is returned as is, so you can translate bit by bit.
- Usage:
  ```text
    Localization::set_table("en", [("Confirm", "OK"), ("{0} points earned", "Got {0} points")]);
    Localization::set_language(&Localization::detect_language(&["ko", "en"], "ko"));
    Localization::text("{0} points earned", &[&120]);
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  The original holds the tables in static fields of the class. The Rust version holds them in thread-local global state. (the engine runs on one thread)
  A table value is one string or a list of strings (LocalizationValue). A JSON table (read with JsonAsset) is put in with set_table_from_json.
  The variadic arguments of text are a list of Display references (&[&dyn Display]).
- Brought into the engine from Exoplanet Miner: matching language tags by dropping trailing parts one by one, and aliases (set_language_aliases),
  right-to-left languages (is_right_to_left, set_right_to_left) and wrapping inserted values in directional isolate characters (isolate_text),
  filling named placeholders (text_named, "{seconds}" style, values joined only by slashes are wrapped once as a whole).
  Layout mirroring (mirror_layout_x, read_layout_text_align, mirrorLayoutX, readLayoutTextAlign of the original LanguagePack).
  On the web detect_language reads navigator.languages as in the original, and on desktop it reads the system's preferred language order with sys-locale.
    (Windows GetUserPreferredUILanguages, Mac CFLocaleCopyPreferredLanguages, Linux LANGUAGE / LC_ALL / LC_MESSAGES / LANG environment variables)

- As in the original, segments are joined into one line. Without markup it draws with the contained Text.
Rich text component. (RichText and parse_markup_to_segments in the original core/component/richtext.js)
- Parses markup (the same form as Unity TMP) and joins segments into one line, each with its own font, size, color, bold, italic, underline and strikethrough.
  Supported tags: `<b>`, `<i>`, `<u>`, `<s>`, `<color=#RRGGBB[AA]>`, `<color=name>`, `<size=N>`. Unknown tags show up as plain text.
- The original inherits Text. The Rust version contains a Text (the same shape as UILabel containing a Text) and forwards the setters.
  Without markup it draws with the contained Text's draw. (multiple lines and wrap width as is) Properties a segment does not set use the Text's values.
- Segment layout (layout_segments) takes a measuring function instead of a Graphic. draw measures with measure_text of the text texture cache (textstringtexturecache).
- Differences from the original:
  - The segment property fontFace (FontFace / FontAsset) is font_family (a registered font name).
  - As in the original, a segment's underline, strikethrough and italic use the Text's values (set_underline, set_strikethrough, set_italic) when the segment property is absent.
  - An invalid #color (non-hexadecimal characters) is white. (the original gives a NaN color)
  - getIntrinsicContentSize is calculate_intrinsic_content_size, which takes a measuring function.
- Text direction: the paragraph direction is decided from the joined segment text (the contained Text's direction, the Graphic's direction if Inherit), and right to left places segments from the right.
  Each segment is shaped in that direction, and alignment Start / End is resolved in that direction too. (the original is the same)

Mac CoreText glyph drawing. (macOS only)
- A file not in the original. The original Chrome on Mac draws glyphs with CoreText (CoreGraphics). On the Mac the Rust version also draws glyphs here with CoreText. (called by textshaping.rs)
  Only this file can draw color emoji and fonts the open parsers cannot read.
  - Color emoji (sbix, Apple Color Emoji): at small text sizes CoreText draws emoji enlarged and lowered. (the 20px version at 16px, the text size as is from 24px)
    The emoji advance measured with measureText of Mac Chrome Canvas2D equals the height of the emoji box CoreText draws. (8px 10, 12px 15, 16px 20, 20px 22, 24px 24, 32px 32, 64px 64)
    Chrome's advance is that box height rounded to an integer. (16.25 at 13px is 16, 12.5 at 10px is 13. Matches Chrome at 23 sizes from 8 ~ 128px, textshaping.rs does the rounding)
    CoreText's advance (CTFontGetAdvancesForGlyphs) adds the font's tracking table (trak) and differs from Chrome, so it is not used.
  - Fonts with glyph outlines in none of glyf, CFF, CFF2: PingFangUI.ttc on Mac 26 (the Chinese fallback font) has its outlines in Apple's private hvgl table.
- The font is built from that face's PostScript name. (CoreText draws emoji enlarged only for fonts registered in the system) For hidden fonts whose name starts with a dot, or when axis values are set,
  it builds from the CTFontManagerCreateFontDescriptorsFromURL descriptors of the file path, chosen by PostScript name (or by order within the collection if none). CTFonts built per text size are kept. (one thread, cleared when full)
- Color glyph pictures are drawn in white into a premultiplied RGBA (sRGB) bitmap context. Grayscale antialiasing like the Chrome canvas, with LCD font smoothing off.
- The coverage of non-color glyphs (rasterize_glyph_mask) is drawn the same way as Mac Chrome Canvas2D. Blink FontPlatformData::CreateSkFont gives canvas text
  kSubpixelAntiAlias and subpixel positioning, and since a transparent canvas does not know the pixel layout (kUnknown_SkPixelGeometry), Skia derives A8 from the LCD drawing instead of LCD.
  Skia SkScalerContext_Mac then draws black text on a white RGB bitmap (DeviceRGB, no alpha) with font smoothing (CGContextSetShouldSmoothFonts) on,
  undoes the CoreGraphics gamma 2 with a square table (gLinearCoverageFromCGLCDValue), and corrects the luminance of the inverted RGB (SkComputeLuminance) with the gamma pre-correction table.
  The glyph box is CTFontGetBoundingRectsForGlyphs plus the subpixel part, rounded outward with 1 pixel added on every side. (SkScalerContext_Mac::generateMetrics)
  Synthetic italic is drawn by CoreText with the text matrix skew (-1/4) like Skia.

맥 게임패드 진동. (macOS 만)\n- 원본에 없는 파일이다. 원본은:
Mac gamepad vibration. (macOS only)
- A file not in the original. The original vibrates with the browser's Gamepad.vibrationActuator, and the Rust version on desktop vibrates with gilrs force feedback.
  gilrs's macOS implementation has empty force feedback (is_ff_supported is always false), so only on Mac it vibrates here with Apple GameController and CoreHaptics.
- Builds a CHHapticEngine with GCController.controllers() → controller.haptics (GCDeviceHaptics) → createEngineWithLocality,
  and starts right away a player of a CHHapticPattern made of one continuous event (intensity, sharpness).
  - The heavy motor (strong) goes to the left handle (GCHapticsLocalityLeftHandle) engine, the light motor (weak) to the right handle (GCHapticsLocalityRightHandle) engine.
    A pad that offers neither goes to one GCHapticsLocalityHandles engine, or failing that a GCHapticsLocalityDefault engine, with the larger of the two intensities.
  - Calling again stops the previous vibration and starts a new one. If the intensity or duration is 0 it only stops.
  - One continuous event lasts up to 30 seconds, so longer ones chain 30-second events.
  - Engines are built once per controller and handle position and kept. Engines of controllers gone from the list are dropped.
    If an engine stops for an outside reason (stoppedHandler) or comes back from a server error (resetHandler), it is only marked and restarted on the next vibration.
    If starting or the player fails, the engine is dropped and rebuilt once.
- Pairing gilrs pads with GCControllers: first pairs those with the same name (gilrs's OS name and GCController.vendorName, case-insensitive),
  and pairs the rest by gilrs connection order and the order of GCController.controllers(). (so with one controller it is used even if the names differ)
  GameController does not give the vendor and product IDs through a public API, so they are not matched by ID.
- objc2-game-controller 0.3.2 binds createEngineWithLocality only for iOS, tvOS, visionOS, so on Mac it is called directly with msg_send.
  (Apple's documentation states GCDeviceHaptics is available from macOS 11)
- GameController objects are handled on the main thread. The engine frame (winit event loop) is on the main thread so it calls as is, and skips if called from another thread.
- startWirelessControllerDiscovery is for pairing new wireless pads, so it is not called. Pads already connected are in controllers().
  GCController.shouldMonitorBackgroundEvents is about forwarding input, and gilrs reads the input, so it is left alone.

머티리얼. (원본 experimental/graphics/material:
Material. (the original experimental/graphics/material.js)
- Shader template reference + metallic-roughness PBR parameters/textures, format neutral. Models only apply material instances.
- Builds GL textures from the neutral material description made by importers (factors + image bytes, MaterialDescription).
- FBX specular/gloss maps approximate roughness through the glossiness path.
- The texture unit layout is the same as the original: 0 = base_color, 1 = shadow map only (do not use), 2 ~ 8 = normal / metallicRoughness /
  glossiness / occlusion / emissive / specular / opacity, extra slots are 9 and above.
- Differences from the original:
  - The shader program is shared with the renderer as `Rc<ShaderProgram>`. Model drawables point to materials with `Rc<Material>`. (the original reference semantics)
    set_texture / set_use_alpha_cutout / set_subsurface_factor, which modify the instance in the original, hold their state in Cell internally so they can be called with &self.
  - Image decoding is done on the spot with the image crate (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, ico) instead of the original createImageBitmap (async). So there is no async.
    As in the original on Chrome, the type is not used for decoding and the format is detected from the content. (Chrome createImageBitmap(Blob) also picks the decoder by content, not by the Blob type)
    Like the original, flip_y flips it vertically and is_color_data uploads it as SRGB8_ALPHA8.
  - The Promise of the original loadImageDescription(url) is a load handle (ImageDescriptionLoadHandle), like ImageAsset. load_image_description(engine, asset path, options)
    requests the bytes through the engine's asset loading (asset folder candidates on desktop, fetch from asset_base_url on the web), and once loaded get_image_description builds the description.
    The handle can be awaited directly. (inside an engine task, Material::load_image_description(engine, path, options).await yields the description like the original await)
    mime_type is the content-type of the response, as in the original. (the web fetch response header, None without the header) Desktop has no response, so it is the type detected from the content.
    (Image::sniff_image_mime_type, the image table of WHATWG MIME sniffing plus AVIF, None when unknown) create_image_description(bytes), which takes bytes, is the same as the original.
  - The source (canvas/bitmap) of the original image description is taken as RGBA pixels (ImageSource).

모달 질문 창. (원본과 게임이 부르는 브라우저 window.alert,:
Modal question dialog. (in place of the browser window.alert, window.confirm, window.prompt called by the original and games)
- The original DevTools' Local Storage tab asks for keys and values, and whether to delete, with window.prompt and window.confirm. Games call the same browser functions too.
  The Rust version does the same with the engine functions Engine::alert, Engine::confirm, Engine::prompt.
- The web calls the browser functions as in the original. The browser shows the dialog and halts the page until answered, then the returned value is put in the handle. (finishes on the spot)
- On desktop the engine draws a question dialog over the window, the same as Chrome's tab modal dialog (JavaScriptTabModalDialogViewViews).
  - Position: horizontally centered inside the window, at the top edge. (Chrome centers it horizontally in the tab content area, overlapping the bottom of the toolbar by 3px. A desktop window has no toolbar, so it is the top edge)
  - Title: "This page says" (the title Chrome uses for pages without an origin (file:, data:), a desktop app has no origin) There is no close X.
  - alert has only OK, confirm and prompt have OK and Cancel. The default button is OK. The button order follows Chrome: Windows `[OK][Cancel]`, Mac and Linux `[Cancel][OK]`.
  - The prompt input field is filled with the default value and receives focus with everything selected. Enter is OK, Escape is Cancel.
  - The text (title, OK, Cancel) is chosen by the system language, standing in for the browser UI language. (core/browseruitext.rs)
  - While it is open, scenes and async tasks are not updated, just as JavaScript halts in the original (drawing keeps the frozen screen), and only the dialog receives input. When it closes, pressed keys and buttons are cleared.
    (in the original the dialog takes focus, so keys do not reach the page)
  - The input field receives IME and editing keys through the text input line (core/textinput.rs). Pressing and dragging sets the cursor and selection. Undo and redo work too. (like Chrome's Textfield)
  - Calling several in one frame shows them in order. (in the original JavaScript halts while a dialog is open, so they cannot overlap)
- The original prompt blocks until answered and returns the value. The Rust version cannot block the engine loop, so it returns a ModalDialogHandle, which finishes when answered. (is_finished)
  A function to call after it finishes is set with set_callback. Inside an engine task, await the Promise of Engine::alert_async, confirm_async, prompt_async.
  (while it is open, async tasks also halt as in original JavaScript)

String texture cache.
- The original bakes strings into an offscreen 2D canvas with fillText / strokeText and uses it as a texture. (LRU limit 512)
- Desktop places glyphs with text shaping (textshaping.rs: bidirectional ordering, rustybuzz shaping), rasterizes them (fontdue, skrifa outlines for variable fonts, CoreText for Mac color emoji) and bakes the string into one image.
  The limit and the key fields (mode, paragraph direction, font string, line width, scale, text) are the same as the original.
  The original concatenates the key into a string. Here, to avoid building a string on every lookup, it looks up by the key's hash and compares keys one by one within the same hash.
- Characters are baked in white and the color is multiplied when drawing. (not rebaked when the color changes)
  Color glyphs (emoji) are baked in their own colors on top of the white text. The original also places a canvas filled with fillText in white, so emoji are baked in their own colors and multiplied by the same color when drawing.
  Even when baking as an outline (Stroke), color glyphs are not stroked and are placed in their colors as is. (same as Chrome strokeText)
- The font string is read in the same form as Canvas2D font (CSS font shorthand). Examples: "16px DOSGothic", "bold 24px default", "italic 500 16px default", "12pt 'A B', C, sans-serif"
  Sizes in CSS units other than px (including ex, ch, cap, ic, lh, rem, viewport units), named sizes and calc() are read like the Chrome canvas, and "/line-height" is skipped.
  For a comma-separated name list, each character is looked up starting from the faces of the earlier names. (same as a browser font list, parse_font_string)
- Like the original document.fonts, fonts put several faces (weight, style, character range) under one name. (register_font_face)
  Selection follows the CSS order, and if there is no italic face, synthetic italic (slant 1/4), if there is no bold face, synthetic bold is applied per glyph. (textshaping.rs)
- Characters missing from the name's faces are looked up in the default font, the system font chain, the standard font (desktop, Chrome's -webkit-standard), then the fallback font. (the same role as browser font fallback)
  The desktop system font chain (set_system_font_chain) is the names of the original SYSTEM_FONT_STRING found in the operating system fonts, and when enabled, names in the font string that were not registered are also
  looked up in the operating system fonts. A face is read the first time a character of that weight and style is used. (platform/desktop/systemfont.rs)
  Fallback fonts are chosen by the operating system. (set_system_font_fallback_enabled, asks for a bold face separately when bold is requested) If candidate files are given (add_fallback_font_candidate), they are used first.
  Candidate files are read when used. Emoji presentation characters read candidates with color glyph tables first, other characters read candidates without color glyph tables first. (only the table list is peeked first)
- When a new font face is registered, only strings baked with font strings using that name and containing characters in that face's character range are dropped. (the original invalidateFontFaces)
  As in the original, this happens only when turned on with set_rebake_text_on_font_load. (the engine turns it on with EngineConfiguration.rebake_text_on_font_load, off by default)
  When off, text baked with another font before loading stays until it is pushed out of the cache. Removing faces and reordering drop regardless of this setting.
  Changing the default font or fallback font drops everything.
- The web always bakes and measures with the browser Canvas2D as in the original. (platform/web/systemfont.rs) Registered font bytes are added to document.fonts as FontFace so the browser picks and draws them.
  When the registered font finishes loading (loadingdone), baked text is dropped at the start of the frame. Desktop bakes with the shaping and rasterizing above.
- Text antialiasing (set_text_antialias_enabled, the original setTextAntialiasEnabled): when off, the alpha of baked characters is split into 0 and 255 at a threshold of 128 and the texture is sampled with NEAREST.
  Projects that draw pixel fonts at integer multiples of their design size turn it off. In the original it is a module global value and already baked characters are left as is.
  Here the cache holds it and puts the on/off state in the key, so after changing it the next drawn text is baked that way right away. (rasterize_text does not take it, like the original ShadowText)
- Text measuring (measure_text) does not measure again if the font string and text are the same. (the original measureTextMetrics cache, 2048 entries)
  The original drops the one least recently used each time it overflows. Here, when it overflows it drops the least recently used half at once. (finding one at a time would scan 2048 entries on every measure after overflowing)
  It is cleared when a new font is registered. (the original clears it when a web font finishes loading) measure_text takes &self, so the cache is in a RefCell.
- Loading faces on demand (watch_unresolved_family_characters, take_unresolved_family_characters): the original browser loads a registered FontFace when drawing characters in its character range.
  The Rust version collects characters not in the ranges of registered faces from text measured or baked with watched names, and UIFont takes them out in update and loads the pieces for those characters.
- Measuring without a Graphic (measure_text_without_graphic): the original measures text anywhere with a shared 2D canvas. The Rust version, each time a font is registered,
  publishes the font list (Rc) to a single-thread global and measures with that list. Used when UI layout needs to know the number of text lines before drawing. (UIConfirmWindow)

바닐라엔진 절차 매크로. (원본 vanilla.js 의 실행 중 반사 자:
vanilla-engine procedural macros. (in place of the runtime reflection of the original vanilla.js)
- The original is JavaScript, so at runtime it walks an object's prototype to find get, is, set functions.
  (collectReflectedProperties in ui/uidocument.js, getComponentProperties in misc/devtools.js)
  Rust has no runtime reflection, so like Unreal's UHT (UPROPERTY) and Qt's moc, it generates code at compile time to do the same job.
- Putting `#[reflect]` on a component's impl block gathers the block's `pub fn get_*(&self) -> T`, `pub fn is_*(&self) -> T` and
  their paired `pub fn set_*(&mut self, value)` to build a vanilla::core::reflection::Reflect implementation.
- Putting `#[reflect]` on an impl Component block adds get_reflection and get_reflection_mut,
  and gathers the getters redefined in that block (like isTickNeeded overridden by an original subclass) for the inspector. Both blocks must have it.
- Follows the original rules as is:
  - Getters are argumentless `get*`, `is*` functions. (original `getterFunction.length === 0`) Saved properties are only getters with a `set*` of the same key. (original `"set" + baseName`)
    &mut self getters are getters too. (the original functions make no &self, &mut self distinction) Reflection calls them through the branches that take &mut (get_reflected_value_mut, collect_reflected_getters_mut).
    Rust _mut accessors (like get_uiview_mut) and functions returning &mut are not original getters, so they are excluded.
  - Setters are `set*` taking one value. Setters taking the tree and a value (like set_snap_current_index(tree, slot)) are also recognized,
    and the side holding the tree (UIDocument reading) calls them with set_reflected_value_in_tree as in the original.
  - Getters taking only the tree (like get_target_button(&self, tree)) are original getters too. The original holds neighbor components directly, but the Rust version takes them out of the tree.
    The side holding the tree (the DevTools inspector) calls them with collect_reflected_getters_in_tree. They are not saved properties.
  - The key is the original name with the prefix (get, is) removed. Rust snake_case is turned back into the original camelCase. (get_line_width → getLineWidth → LineWidth)
  - The order is definition order, and on the same key the first one wins.
- Getters of types that cannot be turned into values do not cause compile errors either. Through autoref specialization (autoref specialization) only convertible types are read as values,
  and the rest are skipped in saving as in the original and shown in the inspector as `[kind name]`.
- Put on functions: `#[reflect(skip)]` excludes from reflection. `#[reflect(transient)]` shows in the inspector but excludes from the property list.
  `#[reflect(unsaved)]` keeps it in the property list but excludes it from reflection saving and reading. (properties saveByReflection does not write because the value is an object in the original, ShadowText's FontFace)
  `#[reflect(name = "UIScale")]` sets the original key name. (names that cannot be recovered from snake_case, like acronym words in original names, and getters whose names differ from the original)
  `#[reflect(after = "getFittedFontSize")]` places an impl Component block getter after that original getter in the inspector list. (the order in the original class body, at the front if absent)
- Put on blocks: `#[reflect(base = field)]` chains the reflection of a held value afterwards, like an original superclass.
  `#[reflect(crate = path)]` engine path. (default ::vanilla, inside the engine crate the same path works through extern crate self as vanilla in lib.rs)

반사. (원본 vanilla.js 의 실행 중 반사 자리: ui/uido:
Reflection. (in place of the runtime reflection of the original vanilla.js: collectReflectedProperties and getReflectedProperties of ui/uidocument.js,
  getComponentProperties of misc/devtools.js)
- The original is JavaScript, so at runtime it scans an object's prototype to find get, is, set functions. Rust has no runtime reflection,
  so like Unreal's UHT (UPROPERTY) and Qt's moc, it generates code at compile time to do the same. In Rust the procedural macro `#[reflect]` does that.
  (the macros/ crate, re-exported by the engine as vanilla::reflect) The place of C++ RTTI typeid, dynamic_cast is already AsAny (std::any::Any).
- This module holds the value type (ReflectValue) and trait (Reflect) used by macro-generated code, and the common properties of the original Component base class.
- Usage: put `#[vanilla::reflect]` on both the component's impl block and its impl Component block.
  ```text
    #[vanilla::reflect]
    impl Spin {
        pub fn get_speed(&self) -> f32 { self.speed }
        pub fn set_speed(&mut self, speed: f32) { self.speed = speed; }
    }
    #[vanilla::reflect]
    impl Component for Spin { ... }
  ```
  Then UIDocument writes and reads with the Speed key without registered write and read functions (the original saveByReflection, loadByReflection),
  and the DevTools inspector shows a speed row. (the original getComponentProperties) If only one side has it, a compile error points to where to put it.
- Follows the original rules:
  - Getters are argument-less pub get_*, is_* functions, and saved properties are getters with a set_* of the same name. The key is the original name with the prefix removed. (get_line_width → LineWidth)
  - The order is the definition order and for the same key the first one wins. GizmoVisible, Enable, ComponentType of the original Component base class are appended at the end.
  - Saved values are the types the original saveByReflection picks (number, boolean, text, Color, Vector2, node). Enums that are text in the original (such as TextAlign) are converted to the same text.
- What it does like the original:
  - Getters of the original superclass come along through the prototype chain. The Rust version has no inheritance, so it links the embedded value with #[reflect(base = field)].
    Functions that belong to the superclass in the original but that the Rust version redefines for convenience are excluded with `#[reflect(skip)]` to keep the original order.
    Reading and setting look up separately starting from the most derived type, like the original `component[getterName]`, `component[setterName]`. (RichText gets the getter from Text and has its own setter)
  - Pairs are made by key (baseName) like the original. (if the key of get_target is set to TargetNode, it is not paired with set_target (key Target))
  - Getters redefined in the impl Component block show only those also in the original class (excluding the rest with `#[reflect(skip)]`), and their place in the original class body is matched with #[reflect(after = "...")].
  - Properties left out of saving in the original because their value is an object are kept in the list but left out of saving with `#[reflect(unsaved)]`. (FontFace of ShadowText)
  - When reading, the type is decided by the setter's type. The original decides by the type of the current value, and takes the saved type if there is no current value (null). (the original saveByReflection writes only Color as four numbers,
    and only Vector2 as two numbers) So both engines read the same document the same way.
- What differs from the original:
  - In the original every object is reflected. In the Rust version only types with `#[reflect]` are. Rust has no way to read a method list at runtime, so there is truly no alternative.
    (the same form as Unreal UCLASS, UPROPERTY) Omissions can be found this way: putting it on only one block makes a compile error point to where to put it,
    and omitting both makes UIDocument warn when writing and the DevTools inspector show a "no reflection" row.
  - &mut self getters are called through the branch taking &mut (get_reflected_value_mut, collect_reflected_getters_mut). In the &self branch the value is None.
    Getters that take the tree (such as get_target_button(tree), the original holds the neighboring component directly) are called by the side holding the tree with collect_reflected_getters_in_tree.
    Setters that take the tree (such as set_snap_current_index(tree, index)) are called by the side holding the tree with set_reflected_value_in_tree.
    Setters that take more arguments than the value (such as set_image(image, slice)) are in the property list (paired if a set function exists, like the original) but are not set.
    In place of the original setComponentType, Rust has no setter (the kind is decided by the type), so it is only written. In the original too, reading this key does not change the kind.

- Press / release / cancel / click / long press / mouse over events, and a tint transition that changes color when pressed or hovered.
- A click happens only when pressed and then released inside the button area. (a press that fired a long press swallows the click)
- As in the original, the tint applies to Sprite / UIImageView (cover color) and Paint / Text / UILabel (original color interpolation) of the host node and all descendants.
  Other components of the host node are found as siblings during tick / touch. (NodeTree briefly takes out only the component it is calling)
  In the original, Sprite inherits Paint, so it is also caught by getComponents(Paint). So sprites get the original color interpolation once more after the cover color,
  and the later one wins. To produce the same result, the Rust version also holds sprites (and UIImageView's sprites) twice.
- Differences from the original:
  - Events are `Box<dyn FnMut(&mut UIButton, &mut ComponentContext)>`. Original callbacks take only the button.
    The context is passed along so callbacks can change, create, and delete other nodes. (the bool return of click events was dropped because the original never used it either)
    Received events are stored in `Rc<RefCell>`. Event getters return that Rc, and the caller borrows it with borrow_mut and calls it with the button and the context.
    If the same event is called again while it is being called (like fire_click_events inside the callback), it is skipped because it is already borrowed.
  - The original setInteractable / UIToggleButton.set_is_on gather the color targets and apply the tint on the spot. The Rust version cannot reach the nodes there, so
    it gathers and applies them on the next tick. (tick reapplies the tint every frame, so the visible result is the same)
  - Excluded components are specified by (node, component type) instead of instance: `exclude_component_from_tint::<Paint>`(node_id).
  - setStateEvent (an empty function in the original too) was not ported.
- attach_to_tree turns the host node interactable. Attach with node_tree.add_component(node_id, UIButton::new()).

View manager.
- canvas_native_size:	Logical size of the window interior. (physical pixels / scale)
- canvas_pixel_size:	Actual rendering pixel size of the window interior. (drawing buffer)
- view_native_rect:	The view area actually used. (a sub-area relative to canvas_native_size)
- view_size:			The view size actually used. (size of the coordinate system the scene draws in)
- The original's device_pixel_ratio is the window's scale factor.
- Render scale limit (set_max_render_pixel_ratio): the original immediately recomputes the view area and shrinks the canvas size.
  In the Rust version the platform fits the canvas, so it refits with the limited scale at the start of the next frame. The web shrinks the canvas drawing buffer,
  and desktop draws at the reduced size in the bottom-left of the default framebuffer, then stretches it to the window size. (platform/desktop/renderscaler.rs)
- Safe area insets (get_safe_area_insets, set_safe_area_override) are SafeAreaInsets with named fields like the original { top, right, bottom, left }.
  The address's ?safeArea=top,right,bottom,left corresponds on desktop to the environment variable VANILLA_SAFE_AREA=top,right,bottom,left.
  CSS env(safe-area-inset-*) is read on the web and is 0 on desktop. Chrome desktop is 0 too. (nonzero values only come in on Android, platform/desktop.rs read_safe_area_insets)
  set_safe_area_override takes effect on both.
- get_client_native_size: the whole page size (window.innerWidth, innerHeight) as in the original. Desktop has no page, so it is the logical size of the window interior.
- convert_client_to_view: screen (client) coordinates to view coordinates. The web subtracts the canvas's current position, and on desktop the window's logical coordinates are the client coordinates.

  if not ready yet it wakes itself and checks again the next frame.

Color glyph raster. (color glyphs of emoji fonts to premultiplied RGBA)
- In the original, the browser's Canvas2D draws color glyphs in their own colors. Only the alpha of fillStyle applies, not its color, and strokeText also fills color glyphs in their own colors without stroking an outline.
  The Rust version reads the font's color glyph data directly and draws it. Like Chrome, it does not draw OT-SVG glyphs.
- Bitmaps: extracts and decodes the PNG and premultiplied BGRA of sbix (Apple Color Emoji) and CBDT/CBLC (the Noto Color Emoji bitmap version), and fits them to the font size.
  The strike used is the smallest one at or above the font size among strikes that have the glyph, otherwise the largest. (Apple Color Emoji has glyphs missing from some strikes) Shrinking uses area averaging, enlarging uses interpolation between two points.
  The position is the strike's pixel position value (the offset of the image's bottom left from the pen origin) scaled by the font size ratio.
- Outlines: COLR/CPAL v0 (one outline per layer in one color) and v1 (gradients, transforms, clipping, compositing). Received through ttf-parser's Painter and painted directly.
  Outlines flatten curves into line segments and compute coverage with area accumulation (the same method as font-rs, nonzero winding).
  Paints (solid color, linear (three points), radial between two circles, sweep gradient) are evaluated at pixel centers. Outside the ends of the color line follows Pad, Repeat, Reflect, and colors are blended in straight alpha.
  Compositing does COLR's 28 modes (Porter-Duff and W3C blending) in premultiplied color. The palette is number 0, and the text color (palette index 0xFFFF) is white. (glyphs are baked in white and the color is multiplied when drawing)
  A v1 paint fills the current clip region. Without a clip (v0) it fills the last received outline.

  Both caches discard the least recently used entries first when they exceed 1024. (the rule of the original fromCache; the same rule was added to the original fromHEXCached)

섀도우 맵. (원본 experimental/graphics/shadowm:
Shadow map. (original experimental/graphics/shadowmap.js)
- Real-time directional light shadows, a depth texture (hardware compare sampling, sampler2DShadow) and an orthographic light matrix.
- begin_render() starts the depth pass, and the main pass samples the resulting texture.
- The light matrix snaps to texel units to reduce shadow edge shimmer while moving. When the light points almost straight up or down, the up axis is taken as z so the matrix does not break.
- Construction restores the previous texture and framebuffer bindings. (so building it after models does not leave the depth texture on a texture unit and make drawing INVALID_OPERATION)
- ShadowAtlas: stores point light and spot light shadows as tiles in one depth texture. (original ShadowAtlas, the form of Unity URP's additional light shadow atlas)
  Tile size follows the URP default. Each tile asks for tile_resolution, and if they do not all fit in the atlas, the tile side is halved until they fit. (512 for one point light, 1024 for one spot light)
  The toon shader pushes the receiving position toward the normal by (1 + 3 x (1 - dot(N, L))) tile texels at that distance before comparing. (larger for surfaces at a grazing angle to the light, prevents shadow acne)
- Texel snapping rounds 0.5 up, like the original Math.round. (Rust round goes away from zero, so it differs for negative numbers)
- The original default resolution argument 2048 is DEFAULT_SHADOWMAP_RESOLUTION. (Rust has no default arguments)

세이브 기록을 글로 두는 곳.\n- 한 키에 쓰기는 다 되거나 안 되거나:
Where save records are kept as text.
- Writing to one key must either fully succeed or not happen at all. (localStorage.setItem, writing a temporary file then renaming) SaveGameManager alternates between two keys on top of that.
세이브 슬롯 관리. (원본 src/experimental/savegame:
Save slot manager. (the original src/experimental/savegame/savegamemanager.js)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Each slot (slot) holds one piece of JSON data and a header (name, save time, version, preview image, size, game-defined metadata).
- Record form: `"VSAVE1 <CRC-32 as 8 hex digits>\n<header JSON>\n<data JSON>"`. The CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, the same polynomial as zlib) is computed over the UTF-8 from the second line to the end.
  Same form as the original (JS), so the two engines read each other's saves. (when the storage uses the same keys)
- Atomic writes: each slot alternates between two keys (`<namespace>.slot.<slot>.0` and `.1`). A new record goes to the key not holding the previous record, with the sequence number raised by one,
  and reading picks the one with the largest sequence number among those whose checksum matches. If writing is cut off (the app dies, storage is full) or a record is corrupted, the previous save remains.
  The storage makes writing one key either fully succeed or not happen at all. (web localStorage.setItem; the desktop LocalStorage writes to a temporary file, then renames it into place)
- Migration: the data records its version (version), and when reading a version lower than the current one, functions registered with add_migration are called in turn for each version. (v → v + 1)
  Saves of a version higher than the current one (written by a newer game version) are not read.
- Autosave: register the slot, interval and a function giving the data with set_autosave, and call update every frame.
- Export and import: export_slot gives JSON text containing the records as is, and import_slot checks the checksum and can import into another slot too.
- Cloud: plugging in a SaveCloudProvider with set_cloud_provider uploads on every save, and pull_from_cloud fetches and imports newer ones. (interface only)
세이브 슬롯. (원본 src/experimental/savegame/)\:
Save slots. (the original src/experimental/savegame/)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- SaveGameManager: multiple slots (name, save time, version, preview image location, size, metadata per slot), migration (a chain of functions per version),
  atomic writes (alternating two keys with sequence numbers), detecting corrupt records (CRC-32), autosave, export and import (JSON), and a cloud plug point (SaveCloudProvider, interface only).
- The default storage is LocalSaveStorage on top of the engine LocalStorage. (web localStorage, desktop localstorage.json, the same keys and record form as the original)
  It can be swapped by implementing SaveStorage. (MemorySaveStorage is memory only)
- Unity has no slot system in the engine (key values of PlayerPrefs), and Unreal has USaveGame and UGameplayStatics::SaveGameToSlot (slot name, user index).
  In both engines, migration, double writes, checksums, autosave and export are left for the game to build, so here the engine takes them on.

세이브 저장소와 클라우드 자리. (원본 src/experimental/s:
Save storage and cloud plug point. (the original src/experimental/savegame/savestorage.js)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- SaveStorage: where save records are kept as text. The default is LocalSaveStorage on top of the engine LocalStorage.
  (web localStorage, localstorage.json in the desktop app folder. For the desktop file, LocalStorage writes to a temporary file, then renames it into place)
- MemorySaveStorage: storage kept only in memory. (tests, trial versions that do not save)
- SaveCloudProvider: plug point for cloud saves (such as Steam Cloud). The engine only provides the interface, and games or platform bundles implement it.

Shader sprite component.
- A port of the original effect/shadersprite.js. Same as Sprite but applies fragment shader effects (dissolve / flash / outline / hologram / wave / mosaic / glitch / shine / silhouette / grayscale / hue rotation / wipe / iris / chromatic aberration).
- The effect time runs by itself (tick), and the progress is pushed in by tweens / timelines.
- Effect names, default parameters, default colors and GLSL bodies are carried over from the original table as they are. Shaders are GLSL ES 3.00, and on desktop ShaderProgram changes only the header to #version 330 core.
- Drawing: if there is an effect, it swaps in the effect program with Graphic.set_shader_program_override, uploads the effect uniforms, and then follows the Sprite output path as is.
  While swapped in, it is not batched. (a ShaderSprite without an effect is batched together with Sprites)
- Usage:
  ```text
    let shader_sprite = node.add_component(ShaderSprite::create_with_image(image));
    shader_sprite.set_effect(ShaderSpriteEffect::Dissolve);
    shader_sprite.set_effect_progress(0.5);
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - The original inherits from Sprite. The Rust version contains a Sprite and lets Sprite functions (set_image, set_image_rect, set_color ...) be called as is through Deref / DerefMut.
    So it cannot be found with `get_component::<Sprite>()`, only with `get_component::<ShaderSprite>()`.
  - Effects are the ShaderSpriteEffect enum instead of strings. (the original string names via get_name / from_name)
  - The effect program cache is held by Graphic.resolve_shader_program instead of the original's per-context WeakMap.
  - If creating a program fails, the original throws an exception, and the Rust version reports it once and draws as a Sprite without the effect.

소리 표로 다루는 배경음악과 효과음. (vanilla.js core/so:
Background music and sound effects handled by a sound table. (SoundSystem of vanilla.js core/soundsystem.js)
- Uses AudioManager and AudioAsset. Does not synthesize sound, only plays files.
- Each row of the sound table is SoundRow { id, paths, volume, minimum_interval, is_music, maximum_voices, pitch_variation, play_seconds, fade_out_seconds }.
  paths: a group of multiple recordings of the same sound. Each time it plays, one of the loaded ones is picked, never the same as the one just before.
  minimum_interval: interval before the same sound can play again. (seconds, so it does not pile up and get noisy)
  maximum_voices: number of copies of the same sound that can play at once. (over that, the oldest is cut, None means up to the total sound effect count, 0 means one as in the original)
  pitch_variation: ratio by which the pitch wobbles each time it plays. (0.05 means ±5%)
  play_seconds, fade_out_seconds: plays only the first play_seconds seconds of a sound effect and fades it out over fade_out_seconds seconds. (0 means to the end)
- Volume: background music = music volume × music ratio × sound volume, sound effect = effect volume × sound volume × volume at the call.
  Music and effect volumes are applied on buses (AudioBus from get_music_bus, get_effect_bus), and follow changes with a 0.05 second time constant. (the original setTargetAtTime)
  Buses are created after the first press. (None before that) Players created from a bus (AudioBus::create_audio_player) also follow the set volume and mute.
- Background music remembers what was requested (get_music_id) and plays it then if it is not loaded yet or before the first press. ("" stops it)
  It can crossfade (fade_seconds), and remembers where each sound stopped so it can resume. (is_resumed) It does not play if the first file failed to load.
- Mute takes priority over the set volume. If any of the following holds, no sound is made.
  External mute (set_external_mute_provider, platform SDK or ads), user mute (set_user_muted), the page being hidden (another tab, app switch),
  the window losing focus (blur) on touch-primary devices. On iPhone the page-hidden notification arrives after the app goes down, so audio freezes without stopping and
  the last sound fragment repeats, but the focus-lost notification comes before that. Desktop (mouse) also loses focus when clicking outside the canvas, so it does not follow this.
  It is released when focus returns, the screen is pressed, or the page becomes visible again.
- While muted, the AudioContext is suspended too. (woken when released) On iPhone, if an app switch or an interstitial ad takes over a running AudioContext, waking it on return
  makes no sound, so it suspends itself beforehand. If it still does not run after being released, it tries waking it again every 0.5 seconds.
- If allowed (set_autoplay_allowed_provider, allowed if not given), it tries waking once on the first update even before a press. If blocked, the engine wakes it on the first press.
  Before the first press (user gesture) or when the AudioContext is not running, sound effects are not played. (so sounds called while suspended do not all play at once on wake)
- Sound files are loaded in the background so they do not block play. (on the web they play once decoding finishes) Sounds that fail to load simply do not play.
- Time: the same-sound interval and the re-wake interval use the wall clock (web_time::Instant) like the original performance.now(), and volume following, fade out,
  and the music's stopped position use the AudioContext clock (AudioManager::get_context_time) as in the original.
- Shared sound: set_sound_system, read_sound_system. (the original module variable, one per thread)
- Differences from the original:
  - It takes the engine instead of AudioManager at creation. The original attaches listeners to document and window, but the Rust version receives them through the engine's page events (PageEvent).
    The AudioContext is suspended or woken right where the event arrives (the sound stops immediately), and cutting sound effects happens on the next update.
  - load_sounds, load_sound take the engine to resolve paths relative to the asset folder. (in the original the browser resolves them against the page address) Desktop reads them on the spot.
    load_sounds returns an awaitable SoundLoadHandle as in the original. (waits until all requested sounds are loaded or fail, same as wait_for_load().await)
  - Volume changes and fade out are left to the sound device as in the original, with GainNode AudioParam automation (value assignment, setValueAtTime, linearRampToValueAtTime, setTargetAtTime,
    cancelScheduledValues) and source.stop(when). On the web they are applied to WebAudio, on desktop to the mixer (same math as Chromium).
    The original { source, gainNode } is one AudioPlayer created from a bus, and finished sounds (the original onended) are removed from the list in update.
    As in the original, values set with the bus's set_volume, mute last until SoundSystem applies the volume again.
  - Picking from a group and wobbling the pitch use the engine's math::random (seeded with the time on first use) in place of the original Math.random.
  - add_sound_asset (adding a sound not loaded from a file) and get_effect_voice_count were made in the Rust version first. (also added to the original under the same names)

스냅 스크롤 뷰. (원본 ui/uisnapscrollview.js 의 U:
Snap scroll view. (UISnapScrollView of the original ui/uisnapscrollview.js)
- On drag release, slides so that the center of one content child (item) lands at the center of the visible area. Items may differ in size.
- Horizontal snap: set_horizontal(true), set_vertical(false) (default). Vertical snap: set_horizontal(false), set_vertical(true).
- One drag moves at most one slot. It moves on if the drag distance is at least the set_page_change_threshold ratio (default 0.35) of the next item's size.
  While dragging, the offset does not go beyond the current slot ±1 slot range.
- page_to(node_tree, index, smooth): moves to the given slot. If smooth, slides with 0.3 seconds cubic.out, otherwise moves right away.
- The original inherits UIScrollView. The Rust version embeds UIScrollView (scroll_view field) and passes through touch, wheel, drawing, and attaching.
  Scroll view settings are made on the embedded view with get_scroll_view_mut. Commonly used ones (content size, offset, axes) are also on this widget.
  Attach with node_tree.add_component(node_id, UISnapScrollView::new()). (the embedded view creates the content node, Mask, and interactable)
- Differences from the original:
  - Functions that change the slot (page_to, set_snap_current_index, play_snap_tween, etc.) need to read content children, so they take the tree.
    Scene code calls them with node_tree.`with_component_mut::<UISnapScrollView, _>`(snap_id, |snap_view, tree| snap_view.page_to(tree, 2, true)).
  - Instead of the original Tween object, the snap slide does the same calculation (0.3 seconds, cubic.out, first step on the tick it is made) inside this widget.
    (the original tween's update callback calls the scroll view itself, but a Rust tween callback takes only the tree and cannot reach this widget, which is taken out during tick)
  - While sliding, the content node is moved right away within that tick. (so it does not lag a frame, since the embedded view applies on the next tick)
  - set_snap_to_nearest, set_velocity_threshold only hold values as in the original. (the original play_snap_tween does not read them either)
  - In the original, the snap view is also a UIScrollView, so TouchRecognizer, UIScrollBar, UIListView recognize it as is.
    In the Rust version, TouchRecognizer and UIListView recognize it through find_scroll_view. UIScrollBar looks only for the UIScrollView component, so
    a scroll bar cannot be attached to a snap view. (setShows...ScrollBar only puts the value into the embedded view)

스킨드 모델. (원본 experimental/graphics/skinne:
Skinned model. (the original experimental/graphics/skinnedmodel.js)
- Model instance, mesh/bone/skin/material/animation data + pose state. Rendering is handled by SkinnedModelRenderer.
- Interprets GLB (binary glTF) and binary FBX into a common neutral schema (MeshDescription + MaterialDescription) and builds GL resources.
  (importers only parse → neutral schema → shared GL upload upload_meshes_and_materials)
- Static meshes without a skin use a synthetic skin (1 joint), and morph targets are uploaded as float textures, so they draw through the same skinning path.
- Supports animation cross-fades, joint rotation offsets (procedural pose adjustment) and morph weights (glTF weights / code) like the original.
- Differences from the original:
  - The original is async and fetches URLs (loadFromUrl, loadFromBytes for bytes). The byte functions of the Rust version
    load_from_bytes / load_from_fbx_bytes / add_animations_from_fbx_bytes finish on the spot.
    The URL functions load_from_url / load_from_fbx_url, like ImageAsset, use the engine's asset loading (asset folder candidates on desktop, fetch from asset_base_url on the web)
    to request the bytes and return a load handle (SkinnedModelLoadHandle). Once loaded, the handle's create_model(gl, renderer) builds the model. (the form without await)
    The original await SkinnedModel.loadFromUrl(gl, url, renderer) becomes load_from_url_async(engine, path, renderer).await inside an engine task. (load_from_fbx_url_async for fbx)
    Once loaded, the model is built with the GL of the engine polling the task. (the renderer only shares its shader program at the call and is not borrowed)
    add_animations_from_fbx_url requests the load and returns an awaitable AnimationLoadHandle. Like the original, the clips are already added when await finishes.
    (the clip list is shared with the handle, and once loaded, whichever comes first among the awaiting future, the next update or play_animation adds them. They are added in load order like the original)
  - Functions that use GL take gl. update(delta_time) does not use GL. Step 6 of the original update (uploading changed morph targets) is
    done instead by the renderer's draw / draw_depth / draw_wireframe through upload_pending_morph_targets. (that is why the draw functions take a &mut model)
    Thanks to this, update can be called in the scene's tick.
  - The original node / drawable / skin / clip objects are the SkinnedModelNode / Drawable / Skin / AnimationClip structs.
    A drawable's material is `Rc<Material>`. Clips are referred to by index, and sample_animation also takes a clip index.
    upload_wireframe_indices / upload_morph_targets take a drawable index instead of the original drawable object. (a drawable cannot be passed while the model is borrowed as &mut)
  - A drawable's mesh_description has empty morph_targets because the morph targets were moved to morph_target_list. (the large delta arrays are not held twice)
  - Like the original, node matrix, CUBICSPLINE interpolation and primitive mode are ignored. Like the original, FBX draws only meshes with a skin attached.
  - Materials deleted by destroy: the original deletes the ones this model built during upload. The Rust version deletes only those among them not held elsewhere with Rc.
    (because reference counts can be checked, JavaScript has no reference counts)
