스프라이트 아틀라스. (vanilla.js resource/spritea:
Sprite atlas. (SpriteAtlas of vanilla.js resource/spriteatlas.js)
- Takes out images gathered on a few page images by name. Sprites using the same page image are batched by the engine and drawn at once.
- The JSON formats read are the same two as the original.
  1. Made by tools/atlas.cjs. { images: { "name.png": { x, y, width, height, page } }, meta: { imageFileName, pages: [{ imageFileName }] } }
     Page 0 if page is missing, a single meta.imageFileName if meta.pages is missing.
  2. Page paths and a [page, x, y, width, height] table. { pagePaths: `["path"]`, frames: { "name": [page, x, y, width, height] } }
- Image names can also be found by the name without the extension. ("icon-close.png" can be found as both "icon-close" and "icon-close.png")
- If a page path has no slash (/), it is read relative to the folder holding the JSON, otherwise as written. (if it starts with "./", that "./" is dropped and it is relative to the asset folder)
- Differences from the original:
  In the original load is async, waiting for the JSON and then receiving the page images. The Rust version only makes requests like assets, and update requests the page images once it sees the JSON has arrived.
  load, load_data return a SpriteAtlasLoadHandle that can be awaited as in the original. The handle shares the loading state and does not borrow the atlas, so
  an atlas held by a scene is also waited on with scene_context.with(|scene, engine| scene.atlas.load(engine, path)).await. (calls update every frame while waiting)
  On desktop it is read on the spot, so everything is read when load finishes. On web the JSON and page images arrive in turn, so call update in tick until is_loaded becomes true,
  and set frames after that. (to have the scene hand it off and wait, use track_json_asset for the JSON, and update requests the page images once it arrives)
  The original list of atlases to search (add_search_atlas, find_frame, apply_search_frame) is one list per thread, and atlases are added as `Rc<RefCell<SpriteAtlas>>` so they can be shared.
  find_frame returns a copy of the frame (a Frame is an image Rc and an area, so it is cheap) instead of a borrowed one. There is also find_frame_in_order, which searches a given list.
  get_page_images is a list of loaded page images (Image) instead of the original list of HTMLImageElement.

- Differences from the original:
  - The original moves the thumb node inside draw. The Rust version cannot change the tree while drawing, so it moves it in tick. (the thumb node is kept as a child of the host)

    Received events are stored in `Rc<RefCell>`. get_value_changed_event returns that Rc, and the caller borrows it with borrow_mut and calls it.

시드 난수 생성기. (원본 base/seededrandom.js, mul:
Seeded random number generator. (the original base/seededrandom.js, mulberry32)
- Deterministic random numbers that always produce the same sequence from the same seed. Used where reproducibility matters, such as stage generation, replays and versus sync.
- With the same seed as the original, the same sequence comes out bit for bit. The original's >>> 0, Math.imul and ^ are 32-bit integer operations, so
  they were ported as is with u32 wrapping_add / wrapping_mul / ^. (the intermediate mixed + imul(...) addition also becomes modulo 2^32 through ToInt32, so
  it equals wrapping_add) next_value is f64 as in the original. (it is a 32-bit value divided by 2^32, so f32 would blur the last digits)
- The seed and state are u32. The original (seed >>> 0) || 1 is the u32 seed as is, 1 if 0.
  Where the original used a negative number or one above 2^32 as a seed, converting that number to u32 and passing it gives the same sequence. (as u32 is the same as ToUint32)
- next_range takes f32 and returns f32, but computes in f64 like the original and narrows to f32 only once at the end.
  next_int is i32 and computes in f64 like the original.
- pick returns `Option<&T>` (the original undefined is None), and shuffle shuffles a slice in place. (the original returns the same array)
- In the original, from_date reads the local year, month and day of a Date. Rust std has no local time, so it takes the year, month (1 ~ 12) and day.

Scene.
- The original inherits the Scene class and overrides create / tick / draw.
- The Rust version implements the Scene trait and keeps the common scene state (node tree, touch target) in SceneBase.
- Nodes are held by SceneBase's NodeTree, and game code points to them with NodeId handles. (get_node_tree_mut().create_child(...))
  In place of the original super.tick() / super.draw(), call get_scene_base_mut().tick() / .draw().
- The original GameScene's pre_draw (filling the whole canvas with the background color and applying the view coordinate system) moved to SceneBase::draw_scene_background.
- Like the original, the scene holds tweens in a list (start_tween), runs them on tick after nodes → touch, and removes finished ones.
  The original points to them by tween object, but the Rust version takes ownership of the tween and returns a TweenId. (stop_tween(tween_id))
- The original SceneManager.unloadScene(scene) points by scene object. In the Rust version the engine holds the scenes, so it points by the SceneId returned from load_scene or
  by the common scene state (&SceneBase, by scene as in the original). A scene knows its own handle with get_scene_base().get_scene_id().
- When unloading, like the original it calls finalize then unload, and the Rust version additionally calls destroy right before dropping the scene.
- In place of the original async load(engine): in create, hand the loading work to Engine::spawn_scene_task and entrust it to the scene with track_task.
  Inside the task, await assets as in the original and touch the scene and engine inside SceneContext::with. initialize is called only after all entrusted tasks and assets finish.
  The synchronous form of entrusting asset handles with track_asset still works. (the two can be mixed)
  In place of the original await unload(engine): the scene stays in the list receiving tick, draw until the tasks entrusted in unload (track_task) finish, then leaves the list.
  If that scene's tasks still remain after that, the scene value lives until they all finish, like the original's Promise chain (it receives no tick, draw), and a scene unloaded while loading
  receives initialize once loading finishes, like the original SceneManager.loadScene. When everything is done, the engine calls destroy and drops it.
- What the original Scene.load does to fit the root to the view size (position 0, top-left pivot, content size is the view size) is done by the engine right after create.
  Like the original SceneManager.loadScene, after all entrusted assets finish it keeps showing the loading screen (draw_on_load) for at least 0.3 seconds more, then calls initialize.
- The scene's touch hooks (touch_press, touch_move, touch_release, touch_cancel, touch_wheel) are called by the engine after tick, in the original Scene.tickTouch order.
  SceneBase.tick also passes them to the frontmost interactable node regardless of the scene type. (same as the original Scene.tickTouch passing them to the scene's TouchRaycaster)
- Unlike the original, the page restore hooks and touch hooks take the engine. (there is no global engine)

- The exit time (exit_time) is the normalized time of the leaving state. When set, the transition can only happen on the update that passes that time.
  For a looping state, an exit time below 1 is checked every cycle (0.5 also at 1.5, 2.5). Otherwise it is checked only once.
- All conditions must hold. A transition with neither an exit time nor conditions is not used.
- If the blend time (duration, seconds) is above 0, both states run together for that time while the weight moves linearly. (Crossfade)
- A transition from any state that leads to the current state is taken only when can_transition_to_self is true. (Default true, the state restarts from the beginning)
Animation transition. (a link between states that runs the target state when the condition is met. States are indices into the Animator state list)

  The original addTask (a hand-made fetch) corresponds to add_load_handle. A load handle requested directly and added is counted in the progress too.

    The handle was already requested before being added, so it cannot be deferred until its turn as in the original, and it is in flight from when it is added.
  The in-flight count is, as in the original, those picked up and started but not yet finished. (images until decoded, sounds until decoded. The original worker waits for that too) Concurrency is counted with this too.

액션. (차례로 스텝을 실행하는 스크립트 꼴 연출)\n- 원본 anima:
Action. (script-style sequencing that runs steps in order)
- A port of the original animation/action.js. Stack wait / condition / call / repeat / forever / loop steps,
  and after start, calling step every frame runs them in order.
- Usage:
  ```text
    let mut action: Action<WorldNode> = Action::new()
        .wait(1.0, ActionCallbacks::new().updated(|progress, node: &mut WorldNode| node.set_local_opacity(progress)))
        .condition(|node: &WorldNode| node.is_active(), ActionConditionCallbacks::new())
        .call(|node: &mut WorldNode| node.set_local_scale(Vector2::create(2.0, 2.0)))
        .repeat(3, Action::new().wait(0.5, ActionCallbacks::new()))
        .forever(Action::new().wait(2.0, ActionCallbacks::new()));
    action.start(&mut node_tree[node_id]);
    // Every frame:
    action.step(&mut node_tree[node_id], time_delta);
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - The original holds the target from start(target) and passes it to the callbacks on every step. Rust cannot hold a borrowed target, so
    start and step take the target (&mut T) and pass it to the callbacks. So get_target and start()'s "previous target when none is given" do not exist.
    T defaults to WorldNode; to handle several nodes or game state, use that as T.
  - The callback objects ({ started, updated, completed }) are ActionCallbacks for wait steps (updated takes (progress, target)),
    and ActionConditionCallbacks for condition steps (updated takes (target)). The original uses one object shape with only the argument count differing,
    but Rust has to fix the callback argument types as types, so they are split in two.
  - loop is a Rust keyword, so it is called as r#loop. (same as Tween's r#in)
  - When call steps follow one another, the original moves on recursively and the Rust version with a loop. (same result)
- The condition function takes the target as in the original (&T in Rust). wait ends with progress 1 if duration is 0 or less.
  repeat moves on without running if the count is 0. (same as the original)

- Differences from the original:
  - The original holds the target from start(target) and passes it to the callbacks on every step. Rust cannot hold a borrowed target, so
    start and step take the target (&mut T) and pass it to the callbacks. So get_target and start()'s "previous target when none is given" do not exist.
    T defaults to WorldNode; to handle several nodes or game state, use that as T.
  - The callback objects ({ started, updated, completed }) are ActionCallbacks for wait steps (updated takes (progress, target)),
    and ActionConditionCallbacks for condition steps (updated takes (target)). The original uses one object shape with only the argument count differing,
    but Rust has to fix the callback argument types as types, so they are split in two.
  - loop is a Rust keyword, so it is called as r#loop. (same as Tween's r#in)
  - When call steps follow one another, the original moves on recursively and the Rust version with a loop. (same result)
- The condition function takes the target as in the original (&T in Rust). wait ends with progress 1 if duration is 0 or less.
  repeat moves on without running if the count is 0. (same as the original)

- Nodes take the place of the original DOM elements. The container is a node (get_container), and content is attached as its children with node_tree.add_child. (original appendChild)
  Desktop has no global document, so functions that create and change nodes take a NodeTree. The length unit is node coordinates, in place of the original CSS pixels.
  ```text
    let main_pane = Pane::new(node_tree, PaneOptions { direction: PaneDirection::Horizontal, ..Default::default() });
    let left_pane = Pane::new(node_tree, PaneOptions { size: PaneSize::Fixed(240.0), min_size: 170.0, ..Default::default() });
    main_pane.add_pane(node_tree, &left_pane);
    let panel_id = PaneStyle::create(node_tree, "div", "panel", &PaneStyleOptions::default());
    node_tree.add_child(left_pane.get_container(), panel_id);
    main_pane.attach_to(node_tree, root_id);
  ```
- Like the original, the container paints its background with COLOR_BACKGROUND and clips overflowing children. (overflow: hidden, Mask)
- Like the original, a resizer is 5 thick if draggable and otherwise a line of 1, painted with COLOR_RESIZER, and with COLOR_RESIZER_HOVER while hovered or dragged.
  Pressing and dragging keeps the gap between the grabbed point and the boundary, changes the fixed size of the previous or next child, and lays out again from the root. The cursor is col-resize, row-resize while hovered or dragged.
- A root pane given to attach_to lays out again when the parent node size changes. (original window resize listener and refresh on the next frame)
- PaneStyle::create builds nodes shaped like the original presets. (PaneElement component)
  Common: placed at the top left filling the parent size (position absolute, 100%), font 13px sans-serif, text color COLOR_TEXT.
  panel: background COLOR_PANEL, padding 10. toolbar: background COLOR_TOOLBAR, bottom border 1px COLOR_BORDER, gathered horizontally in the center 10 apart (flex).

Engine.

  In the Rust version the platform layer (crate::platform) handles the window, GL context, input events and presenting the screen,
  and EngineRunner here runs only the scenes and frame flow without knowing the platform. (desktop: platform/desktop.rs, web: platform/web.rs)
- Scenes are passed &mut Engine. Scenes take the managers (time, view, input) from it. (in place of the original Engine.getEngine())
- The Graphic is handed over through attach_graphic after the platform creates the GL context, and passed separately to the scene's draw family.
- As in the original, the audio manager is created and held at construction. The AudioContext (sound device) is created on first use. There is no per-frame audio work.
  On the web the platform calls resume_on_user_gesture on click / touchstart / keydown, and resume on focus / visibilitychange.
- The original SceneManager.getAllLoadedScenes is get_all_loaded_scenes, which returns handles (SceneId) instead of scene objects. (while each scene runs with &mut Engine, other scenes cannot be borrowed)
- As in the original, loading a scene fits the root to the view size (right after create), and even after the tracked assets have all finished, shows the loading screen 0.3 seconds longer and calls initialize.
- Text input focus (is_text_input_focused) looks at the document focus as in the original, and desktop, which has no document, looks at the focus of the engine input field.
- Unloading a single scene (unload_scene) stands in for the original SceneManager.unloadScene. The original refers to it by the scene object, the Rust version by the SceneId returned by load_scene,
  and like unload_all_scenes it unloads after the current frame ends. A scene not yet created (loaded in the same frame) is removed without calling create or destroy.
- Page events (PageEvent): in the original each module attaches listeners to document / window. In the Rust version the platform notifies the engine,
  and the engine passes it on the spot to the listeners received through add_page_event_listener. (SoundSystem receives occlusion and focus through this)
  Web: visibilitychange (Hidden, Visible), blur (Blurred), focus (Focused), pointerdown (PointerDown).
  Desktop: window occlusion (Occluded, reported by macOS and X11), minimization (how Windows reports it), app suspension (mobile) and Wayland frame callbacks not arriving for more than 3 seconds are Hidden; also focus, and mouse button and finger presses.

  Web: visible of visibilitychange → on_page_visibility_restored, document resume and pageshow (persisted) → on_page_process_restored.
  pageshow does the same recovery as resume. (the original called the undefined dispatchPageProcessRestored and threw, which was fixed the same way in the original too)
  Desktop: on_page_visibility_restored when window occlusion ends, on_page_process_restored when the app is resumed after being suspended.
  (winit on Windows, Mac and Linux does not send suspended, so on_page_process_restored is not called on desktop)
- async/await: the engine contains a single-threaded executor (core/task.rs). spawn_task and spawn_scene_task, like original async functions, run at the call site

  also have a form that can be awaited. (load_scene_async, unload_scene_async, unload_all_scenes_async, read_clipboard_text_async, request_frame_capture_async,
  and alert_async, confirm_async, prompt_async for the original window. While a question dialog is open, tasks are not polled either, as in original JavaScript)
- Unloading a scene calls finalize and unload like the original SceneManager.unloadScene, and waits for the tasks unload tracked with track_task to finish.
  (meanwhile it stays in the list and receives tick and draw, as in the original) When done it is removed from the list, and if the scene still has tasks, like the original Promise chain
  the scene value is kept alive until they all finish. (it receives no tick or draw, and SceneContext::with gives that scene) A scene unloaded while loading, like the original loadScene,
  still receives initialize once loading finishes. When everything is done, destroy is called and it is dropped.

6. Stats output (optional) → clear one-shot input flags (including finishing the text input line) → flush batches → (screen capture for verification)

- The Graphic is handed over through attach_graphic after the platform creates the GL context, and passed separately to the scene's draw family.
- As in the original, the audio manager is created and held at construction. The AudioContext (sound device) is created on first use. There is no per-frame audio work.
  On the web the platform calls resume_on_user_gesture on click / touchstart / keydown, and resume on focus / visibilitychange.
- The original SceneManager.getAllLoadedScenes is get_all_loaded_scenes, which returns handles (SceneId) instead of scene objects. (while each scene runs with &mut Engine, other scenes cannot be borrowed)
- As in the original, loading a scene fits the root to the view size (right after create), and even after the tracked assets have all finished, shows the loading screen 0.3 seconds longer and calls initialize.
- Text input focus (is_text_input_focused) looks at the document focus as in the original, and desktop, which has no document, looks at the focus of the engine input field.
- Unloading a single scene (unload_scene) stands in for the original SceneManager.unloadScene. The original refers to it by the scene object, the Rust version by the SceneId returned by load_scene,
  and like unload_all_scenes it unloads after the current frame ends. A scene not yet created (loaded in the same frame) is removed without calling create or destroy.
- Page events (PageEvent): in the original each module attaches listeners to document / window. In the Rust version the platform notifies the engine,
  and the engine passes it on the spot to the listeners received through add_page_event_listener. (SoundSystem receives occlusion and focus through this)
  Web: visibilitychange (Hidden, Visible), blur (Blurred), focus (Focused), pointerdown (PointerDown).
  Desktop: window occlusion (Occluded, winit reports it only on Mac and X11, it does not come on Windows and Wayland), focus, mouse button and finger presses.
- Page restore hooks: as in the original setupAllDocumentEvents, wakes the sound again, clears input, then calls each scene.
  Web: visible of visibilitychange → on_page_visibility_restored, document resume and pageshow (persisted) → on_page_process_restored.
  pageshow does the same recovery as resume. (the original called the undefined dispatchPageProcessRestored and threw, which was fixed the same way in the original too)
  Desktop: on_page_visibility_restored when window occlusion ends, on_page_process_restored when the app is resumed after being suspended.
  (winit on Windows, Mac and Linux does not send suspended, so on_page_process_restored is not called on desktop)
- async/await: the engine contains a single-threaded executor (core/task.rs). spawn_task and spawn_scene_task, like original async functions, run at the call site
  up to the first await, and the remaining tasks are polled once per frame before the scenes' tick, only those that were woken. Engine functions that return a Promise in the original
  also have a form that can be awaited. (load_scene_async, unload_scene_async, unload_all_scenes_async, read_clipboard_text_async, request_frame_capture_async,
  and alert_async, confirm_async, prompt_async for the original window. While a question dialog is open, tasks are not polled either, as in original JavaScript)
- Unloading a scene calls finalize and unload like the original SceneManager.unloadScene, and waits for the tasks unload tracked with track_task to finish.
  (meanwhile it stays in the list and receives tick and draw, as in the original) When done it is removed from the list, and if the scene still has tasks, like the original Promise chain
  the scene value is kept alive until they all finish. (it receives no tick or draw, and SceneContext::with gives that scene) A scene unloaded while loading, like the original loadScene,
  still receives initialize once loading finishes. When everything is done, destroy is called and it is dropped.

Every frame (update_engine):
1. graphic.apply_settings()      # viewport/projection update + state reset + clear screen
2. time_manager.update()         # compute time_delta
3. input_manager.tick()
4. Poll woken tasks (begin_poll_frame, poll_woken_tasks and unload finishing until the woken queue is empty)
5. For each scene tick → pre_draw → draw → post_draw (→ draw_gizmos)
6. Stats output (optional) → clear one-shot input flags (including finishing the text input line) → flush batches → (screen capture for verification)
The platform presents the screen after update_engine.

Audio manager.
- The original core/audiomanager.js. Holds the shared AudioContext and handles AudioPlayer creation.
- The backend fills the AudioContext slot. (platform/audio)
  Desktop: the engine mixer on top of cpal output (platform/audio/mixer.rs, same math as Chrome WebAudio). Opens the sound device on first use. When suspended (SoundSystem mute) the sound and the clock stop in place, as in the original.
  Web: a WebAudio AudioContext, same as the original. Created after a user gesture as in the original, and on iOS the clock is checked after resuming.
- As in the original, the AudioContext is created lazily. resume_context() does nothing before a user gesture,
  while create_audio_player() creates it (reluctantly) even before a user gesture.

Web text input. (hidden DOM <input> → engine text input queue, DOM context menu, canvas mode keys, clipboard)
- A port of the DOM side of the original UIInputField. In the original each field creates its own <input> and attaches listeners.
  In the Rust version fields post their state (position, value, selection, focus) to the engine every frame, and here one hidden <input> is matched to each attached DOM input field.
  - The DOM owns the value and selection. input / compositionstart / compositionupdate / compositionend / Enter keydown / focus / blur are
    put into the text input queue with that field id (replaceValue, composition, focus), and native moves like arrows are put in by polling the selection every frame. (the original tick)
  - When the field side changes the value or cursor (set_text, pressed position, cut), the state's value_revision increases and it is written back to the <input> here. (deferred during composition)
  - iOS shows the keyboard only if focus() is called inside a user gesture. As in the original, synchronous handlers are attached to canvas touchstart / mousedown (touchend if set),
    which check against the previous frame's field positions and focus / blur on the spot.
  - The right-button context menu is a DOM menu shaped like the original's. Items are put into that field as cut / copy keys or text to paste.
  - Fields with use_dominput off convert window keydown into editing keys and characters, like the original canvas mode.
- DOM event listeners do not borrow the engine. They go into a pending queue (PENDING_EVENT_LIST) and move to the engine at the start of the next frame.
  (because focus() called by apply_frame fires focus / blur events on the spot)
- Differences from the original: the hidden <input> exists only while the field runs its tick. (it goes away when the node is turned off or removed) Cursor moves deferred with setTimeout and
  the menu-close listener are the same as the original.

웹 오디오 백엔드. (wasm32, WebAudio 를 web-sys 로:
Web audio backend. (wasm32, calls WebAudio directly through web-sys)
- Ports the WebAudio calls of the original audiomanager.js, audioplayer.js, audioasset.js, beepplayer.js as they are.
- AudioContext: as in the original, AudioContext, or webkitAudioContext if missing. Created after a user gesture. (create_audio_player creates it even before that)
- resume: calls resume() only when "suspended" or "interrupted" (a nonstandard state of iOS WebKit) and ignores rejection.
  The state is read as a string. (web-sys's AudioContextState has no "interrupted")
- iOS clock check: the original verifyContextClock as is. (2026-10-22 03:41, for the iOS 26.6.2 update)
  If after restoring it is "running" but current_time advances less than 1/4 of real time over 0.5 seconds, calls suspend() then resume() and checks again.
  If that resume() is rejected, restores again with resume_context() after the same interval. Only one runs at a time.
- Decoding: done with OfflineAudioContext(1, 1, 44100) as in the original. If missing, done with a temporary AudioContext which is then closed.
- Context suspend: like the original SoundSystem.applyContextPause, calls suspend() only when "running", and reports and ignores rejection.
- Pan: like the original SoundSystem.playEffect, inserts a StereoPannerNode between the GainNode and the output if nonzero. (not inserted if createStereoPanner is missing)
- Bus: like the original AudioBus, one GainNode connected to the output. Players made on a bus connect their GainNode to the bus's GainNode instead of the output.
- The player's output (AudioOutputNode): like the outputNode of the original AudioPlayer constructor, takes an AudioNode and connects the player's GainNode to it. (the output if none)
- If the fetch response has a failure status, it counts as a failure before decoding, as in the original.
- Async: promises are awaited with spawn_local and JsFuture of wasm-bindgen-futures. (in place of the original then / await)
  Callbacks hold the manager's or player's state as Weak, and do nothing if it was dropped in the meantime.
- Differences from the original:
  Dropping a player stops the playing source node and disconnects the GainNode. (so the onended callback does not call a dropped closure)
  If another source started while waiting for resume after play in the suspended state, it stops that one and plays. (the original plays both)

웹소켓 통신 처리기. (JSON 을 주고받는 클라이언트)\n- 원본 we:
WebSocket communication handler. (a client that exchanges JSON)
- A port of the original web/websocketclient.js. Follows connect / disconnect / send(JSON) / is_connected / set_receive_event.
- The socket is ewebsock 0.8. Desktop uses a thread running tungstenite, the web (wasm) uses the browser WebSocket.
- In the original the browser calls onopen / onmessage / onclose. In the Rust version the scene calls tick every frame to take out the accumulated events.
  The read JSON is passed to receive_message as in the original. (the caller can also put it in directly)
  ```text
    // scene create
    self.web_socket_client.connect("ws://localhost:8080");
    // scene tick
    self.web_socket_client.tick();
    for message in self.web_socket_client.take_received_messages() { ... }
    self.web_socket_client.send(&serde_json::json!({ "type": "move", "x": 3 }));
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - Received JSON calls the receive callback if there is one, otherwise it is collected and taken out with take_received_messages. (also added to the original, up to RECEIVED_MESSAGE_LIMIT, the oldest are dropped first on overflow)
  - disconnect, as in the original, only requests the close on the spot, and the disconnection counts from the next tick. (in the original onclose comes later, so is_connected stays true until then.
    ewebsock desktop does not send a Closed event when closed from this side, so it disconnects after taking out the remaining events in that tick)
  - Error events are notified as in the original and counted as disconnected. (the browser always sends onclose after onerror, and the ewebsock desktop thread ends after an error)
  - get_web_socket is ewebsock's sender (WsSender).
  - The receive callback is kept in an `Rc<RefCell>`. get_receive_event returns that Rc, and the caller borrows it with borrow_mut to call it.
  - wss:// on desktop is opened with ewebsock's "tls" feature (tungstenite's rustls and webpki root certificates). The rustls crypto provider is ring and is set on the first connection.
    Only with the engine's tls feature (on by default). If it is off, desktop opens only ws://.
  - Binary messages are also received if they are UTF-8 JSON. (also added to the original)

- Standardizes the "string state + switch statement + manual transitions" that many games each built on their own.
- Register enter / tick / exit handling for each state and transition with change_state().
- set_transition_guard() can block disallowed transitions.
- The original's state names are strings. The Rust version lets you pick the state name type. (String by default; enums or &'static str also work)

- The original handlers object { enter?, tick?, exit? } is the StateHandlers struct. Callbacks are `Box<dyn FnMut>`, so
  to change game state, capture `Rc<Cell>` / `Rc<RefCell>`.
- The original calls the same machine's change_state right there inside a handler. In the Rust version a handler cannot borrow the machine, so
  capture the handle (StateChangeRequester) received from get_state_change_requester in the handler and request through its change_state.
  The machine transitions in request order after that handler ends. (the same as the original calling change_state at the very end of a handler)
  Whether the request succeeds is not returned right there. A request made outside a handler transitions on the next tick or change_state.

인체 피부 렌더러. (원본 experimental/graphics/hum:
Human skin renderer. (the original experimental/graphics/humanskinrenderer.js)
- Builds skin / eye / hair shading templates on top of the SkinnedModelRenderer skinning/morph vertex path.
- Outputs irradiance / albedo / specular / normal split into MRT in linear HDR, and compositing is done by the caller after SubsurfaceScatteringEffect.
- Registers a shading mode per material (set_material_shading). The opaque pass (draw) draws skin / eye / hair cutout,
  and the blend pass (draw_blended) draws hair fringe / occlusion / fluid. (the caller sets the blend state)
- Environment state: 3 lights (0 = key light, receives shadows), 3-color hemisphere ambient, normal, detail, roughness, specular, wrinkle, micro, eye, hair parameters.
- The GLSL is the same as the original. ${WRINKLE_CHANNEL_COUNT} / ${SHADOW_SAMPLE_COUNT} / ${SKIN_SHADING_*} in the original template strings became numbers,
  and ${MORPH_GLSL} became MORPH_GLSL concatenated at construction. (a test checks that the numbers match the constants)
- Texture units: 0 = base_color, 1 = shadow map, 2 ~ 8 = material slots, 9 ~ 14 = extra skin slots, 15 = morph target texture.
- Differences from the original:
  - The original inherits from SkinnedModelRenderer. The Rust version embeds a SkinnedModelRenderer and uses Deref / DerefMut so the base functions
    (draw_wireframe, apply_morph_uniforms, set_sun_direction, get_shader_program ...) can be called as is.
    draw / draw_depth / set_shadow_map / set_shadow_strength, which the original redefines, call this type's functions first.
    It can be passed as is in place of the base renderer, as in SkinnedModel::load_from_bytes(gl, bytes, &human_skin_renderer). (Deref coercion)
  - The draw functions take gl and &mut SkinnedModel like the base renderer, and upload changed morph targets first.
  - The material shading mode table is keyed by material instance (Rc pointer), like the original `Map<Material, number>`.
  - set_ambient_colors / set_hair_parameters take fixed-length arrays instead of the original arrays. set_shadow_sample_count takes an integer and
    clamps it to 1 ~ 24 without the original Math.floor.
  - set_shadow_map copies the 16 matrix values like the base renderer. Construction returns shader compile failures as an error (Result).

인체 피부 프래그먼트 셰이더. (선형 HDR, 화면 공간 SSS 를 위해:
Human skin fragment shader. (linear HDR, outputs irradiance / albedo / specular separately for screen-space SSS)
- Lighting: 3 directional lights (0 receives the shadow map) + 3-color hemisphere ambient + softbox reflection environment in the light directions.
- Skin: normal map + expression wrinkle maps (weighted blend of the mask atlas) + tiling micro normal / cavity + height derivative detail, dual-lobe GGX, peach fuzz.
- Eyes: samples the iris with corneal refraction parallax, iris normal / limbus / pupil, corneal glass highlights + environment reflection, scleral vein normals.
- Hair: Kajiya-Kay dual-lobe anisotropic highlights from the card tangent atlas, root occlusion, transmitted backlight, 2 passes of cutout + fringe blend.
- Occlusion / fluid: blend pass only, the eyelid occlusion mesh only darkens irradiance, tear lines / saliva only add specular.
- Facial hair (eyebrows / beard): the same shading as hair but without sway.
- Output 0: diffuse irradiance (rgb) + SSS mask (a) / 1: linear albedo (rgb) + coverage (a) / 2: specular (rgb) / 3: world normal (rgb).

입력 관리자.\n- 키 이름은 원본과 같이 KeyboardEvent.co:
Input manager.
- Key names are in KeyboardEvent.code form like the original. ("KeyA", "ArrowLeft", "Space" ...)
  winit's KeyCode names follow the same W3C convention, so they are converted to strings as is. Only for the Windows key (Command key), winit calls it SuperLeft, SuperRight
  and calls the old W3C Super key Meta, so the desktop platform puts in MetaLeft, MetaRight, Super instead.
- The constant names of KeyCode are the original KeyCode key names converted to Rust constant form. (DIGIT0 for things like "0" that cannot be a name)
  LEFT, UP, RIGHT, DOWN, which were not in the original, are kept with the same values as the ARROWLEFT family.
- The mouse button (or first finger) is handled as touch. (the original merges mouse and touch into one) Like the original, initially any button is touch,
  and with set_touch_from_left_button_only(true) only the left button is touch. Whether to block the canvas right-click menu (set_context_menu_prevented, initially true) blocks the browser context menu on the web.
  Desktop windows have no browser context menu, so the result is the same as blocking it in Chrome.
- It also holds the pressed state of the three mouse buttons (left, middle, right), the list of touching fingers, whether the last input was a finger, and whether the wheel was rolled with Ctrl.
  Places that use input beyond the single button touch, like camera gestures (CameraGestures), read them. The platform fills them in. (vanilla.js read canvas DOM events directly)
- Gamepads, like the original, are polled in tick by the GamepadManager that InputManager holds. (core/gamepadmanager.rs)
- Text input (committed text, IME composition, editing keys) is gathered in the TextInput queue. Input fields take it from there. (core/textinput.rs, a layer not in the original)
- This frame's presses and releases of keys and mouse buttons are seen by accumulating events that came after the end of the last frame, like the original. A press and release between frames is also caught.
- Fingers, like the original, receive touch (begin_touch_point), move and release and are given a phase (TouchPhase), and a lifted finger stays in get_ended_touch_points for one frame.
- It holds the last used device (InputDevice) and pad kind, the keys to block (set_prevented_keys), whether typing in a text field (is_typing_in_text_field), and input actions (InputActions).
  The keys to block prevent browser default actions on the web (such as Tab moving focus, Space and arrows scrolling, F5 refreshing). Desktop windows have no such default actions, so the result is the same as blocking them.
  For text fields it looks at the engine input field (the active field of TextInput) and, on the web, the document focus (text input, textarea, contenteditable, select).
입력 관리자. (원본 InputManager)\n- 엔진이 하나 들고 플:
Input manager. (the original InputManager)
- The engine holds one and the platform puts in key, mouse, finger and wheel events. Scenes read it with engine.get_input_manager().
- This frame's presses and releases, touch Pressed / Released / Cancelled, and wheel deltas are cleared by the engine at the end of the frame.
입력 동작.\n- 동작은 bind_key, bind_gamepad_but:
Input actions.
- Only actions recorded once with one of bind_key, bind_gamepad_button, bind_axis or set_repeat are updated.
Input actions.
- A port of the original core/inputactions.js. Binds keys, gamepad buttons and one side of gamepad axes to action names (text the game chooses, like "confirm" or "left").
  Several can be bound to one action, and it is pressed if any one of them is pressed.
- The engine's InputManager holds one (get_input_actions) and calls update in tick at the start of the frame. The game only reads.
- A key pressed and released between frames also counts as pressed once in that frame. (InputManager.is_key_just_pressed)
- For an action with set_repeat, while held, is_just_pressed becomes true again at each interval after the wait. (menu selection)
- Axes subtract the dead zone (set_dead_zone) and rescale the rest to 0 ~ 1. Sticks are filtered by length, bound axes by one side's value.
- External sources (add_source) are where the game plugs in input the engine does not know (such as a platform SDK's pad). They implement the InputActionSource trait.
- Keys are not listened to while typing in a text input. (turned off with set_keys_ignored_while_typing)
- Like the Unity Input System, it updates once in update at the start of the frame, and reads within that frame return the values recorded then. (same as the original)
  During update it records the move keys, pad axes and external sources' move axes, and read_gamepad_stick and read_move_axis read those values.
- Differences from the original: external sources are a trait instead of JS objects, and removal uses the number given by add_source.

입력 필드. (원본 ui/uiinputfield.js 의 UIInputF:
Input field. (UIInputField, BackgroundLayerRenderer, OverlayLayerRenderer of the original ui/uiinputfield.js)
- Draws text, cursor, selection, IME composition text and its underline, and the focus border directly onto the canvas, and sets the cursor and selection by pressing and dragging.
- The original is a node inheriting WorldNode, with text drawn by two UILabel child nodes (value, placeholder) and the cursor and border drawn by an overlay child node.
  The Rust version is a component like the other widgets. Attach it with node_tree.add_component(node_id, UIInputField::new()).
  It contains a UIControl, creates the content node in attach_to_tree and turns the host interactable. The pivot and anchor are set to the top left as in the original.
  Text is drawn with two contained Text instances (value, placeholder), and the background (the original Paint component) is also drawn with a contained Paint.
  The layer order is the same as the original: background → selection → text → composition underline → cursor → focus border. One component draws them all at once, so
  even if scene code calls set_text outside tick, it shows up immediately that frame. (splitting into child nodes would lag one frame while moving the state)
- Input is received from the engine's text input queue (core/textinput.rs). The attach()ed field with focus takes it out in tick.
  - Desktop: winit KeyboardInput and Ime events. IME is enabled only when a field with use_dom_input (the original setUseDOMInput) on has focus.
  - Web: as in the original, a hidden DOM <input> is placed over each field. (platform/web/textinput.rs) The DOM owns the value and selection, and the field follows.
    Fields with use_dom_input off receive window keydown like the original canvas mode.
- Differences from the original:
  - Events are Box<dyn FnMut(&mut UIInputField, &mut ComponentContext)>. Original callbacks receive only the value. (the value is field.get_text())
  - setFont(FontFace) became set_font_family(registered font name). setEngine was not ported. (the engine comes from the context)
  - Character positions in the public functions (get_cursor_index, get_selection_start, get_selection_range, move_cursor, measure_index_at_local_x) and max_length
    count in UTF-16 units as in the original. Internally they are held in characters (char) so surrogate pairs (characters like emoji) are not split.
    So a UTF-16 position in the middle of a surrogate pair is treated as after that character. (the original does the same) With max_length, inserted text is cut to the remaining length like a Blink input box.
  - Pressed position → character position is found from the character boundaries measured during draw. (the original measures each time with an offscreen 2D canvas)
  - On desktop, fields with use_dom_input on also lose focus when pressing outside the field, like the original DOM mode. There is only one focus in the engine.
    (in the original canvas mode, the previous field keeps focus even when another field is pressed. The Rust version keeps only the field that gained focus last)
  - When focus is lost, text being composed is committed into the value. (same as what browsers do for DOM inputs)
  - The desktop context menu (right button) is drawn on the canvas since there is no DOM. It is created as the last child node of the root and drawn on top. On the web it is a DOM menu as in the original.
    Fields that let the DOM input be pressed directly (use_direct_touch) draw the edit box menu Chrome shows in the original, with the same items and shortcut text. (ui/uiinputfieldmenu.rs)
    Those fields select a word with a finger long press (650ms, within 15 DIP) like Chrome desktop touch and show touch handles and the quick menu. (Windows decides the menu on release)
  - Desktop DOM input fields undo and redo like the original DOM input box. (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y, Cmd on Mac, Blink's grouping rules, TextEditBuffer)
  - Desktop single-line DOM input fields, like a Blink input box, remove trailing line breaks from inserted text and replace middle line breaks with spaces, and up and page up move to the text start, down and page down to the text end.
  - With set_multiline(true), it is a multiline input like Chrome textarea. (not in the original engine, where the original uses a DOM textarea through the textarea preset of Pane)
    Text is split by line break characters and width, like white-space: pre-wrap, overflow-wrap: break-word. (ui/textarealayout.rs, line break positions follow Unicode line breaking like Chrome)
    Enter inserts a line (in the character insertion undo group), up and down keep the horizontal position from the first vertical move (up on the first line goes to the text start, down on the last line to the text end),
    Home and End go to the start and end of the visible line (also Cmd + Left, Right on Mac), Ctrl + Home, End (Cmd + Up, Down on Mac) go to the text start and end,
    PageUp, PageDown (with Option on Mac) move to the farthest line within 87.5% of the visible height (on Mac, the larger of that and height - 40) and bring that line to the top.
    CR and CRLF in inserted text become LF. After edits and moves it scrolls to keep the cursor visible (to the edge except on macOS, to the center on macOS), and it scrolls with the wheel and thumb dragging.
    A normal line height is computed from the first font's ascent, descent and line gap like Chrome. With classic scroll bars (Windows, Linux, the macOS classic setting), the scroll bar takes away text width when overflowing, like Chrome.
    On macOS, Home and End leave the cursor and scroll to the start and end like Chrome on macOS (line start and end if there is nothing to scroll), and PageUp, PageDown leave the cursor and scroll by one screen.
  - Fields imitating DOM input (use_dom_input, multiline) select a word (with the trailing space on Windows) on a double click and a paragraph on a triple click like Chrome, and dragging extends by that unit.
    Repeated presses are within 500ms (the system double-click time on macOS) and within 2 DIP horizontally and vertically, like Chrome aura. The web uses the mousedown detail counted by the browser.
  - Cursor movement and Delete work by grapheme cluster (extended grapheme cluster) like Chrome, and Backspace follows Blink's BackspaceStateMachine (one code point, emoji sequences whole).
    For web DOM input, a hidden `<textarea>` handles text, composition and undo, and keys that move by visible lines (up and down, page, Home, End) are handled by the field using the engine layout.
  - Word movement and deletion (Ctrl on Windows and Linux, Option on macOS, with Left, Right, Backspace, Delete) follow Blink NextWordPosition, PreviousWordPosition like Chrome's textarea.
    (Right goes to the start of the next word only on Windows, and to the end of the current word on macOS and Linux. On macOS, an extending selection does not cross the anchor) For web DOM input, the browser does it.
  - Turning off (set_active(false)) or removing the node stops tick, so focus, IME and the web's hidden <input> go away together. (the original goes away only when detached)
  - getRenderState was not ported. (there is only one drawing component, so there is nothing to pass)
  - UI documents (UIDocument) write and read it in the original node form when registered with register_node_type. (node type "UIInputField", background Paint, draw layers, placeholder and value UILabel children,
    overlay child. UIDocumentNode in uidocument.rs) The content node the Rust version creates is not written to the document.
    The positions and sizes of the text labels and overlay are written from the node size last placed by tick (text_layout_size), like the original refreshTextPositions.

Input field. (UIInputField, BackgroundLayerRenderer, OverlayLayerRenderer of the original ui/uiinputfield.js)
- Draws text, cursor, selection, IME composition text and its underline, and the focus border directly onto the canvas, and sets the cursor and selection by pressing and dragging.
- The original is a node inheriting WorldNode, with text drawn by two UILabel child nodes (value, placeholder) and the cursor and border drawn by an overlay child node.
  The Rust version is a component like the other widgets. Attach it with node_tree.add_component(node_id, UIInputField::new()).
  It contains a UIControl, creates the content node in attach_to_tree and turns the host interactable. The pivot and anchor are set to the top left as in the original.
  Text is drawn with two contained Text instances (value, placeholder), and the background (the original Paint component) is also drawn with a contained Paint.
  The layer order is the same as the original: background → selection → text → composition underline → cursor → focus border. One component draws them all at once, so
  even if scene code calls set_text outside tick, it shows up immediately that frame. (splitting into child nodes would lag one frame while moving the state)
- Input is received from the engine's text input queue (core/textinput.rs). The attach()ed field with focus takes it out in tick.
  - Desktop: winit KeyboardInput and Ime events. IME is enabled only when a field with use_dom_input (the original setUseDOMInput) on has focus.
  - Web: as in the original, a hidden DOM <input> is placed over each field. (platform/web/textinput.rs) The DOM owns the value and selection, and the field follows.
    Fields with use_dom_input off receive window keydown like the original canvas mode.
- Differences from the original:
  - Events are Box<dyn FnMut(&mut UIInputField, &mut ComponentContext)>. Original callbacks receive only the value. (the value is field.get_text())
  - setFont(FontFace) became set_font_family(registered font name). setEngine was not ported. (the engine comes from the context)
  - Character positions in the public functions (get_cursor_index, get_selection_start, get_selection_range, move_cursor, measure_index_at_local_x) and max_length
    count in UTF-16 units as in the original. Internally they are held in characters (char) so surrogate pairs (characters like emoji) are not split.
    So a UTF-16 position in the middle of a surrogate pair is treated as after that character. Truncating with max_length also cuts only as far as it can without splitting a character. (the original can split pairs)
  - Pressed position → character position is found from the character boundaries measured during draw. (the original measures each time with an offscreen 2D canvas)
  - On desktop, fields with use_dom_input on also lose focus when pressing outside the field, like the original DOM mode. There is only one focus in the engine.
    (in the original canvas mode, the previous field keeps focus even when another field is pressed. The Rust version keeps only the field that gained focus last)
  - When focus is lost, text being composed is committed into the value. (same as what browsers do for DOM inputs)
  - The desktop context menu (right button) is drawn on the canvas since there is no DOM. It is created as the last child node of the root and drawn on top. On the web it is a DOM menu as in the original.
    Fields that let the DOM input be pressed directly (use_direct_touch) draw the edit box menu Chrome shows in the original, with the same items and shortcut text. (ui/uiinputfieldmenu.rs)
    Those fields select a word with a finger long press (650ms, within 15 DIP) like Chrome desktop touch and show touch handles and the quick menu. (Windows decides the menu on release)
  - Desktop DOM input fields undo and redo like the original DOM input box. (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y, Cmd on Mac, Blink's grouping rules, TextEditBuffer)
  - Desktop single-line DOM input fields, like a Blink input box, remove trailing line breaks from inserted text and replace middle line breaks with spaces, and up and page up move to the text start, down and page down to the text end.
  - With set_multiline(true), it is a multiline input like Chrome textarea. (not in the original engine, where the original uses a DOM textarea through the textarea preset of Pane)
    Text is split by line break characters and width, like white-space: pre-wrap, overflow-wrap: break-word. (ui/textarealayout.rs, line break positions follow Unicode line breaking like Chrome)
    Enter inserts a line (in the character insertion undo group), up and down keep the horizontal position from the first vertical move (up on the first line goes to the text start, down on the last line to the text end),
    Home and End go to the start and end of the visible line (also Cmd + Left, Right on Mac), Ctrl + Home, End (Cmd + Up, Down on Mac) go to the text start and end,
    PageUp, PageDown (with Option on Mac) move to the farthest line within 87.5% of the visible height (on Mac, the larger of that and height - 40) and bring that line to the top.
    CR and CRLF in inserted text become LF. The cursor scrolls into view after editing and moving (to the edge except on Mac, to the center on Mac), and the wheel and dragging the overlay thumb scroll.
    For web DOM input, a hidden `<textarea>` handles text, composition and undo, and keys that move by visible lines (up and down, page, Home, End) are handled by the field using the engine layout.
  - Turning off (set_active(false)) or removing the node stops tick, so focus, IME and the web's hidden <input> go away together. (the original goes away only when detached)
  - getRenderState was not ported. (there is only one drawing component, so there is nothing to pass)
  - UI documents (UIDocument) write and read it in the original node form when registered with register_node_type. (node type "UIInputField", background Paint, draw layers, placeholder and value UILabel children,
    overlay child. UIDocumentNode in uidocument.rs) The content node the Rust version creates is not written to the document.
    The positions and sizes of the text labels and overlay are written from the node size last placed by tick (text_layout_size), like the original refreshTextPositions.

Tasks. (the engine continues game code written with async/await every frame. A file only in the Rust version)
- In the original the browser runs Promises, and an async function pauses at await and continues when the Promise resolves.
  In the Rust version the engine contains a single-threaded executor. Engine::spawn_task, spawn_scene_task, like calling an original async function,
  poll once up to the first await right where it is entrusted, and the remaining tasks are polled every frame (after updating time and input, before the scene's tick) only if woken.
  (where there is only &Engine, entrust with spawn_deferred_task, spawn_deferred_scene_task and it runs for the first time on the next polling turn)
  No external runtime is used, and desktop and web run the same code. Futures need not be Send. (they may hold Rc, the web has no threads)
- Waking: like the original microtask queue, woken tasks go into a queue (TaskWakeQueue) in the order woken, and on the polling turn they are polled from the front until the queue is empty.

  A Promise is woken by resolve, a TaskHandle when that task finishes, and a JsFuture wrapping a web Promise when the browser resolves it.
  Waker is Send + Sync, so the queue is held in Arc and Mutex and the flags in atomic values. (the same code on the web even without threads)
- Reaching the engine and scene: a future cannot hold &mut across an await. A task receives a context (EngineContext, SceneContext),
  and borrows the engine and scene only inside a with(|scene, engine| ...) closure. The closure is synchronous so it cannot await inside, and the lifetime of the references the closure receives
  is assigned fresh for each closure (`for<'a>`) and cannot be put in the returned value (R), so references cannot leak out of the closure.

     The task list being polled is a local value taken out of the engine, so borrowing the engine does not reach it. (new tasks entrusted meanwhile pile up in a separate list in the engine)
  3. with takes the pointers out of the slot (take) and restores them when done. The slot is empty meanwhile, so a second &mut cannot be made by any path.

Preserves unpaired surrogates in stored text. (only in the Rust version, used by LocalStorage and PersistedStore)
- The original localStorage and JSON are JS strings (UTF-16), so they hold unpaired surrogates (U+D800 ~ U+DFFF that lost their pair).
  They come from user input such as cut emoji, and JSON.stringify writes them as escapes like \ud83d. (the well-formed JSON.stringify of ES2019)
- Rust String is UTF-8 and cannot hold such text. So they appear as the replacement character (U+FFFD) on the Rust side,
  and unmodified text is written back in its original UTF-16 units. Values saved by the original version are not lost when the Rust version reads and rewrites them.
- PreservedText: the original UTF-16 units and the text as displayed with replacement characters.
- parse_json, parse_json_code_units: read like JSON.parse but read unpaired surrogates (both escapes and raw units) as the replacement character,
  and record the places (JSON paths) where such text was and the original units in a JsonSurrogateTable. Numbers are the same as what serde_json reads.
- stringify_json: writes the same text as serde_json's compact form (Value::to_string), but if text displayed with replacement characters is still at a place in the table, it writes the original units,
  and even at another place, if the text is the same (same as moving text over in the original), it writes the original units as \udXXX like JSON.stringify.
  If two or more texts look the same with replacement characters but have different original units, only those at matching places are written in the original units.

절차적 비프 재생기.\n- 원본 misc/beepplayer.js. 오디:
Procedural beep player.
- The original misc/beepplayer.js. Synthesizes UI sound effects without audio files.
  An attack / sustain / release envelope avoids clicks.
- Provides click / confirm / cancel / error / success / warning / notification presets and
  arbitrary tone sequence playback (play_sequence).
- Usage:
  ```text
    let beep_player = BeepPlayer::new(engine.get_audio_manager(), BeepPlayer::DEFAULT_VOLUME);
    beep_player.play_preset("confirm");
  ```
- Where the sound is made:
  Web: like the original, creates an OscillatorNode + GainNode and connects them straight to the audio context output.
  Desktop: builds the same graph in the mixer (OscillatorNode → GainNode AudioParam automation → output, computed the same way as Chrome). (platform/audio/oscillator.rs, mixer.rs)
- Differences from the original:
  Waveform names are BeepWaveform instead of strings, and sequence tones are BeepTone. Preset names are strings like the original.

점토 모형(GLB) 읽기와 뼈대 자세. (vanilla.js graphi:
Reading clay models (GLB) and skeleton poses. (vanilla.js graphics3d/toon/glbmeshreader.js)
- Reads models painted with material colors into toon 3D MeshBuilder vertex arrays. Texture coordinates and material textures are read too if present. (Came from webgame-rimminer)
  - One part is one node, and a node's mesh is one primitive per color. Vertices are position and normal, plus joint indices and weights if there is a skeleton.
  - The material's baseColorFactor is a linear color, so it is converted to sRGB, and emissiveFactor, if present, is stored as glow. (If there is an emissiveTexture, glow is passed only through the material range)
  - TEXCOORD_0, if present, goes into uv_data and TEXCOORD_1 into uv1_data (second UV, angel ring). A material range (ToonMaterialRange) is stored per primitive. (Material name, extras, texture image order)
    When painting split areas inside a part (accent color areas, display panels), pick them by material name or extras and draw only that area with index_start and index_count of ToonDrawOptions.
  - Images are read with read_glb_images, decoded with decode_glb_image and passed to ToonRenderer::create_texture.
  - outline in material extras is an outline shell (only back faces drawn), and basic is a part that does not receive light.
    If outline options are given, that shell is not stored, and a shell of uniform thickness per point is newly built from the body of each node that has a ".outline" pair.
  - If there is a skeleton (skin), the joint nodes and their inverse bind matrices, the animations (animations) and their extras are read together. Poses are computed by write_skin_pose.
  - Models whose parts are hidden or painted separately are read per node with read_glb_node_arrays. (Together with node extras and transparency)
  - For a skeletal model read as one lump, node extras, part positions and the joints they follow are read separately with read_glb_node_infos.
- Separate from the engine's SkinnedModel (textured PBR). Only the vertex arrays used for toon drawing are extracted.

지속 저장소.\n- 원본 misc/persistedstore.js 를 옮:
Persistent store.
- A port of the original misc/persistedstore.js. Saves a state object as JSON under one key and notifies subscribers when it changes.
- If the version number (version) differs or parsing fails, it falls back to the defaults.
- Saving uses LocalStorage. The save format ({"version":1,"state":{...}}) is the same as the original, so on the web it reads the original game's saves as is.
  set_storage_backend can put only this store somewhere else (LocalStorageBackend, such as a platform's storage).
  The passed storage is put in `Rc<RefCell>`. get_storage_backend returns that Rc, and the caller borrows it with borrow / borrow_mut.
  (reading or writing this store while it is borrowed gives empty text for reads, and writes report it and move on)
- Usage:
  ```text
    let mut store = PersistedStore::new("game.settings", serde_json::json!({ "volume": 0.8, "is_muted": false }), 1);
    store.set(serde_json::json!({ "volume": 0.5 }));

  ```
- Merging is the same as the original Object.assign. Arrays are merged by index keys ("0", "1" ...) (even if the saved state is an array), and the key order puts index-like keys first from the smallest number, like JS objects.
- Differences from the original:
  The state object is serde_json::Value (an object). Values that are neither objects nor arrays are treated as an empty object. (the original Object.assign merges a string by character index keys)
  subscribe returns a subscription number (PersistedStoreSubscription) instead of an unsubscribe function, and unsubscribe(number) removes it.
  Rust String cannot hold unpaired surrogates, so such text saved by the original (like \ud83d from JSON.stringify) appears as the replacement character (U+FFFD) in the state.
  Their places are remembered when reading, and writing back unmodified writes \udXXX like the original. (misc/storagetext.rs, saves from the original version are not lost when read and rewritten)

- Dims the whole area (presses do not pass through to what is behind) and shows a panel in the center. The dim also covers the safe area (set_view_bleed).
- The panel widens to fit the area's width but does not exceed maximum_width. Its height is the value returned by layout_content, and if it is larger than the area the whole panel is scaled down.
- The open and close motion is PopupMotion. When the close motion finishes, the window layer (UIWindowLayer) removes the node. (it does not receive presses in the meantime)
- Pressing outside (the dim) closes it. Turned off per window with set_outside_close_enabled. The window layer's close_top_window (back) also follows this value.
- Node structure: window (area size) ├ dim (Paint + UIButton) └ frame (panel center pivot, motion scale) └ panel (a single Paint, content goes here)
- Differences from the original:
  - In the original it is a node inheriting WorldNode, and derived classes override layoutContent, layoutPanel, applyMotion, setCovered, handleWheel, dispose.
    The Rust version is a component attached to the window node, and the override points are the UIWindowBehavior trait. (the default implementation is UIWindowDefaultBehavior,
    and an override that wants to call the default like the original super uses UIWindow::layout_panel_default, apply_motion_default, set_covered_default)
    The panel look (shadow, border, gloss) is done by the game attaching decoration nodes to the frame in build (set_sibling_index(0) for behind the panel) and placing them in layout_panel.
  - The window node is created under the window layer node with UIWindow::create(node_tree, layer_id, name, behavior). When the close motion finishes, it is detached from the layer and not removed, so
    the same window node can be opened again as in the original. (UIWindowLayer::open_window) The original window attaches to the layer when opened, so create keeps the node off until it is opened.
    When attached, it does not turn the node off as the original constructor does. (so the UI document reads and writes the window node as active, as in the original)
  - Closing goes through the window layer. Scene and callback code calls UIWindow::close_in_tree(node_tree, window_id).
  - The notification (set_close_event) is an argumentless `Box<dyn FnMut()>`. (same form as the PopupMotion notification, node changes are done by the scene checking the state in tick)
  - As in the original, GameSceneBase passes wheel input pointing inside the window layer to UIWindowLayer::scroll_window_at so the top window (UIWindowBehavior::handle_wheel) gets it first,
    and if it does not take it, the scroll view at that spot does. Wheel input that reaches a window through the engine's wheel delivery (from the pointed node toward the parents) without going through GameSceneBase is also taken by the window and always swallowed.
  - The panel and dim Paints are components of nodes, so get_panel_paint and get_dim_paint take the tree.

Detects slow devices. (FrameProbe of vanilla.js misc/frameprobe.js)
- Measures the frame intervals of the first few seconds, used to automatically turn on a light path that disables heavy effects.
- After the wait seconds from the start of measuring have passed, looks at each frame's interval during the measure seconds. (the first few seconds stutter while models and images load)
- If the share of frames exceeding the slow factor times the target interval (one tick of the maximum frame rate, or one tick of 60 frames if unlimited) is at least the slow share, it is a slow device.
  - Why 1.4 times instead of one tick: a 90 Hz screen at a maximum of 60 has the engine drawing every other frame, always 22 ms apart, and that is not the device being slow.
  - On 60 Hz and 120 Hz screens, frames that missed one refresh (33 ms, 25 ms) are counted as slow. One in four means below 48 fps.
- Once decided as a slow device, it does not measure again. If the window is hidden before measuring is done, restart measures again from the beginning.
  If not slow, measure_again can measure once more in a heavy scene.
- Does not import the engine. The caller passes the frame interval and the maximum frame rate.

- Gestures that rotate, pan, and zoom a 3D board or a map. Uses input outside the engine's touch (left button, first finger).
  - Dragging with the right mouse button held: rotates by the horizontal drag (the canvas width is one full turn) and tilts by the vertical drag. Releasing without dragging is a right click.
  - Dragging with the middle mouse button held: pans.
  - Two fingers: dragging in the same direction pans, pinching in and out zooms around the midpoint of the two fingers, and twisting past the twist threshold rotates. (prevents slowly rotating while pinch zooming)
    As in the original, the gesture continues until every finger is lifted. When only one finger remains its movement is ignored, and when the finger count changes that spot becomes the new reference.
- The engine handles the wheel. This only records whether Ctrl was held. (is_last_wheel_ctrl, laptop touchpad pinches also arrive as Ctrl wheel)
- Also reads whether the last input was a finger (is_touch_input, initially whether the device's primary input is touch). Within the time that emulated mouse events are ignored after a finger is lifted (fourth argument of set_thresholds, initially 800 milliseconds),
  mouse moves and presses do not switch the input, and right or middle buttons pressed then do not start a gesture until released.
- The original listens to the canvas DOM events directly (hence addListener, dispose). The Rust version reads the input manager (mouse buttons, finger list, wheel Ctrl) with update every frame.
  The web platform passes the buttons and positions of emulated mouse events without filtering, like the original engine.js (only the last device is filtered for 800 milliseconds), so the fourth argument threshold works whether it is shorter or longer than 800, as in the original.
  It measures by frame time instead of event time. (the frame that had the finger event and the frame that read the mouse button)
- During a gesture it reports is_gesture_active so presses and releases passed by the engine are not used for gameplay.
- The accumulated amounts (pan, rotation, tilt, zoom) are taken out every frame with take. Pan is in view units, rotation and tilt in radians, and zoom is a ratio to multiply by.

Context menu. (UIContextMenu of the original ui/uicontextmenu.js, a right click / long press menu)
- show(node_tree, position, item_list) pops up the item list at that position. Pressing outside closes it, and pressing an item closes it and then calls the handler.
- The menu is pinned to the right / bottom edge so it does not go outside the parent area. (960 x 640 if the parent size is unknown)
- Place it at the top of the scene root (the last child).
- The original is a node that inherits WorldNode. The Rust version is a component attached to a node (host), and on attach, like the original constructor, it
  sets up the host (top-left pivot, inactive) and creates an outside-press blocker (transparent UIButton) and a menu panel (rounded Paint) as children.
  UIContextMenu::create(node_tree, parent_id, options) takes the place of the original new UIContextMenu(options) + add_child.
- Usage:
  ```text
    let menu_id = UIContextMenu::create(node_tree, root_id, UIContextMenuOptions::default());
    node_tree.with_component_mut::<UIContextMenu, _>(menu_id, |context_menu, tree| {
        context_menu.show(tree, view_position, vec![UIContextMenuItem::create("Copy", Box::new(|context| { ... })), UIContextMenuItem::create_disabled("Delete")]);
    });
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - show / close change nodes, so they take the tree. Scene code calls them with node_tree.with_component_mut.
  - Items are a UIContextMenuItem struct ({ text, handler?, is_disabled }), and a handler is a one-shot function (FnOnce) that takes the context of the pressed row node.
  - is_showing returns the value changed by show / close instead of the node's active state.
  - Previous rows are deleted instead of detached (removeChild). Row node names are "ContextMenuItem{index}" as in the original.

Component.
- A unit of functionality attached to a node. In the original it inherits the Component class, here it implements the Component trait.
- Components in the original find their own node with get_node(). The Rust version passes a ComponentContext on tick / touch.
  From the context it takes its own node (transform), the whole tree (finding, creating, removing other nodes) and the engine (input, time, view).
- draw receives only its own transform, with the node transform applied. (the tree is not changed while drawing)
- push_transform and pop_transform are called before and after drawing the node (wrapping its own components, children and gizmos). This is where an original node overrode pushTransform and popTransform
  to change drawing state for its descendants too (such as blending). (TouchEffect's additive blend)
- Common state such as enable / gizmo lives in ComponentBase, and implementors only return it.
- Dependent components (the original require): the original returns a list of classes. The Rust version returns a list of RequiredComponent (a type and a function that creates it with default values),
  and WorldNode::add_component creates and attaches that type before attaching if it is missing. When detached, detach is called as in the original.
- The original setNode, getNode and setComponentType were not ported. The Rust version passes the node through the context (there are no global object references) and the type decides the name.
- Reflection (the original scans the prototype at runtime to find get, is, set functions): attach `#[vanilla::reflect]` to the impl block and the impl Component block, and
  the macro builds the list and the calling code at compile time, and get_reflection returns it. (core/reflection.rs) Components without it return None.
  Rust has no way to read a method list at runtime, so only types with the attribute are reflected. (in the original every object is, the same shape as Unreal UCLASS)
  Getting the concrete type out (in place of C++ RTTI's dynamic_cast) is done with AsAny.

Tilemap layer. (the original src/experimental/tilemap/tilemaplayer.js)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- Each cell holds a tile value (32 bits, the top 4 bits are flip and rotation, the bottom 28 bits are the map-wide tile id gid, 0 is an empty cell). (same form as Tiled's global tile ids)
- Cells are held in chunks (chunk, default 16 x 16). Only written chunks are created, so it holds large maps and endless maps (negative cells), and Tilemap culls off-screen chunks one by one.
- Each layer has a color (multiply tint), opacity, drawing position offset, blend mode and properties.
- Differences from the original: chunks are held in a BTreeMap in (row, column) order. (the original uses a Map and a flat list) The blend mode is BlendMode. (the original uses Canvas2D name strings)
타일맵. (원본 src/experimental/tilemap/tilema:
Tilemap. (the original src/experimental/tilemap/tilemap.js)
- Draft: a feature after 0.4.0, the API may change.
- A component attached to a node. The top left of the node's content area is the map's (0, 0), and layers (TilemapLayer) are drawn in the order they were added.
- There are four orientations: orthogonal (orthogonal), isometric (isometric, diamond), staggered (staggered, staggered isometric) and hexagonal (hexagonal).
  Coordinate conversion, draw order, tile image alignment (the cell's bottom left), flips and rotations use the same math as the Tiled renderer (libtiled).
- Each layer chunk (chunk) is checked for overlap with the screen and skipped entirely if it does not overlap. Overlapping chunks append tiles that use the same image to a vertex buffer,
  drawing with one `Graphic::draw_vertices` call only when the image changes or the buffer fills. (Chunk mode of Unity TilemapRenderer)
  Individual mode draws in the cell order of the whole map across chunks. (the order is exact when large tiles overlap neighboring chunks)
- Tile animation runs on one clock advanced by tick, so all cells animate together. (same as Tiled)
- Collision shapes do not depend on physics. read_cell_collision_shapes returns map-coordinate shapes (TileCollisionShape) with each cell's flip, rotation and offset applied.
- Differences from the original: tilesets and layers are held by value. (in the original they are object references, so several maps share the same tileset; Rust clones the Tileset)

Timeline. (keyframe animation document player)
- A port of the original animation/timeline.js. The document (description) is JSON made of a stage node list + tracks (target name / property / keys) + markers,
  saved by the timeline editor. A key's easing applies to the span from that key to the next key.
- Easing curves use easing_function from core/tween.rs as is. "bezier" uses the same control points as CSS cubic-bezier.
- Usage:
  ```text
    // Request the document in the scene's create and hand it over.
    self.timeline_asset.load(engine, "assets/intro.timeline.json");
    self.scene_base.track_asset(&self.timeline_asset);
    // Build the stage in initialize and play it.
    let mut timeline = Timeline::create_from_json_asset(&mut self.timeline_asset).unwrap_or_default();
    let stage_id = self.scene_base.get_root_id();
    timeline.build_stage(self.scene_base.get_node_tree_mut(), stage_id, Some(&|image_name: &str| image_table.get(image_name).cloned()));
    timeline.play();
    // Every frame (tick):
    timeline.tick(self.scene_base.get_node_tree_mut(), time_delta);
  ```
- Differences from the original:
  - Targets are TimelineTarget instead of object references. Nodes are Node(NodeId), and things that are not nodes (such as screen effects) are External(`Rc<RefCell<dyn TimelinePropertyTarget>>`).
    Functions that act on nodes (tick, seek, stop, evaluate, compile, build_stage, bind) also take the NodeTree.
  - For External targets, evaluate calls set_timeline_property right there, as in the original. (the scene shares the target as `Rc<RefCell>`)
    The receiving side implements the TimelinePropertyTarget trait. ScreenEffect implements it in this file.
    Values the last evaluate applied to External targets can be read with get_external_properties. (for editors and tests)
  - Values hold the original's number / string / boolean as the TimelineValue enum. Numbers are f32.
  - Handlers take the timeline itself (&mut Timeline) as the last argument as in the original, followed by the NodeTree to pass to node functions.
    The handler is taken out of its slot while it is called, so pause, seek and set_*_handler can be called inside a handler. (a newly set handler wins)
  - Text properties (text, number, fontSize, visibleCharacters, color) also apply to RichText nodes, just as the original getComponent(Text) also finds RichText, which inherits Text.
  - resolve_timeline_easing returns a TimelineEasing value instead of a function. (call it with evaluate(progress))
  - TIMELINE_PROPERTY_DEFINITIONS is an array of definitions instead of a name → definition object, searched with find_timeline_property_definition.
    TIMELINE_NODE_DEFAULTS is a TimelineNodeDescription filled with the defaults. (the original key type is node_type)
  - The original's sprite grid table and sound table (WeakMap) became small components attached to nodes, TimelineSpriteFrameGrid and TimelineSound.
  - The original Timeline.setAudioManager (static) and the asynchronous loading of sound nodes became load_sounds(node_tree, engine).
    Calling it once after building the stage loads an audio asset and creates a player for each sound node. (the scene may take over the returned assets with track_audio_asset)
  - loadFromUrl (asynchronous fetch) is load_from_url(engine, asset path). It asks for the bytes through the engine's asset fetching, and awaiting it inside an engine task yields the timeline.
    (desktop uses the asset folder candidates, web fetches from asset_base_url) Without await, pass a document received with JsonAsset to create_from_json_asset / load_from_text.
  - "data:" URL images: on the web, as in the original, the browser decodes them (fetch and HTMLImageElement, platform/web.rs), and once decoded they are set on the sprite and the description's cell is picked again.
    (the original image.onload's applySpriteFrame; meanwhile TimelineSpriteFrameGrid waits and updates)
    On desktop they are decoded right there. Like a browser, it first decodes percent forms (%XX) in the body, and decodes base64 if ;base64. If the URL's type is image/svg+xml it is an SVG drawn with resvg,
    otherwise a raster identified by its content (png, jpeg, webp, gif, bmp, ico, avif). (Image::load_from_memory_with_mime_type)
- Easing curve values are the same as the original. If two stage nodes have the same name, both are attached and the later one stays in the name table (same as the original).
  If a parent is itself or forms a cycle, the node is attached to the stage parent. load_from_text and create_from_json_asset also exist in the original.
