툰 HDR 마무리. (vanilla.js graphics3d/toon/t:
Toon HDR finishing. (ToonPostProcess of vanilla.js graphics3d/toon/toonpostprocess.js)
- Outputs linear color drawn to a float render target to the screen with bloom, exposure, tone mapping and gamma.
- Combines the engine's RenderTarget (half-float color, depth), BloomEffect (or MultiLevelBloomEffect) and FullscreenPass.
- Usage: after ToonRenderer::set_hdr_output(true)
  begin(gl, background linear color) → draw with ToonRenderer → end(gl, output framebuffer, viewport)
  end (resolves first if multisampled) computes bloom and draws the tone-mapped color into the output framebuffer (screen if None). To mix with 2D, call Graphic::restore_render_state after it.
- Constructor options: new_with_options(gl, width, height, ToonPostProcessOptions { sample_count, use_float_color, depth_bits, use_depth_texture }) (the options of the original constructor, new uses the default options, same as now: RGBA16F, depth 16, no multisampling)
  If sample_count is 2 or more, the scene is drawn to a multisampled (MSAA) renderbuffer and resolved to a texture before end. Reduced to a count the device supports. (get_sample_count, set_sample_count)
  depth_bits 24 means 24-bit depth. (scenes with a distant far plane) use_depth_texture keeps the scene depth as a texture. (used by set_lit_area)
- Color space: linear color is written to the scene render target. (ToonRenderer::set_hdr_output(true), ToonScreenOutline::set_hdr_output(true), ToonVfx colors are also treated as linear)
  Games that wrote gamma-encoded color g to the float target and converted back with g^2.2 in compositing should convert those values to linear beforehand. Colors become c^2.2, and a brightness multiplier k applied on the gamma side becomes linear k^2.2.
  (e.g. 1.37 is linear 2, 1.6 is 2.81, 2.08 is 5, brightness 1.6 with multiplier 1.6 gives (1.6 x 1.6)^2.2 = 7.9) Bloom threshold and knee are linear brightness.
- Devices that cannot use float targets: even with use_float_color (default true), if is_float_color_supported is false, RGBA8 targets are built. (get_use_float_color is false)
  That case and use_float_color: false take the LDR path. The scene is drawn in screen color (gamma-encoded color, ToonRenderer::set_hdr_output(false)), and compositing adds bloom without tone mapping and gamma and applies only color grading.
- Bloom: default is a half-resolution 9-tap Gaussian (BloomEffect, threshold 0.9 ~ 1.6, ping-pong targets RGBA8, RGBA16F with set_bloom_float_color).
  Giving set_bloom_levels(gl, level count, threshold, knee) a level count of 1 or more switches to MultiLevelBloomEffect (halves down then scales up with a tent filter while adding, targets at the same precision as the scene). 0 restores the default. Strength is applied to both by set_bloom.
- Tone mapping is the ACES approximation (Krzysztof Narkowicz 2016, whose post lets it be used under CC0 or MIT). Exposure (set_exposure) is multiplied in before mapping, then sRGB gamma is applied.
- Color grading: after gamma, applies in order brightness (set_brightness, toward 1 inside the lit area set_lit_area), saturation, color tone (multiplies a color normalized to brightness 1), fog light (pulls dark areas toward that color), contrast, edge darkening. (set_color_grade, set_vignette)
  Defaults are brightness 1, saturation 1, contrast 1, color tone 0, fog light 0, edge 0, so there is no grading.
- Resolution scale: with set_resolution_scale(gl, scale), the scene target is built at output size x scale and scaled up to end's viewport (linear filtering) for output. (to render only 3D at a lower resolution while leaving UI at device pixels, default 1)
- Outputting inside a node rectangle: resize(rectangle width, height) → begin → draw (leave ToonRenderer's screen rectangle cleared) → end(None, [x, drawing buffer height - y - height, width, height]).
- Differences from the original: settings that rebuild GL objects (set_sample_count, set_resolution_scale, set_bloom_levels, set_bloom_float_color) take gl and return a Result.
색 글리프 래스터. (이모지 글꼴의 색 글리프를 프리멀티플라이드 RGBA:
Color glyph raster. (color glyphs of emoji fonts to premultiplied RGBA)
- In the original, the browser's Canvas2D draws color glyphs in their own colors. Only the alpha of fillStyle applies, not its color, and strokeText also fills color glyphs in their own colors without stroking an outline.
  The Rust version reads the font's color glyph data directly and draws it. Like Chrome, it does not draw OT-SVG glyphs.
- Bitmaps: extracts and decodes the PNG and premultiplied BGRA of sbix (Apple Color Emoji) and CBDT/CBLC (the Noto Color Emoji bitmap version), and fits them to the font size.
  The strike used is the smallest one at or above the font size among strikes that have the glyph, otherwise the largest. (Apple Color Emoji has glyphs missing from some strikes) Shrinking uses area averaging, enlarging uses interpolation between two points.
  The position is the strike's pixel position value (the offset of the image's bottom left from the pen origin) scaled by the font size ratio.
  For bitmap-only CBDT fonts, the advance and pixel box are the strike's glyph metrics (integer advance) and image box scaled by the font size ratio, like Chrome on Linux (FreeType and Skia). (read_bitmap_glyph_advance, read_bitmap_glyph_bounds)
- Outlines: COLR/CPAL v0 (one outline per layer in one color) and v1 (gradients, transforms, clipping, compositing). Received through ttf-parser's Painter and painted directly.
  Outlines flatten curves into line segments and compute coverage with area accumulation (the same method as font-rs, nonzero winding).
  Paints (solid color, linear (three points), radial between two circles, sweep gradient) are evaluated at pixel centers. Outside the ends of the color line follows Pad, Repeat, Reflect, and colors are blended in straight alpha.
  Compositing does COLR's 28 modes (Porter-Duff and W3C blending) in premultiplied color. The palette is number 0, and the text color (palette index 0xFFFF) is white. (glyphs are baked in white and the color is multiplied when drawing)
  A v1 paint fills the current clip region. Without a clip (v0) it fills the last received outline.
- ttf-parser is the one re-exported by rustybuzz. (the same face as the shaping face)
문자열 텍스처 캐시.\n- 원본은 오프스크린 2D 캔버스에 fillTex:
String texture cache.
- The original bakes strings into an offscreen 2D canvas with fillText / strokeText and uses it as a texture. (LRU limit 512)
- Desktop places glyphs with text shaping (textshaping.rs: bidirectional ordering, rustybuzz shaping), rasterizes them (fontdue, skrifa outlines for variable fonts, CoreText for Mac color emoji) and bakes the string into one image.
  The limit and the key fields (mode, paragraph direction, font string, line width, scale, text) are the same as the original.
  The original concatenates the key into a string. Here, to avoid building a string on every lookup, it looks up by the key's hash and compares keys one by one within the same hash.
- Characters are baked in white and the color is multiplied when drawing. (not rebaked when the color changes)
  Color glyphs (emoji) are baked in their own colors on top of the white text. The original also places a canvas filled with fillText in white, so emoji are baked in their own colors and multiplied by the same color when drawing.
  Even when baking as an outline (Stroke), color glyphs are not stroked and are placed in their colors as is. (same as Chrome strokeText)
- The font string is read in the same form as Canvas2D font (CSS font shorthand). Examples: "16px DOSGothic", "bold 24px default", "italic 500 16px default", "12pt 'A B', C, sans-serif"
  Sizes in CSS units other than px (including ex, ch, cap, ic, lh, rem, viewport units), named sizes and calc() are read like the Chrome canvas, and "/line-height" is skipped.
  For a comma-separated name list, each character is looked up starting from the faces of the earlier names. (same as a browser font list, parse_font_string)
- Like the original document.fonts, fonts put several faces (weight, style, character range) under one name. (register_font_face)
  Selection follows the CSS order, and if there is no italic face, synthetic italic (slant 1/4), if there is no bold face, synthetic bold is applied per glyph. (textshaping.rs)
- Characters missing from the name's faces are looked up in the default font, the system font chain, the standard font (desktop, Chrome's -webkit-standard), then the fallback font. (the same role as browser font fallback)
  If no face is found for any name in the list (only missing names other than default), the standard font is placed before the default font, like Chrome.
  The desktop system font chain (set_system_font_chain) is the names of the original SYSTEM_FONT_STRING found in the operating system fonts, and when enabled, names in the font string that were not registered are also
  looked up in the operating system fonts. A face is read the first time a character of that weight and style is used. (platform/desktop/systemfont.rs)
  Fallback fonts are chosen by the operating system. (set_system_font_fallback_enabled, asks for a bold face separately when bold is requested) If candidate files are given (add_fallback_font_candidate), they are used first.
  Candidate files are read when used. Emoji presentation characters read candidates with color glyph tables first, other characters read candidates without color glyph tables first. (only the table list is peeked first)
- When a new font face is registered, only strings baked with font strings using that name and containing characters in that face's character range are dropped. (the original invalidateFontFaces)
  As in the original, this happens only when turned on with set_rebake_text_on_font_load. (the engine turns it on with EngineConfiguration.rebake_text_on_font_load, off by default)
  When off, text baked with another font before loading stays until it is pushed out of the cache. Removing faces and reordering drop regardless of this setting.
  Changing the default font or fallback font drops everything.
- The web always bakes and measures with the browser Canvas2D as in the original. (platform/web/systemfont.rs) Registered font bytes are added to document.fonts as FontFace so the browser picks and draws them.
  When the registered font finishes loading (loadingdone), baked text is dropped at the start of the frame. Desktop bakes with the shaping and rasterizing above.
- Text antialiasing (set_text_antialias_enabled, the original setTextAntialiasEnabled): when off, the alpha of baked characters is split into 0 and 255 at a threshold of 128 and the texture is sampled with NEAREST.
  Projects that draw pixel fonts at integer multiples of their design size turn it off. In the original it is a module global value and already baked characters are left as is.
  Here the cache holds it and puts the on/off state in the key, so after changing it the next drawn text is baked that way right away. (rasterize_text does not take it, like the original ShadowText)
- Text measuring (measure_text) does not measure again if the font string and text are the same. (the original measureTextMetrics cache, 2048 entries)
  The original drops the one least recently used each time it overflows. Here, when it overflows it drops the least recently used half at once. (finding one at a time would scan 2048 entries on every measure after overflowing)
  It is cleared when a new font is registered. (the original clears it when a web font finishes loading) measure_text takes &self, so the cache is in a RefCell.
- Loading faces on demand (watch_unresolved_family_characters, take_unresolved_family_characters): the original browser loads a registered FontFace when drawing characters in its character range.
  The Rust version collects characters not in the ranges of registered faces from text measured or baked with watched names, and UIFont takes them out in update and loads the pieces for those characters.
- Measuring without a Graphic (measure_text_without_graphic): the original measures text anywhere with a shared 2D canvas. The Rust version, each time a font is registered,
  publishes the font list (Rc) to a single-thread global and measures with that list. Used when UI layout needs to know the number of text lines before drawing. (UIConfirmWindow)
글자 모양 짓기. (글꼴 얼굴 고르기, 양방향 정렬, 글자 모양 잇기,:
Text shaping. (font face selection, bidirectional ordering, glyph shaping, glyph rasterization)
- In the original, the browser's Canvas2D does all of this. (CSS font selection, the bidirectional algorithm, HarfBuzz shaping, Skia rasterization)
  The Rust version follows the same steps with crates:
  - Font faces (FontFaceDescriptors): like CSS @font-face, several faces with different weight, style and character ranges (unicode-range) sit under one name.
    Selection follows the CSS Fonts order (style → weight), and faces with the same weight and style split the drawing by character range. Faces loaded later come first.
  - Bidirectional ordering: unicode-bidi (UAX #9). The paragraph direction is given by the baking side. (the original canvas.direction)
  - Shaping: rustybuzz (a port of HarfBuzz). Places Arabic joining, ligatures, kerning and combining mark positions like the browser does.
  - Rasterization: fontdue's glyph index rasterization. If there is no bold face, fake bold is applied per glyph, and if there is no italic face, fake italic.
    Color glyphs (sbix, CBDT, COLR) are drawn in their own colors by colorglyph.rs. Like Chrome, fake italic is applied to them and fake bold is not.
- Emoji presentation: faces of the name list are used first whenever they have the glyph, regardless of color. In the system fallback stage, VS16 (FE0F), Emoji_Presentation characters, skin tone modifiers, flags, keycaps and tag sequences
  pick a face with color glyphs first, and everything else (including VS15) picks a non-color face first. Clusters with a variation selector accept only a face matching that presentation, even in the name list.
  Chrome draws ❤️ (FE0F) with a color emoji font even if the specified font has a monochrome ❤, and a plain ❤ with the specified font. (checked with Canvas2D in Chrome on Mac)
  Chrome 157 on Linux draws a plain 😀 in "16px DejaVu Sans" with DejaVu Sans's monochrome glyph. (measureText in CI)
- Fake italic and fake bold use the same values Chromium gives Skia:
  a skew of 1/4 (setSkewX(-SK_Scalar1 / 4) in font_platform_data.cc), and bold widens the outline by stroking it with a thickness of 1/24 (9px or less) ~ 1/32 (36px or more) of the font size.
  (kStdFakeBoldInterpKeys / Values in Skia SkTextFormatParams.h) Neither changes the advance.
  Fake bold is used when the requested weight is 600 or more and the chosen face is below 600. (Blink kBoldThreshold)
- LoadedFont holds the font bytes together with the rustybuzz face. (self_cell, the face borrows the bytes) When the registration is removed and nothing uses it anymore, the bytes are freed too.
  Several faces from the same file (the weights in a TTC, weight instances of a variable font) share the bytes (Rc).
- Font collections like TTC are read by choosing a face index (face_index). (find_collection_face_index chooses by weight and style)
- Variable fonts (the wght axis in fvar) make weight instances from axis values. (variation_list of create_from_shared_bytes) rustybuzz reads the axis values for shaping,
  but fontdue cannot read axis values for rasterization and cannot draw the outlines of variable fonts like Mac SFNS, so variable fonts get axis-applied outlines from skrifa and are drawn with colorglyph's area accumulation rasterizer.
  (Chrome also draws variable font weights from axis values)
- Optical size (the opsz axis) and the tracking table (trak): Chrome sets a font's opsz axis to the font size. (the initial value auto of font-optical-sizing, FontPlatformDataFromCTFont in Mac
  font_platform_data_mac.mm, font_custom_platform_data.cc for web fonts on every OS. Not applied to Windows and Linux system fonts)
  Shaping gives HarfBuzz the font size as ptem to add the AAT trak table's tracking. (GetScaledFont in harfbuzz_face.cc, on Mac the advances of fonts with trak and without sbix
  are computed with HarfBuzz instead of CoreText) The Rust version also applies opsz and adds trak at the baking size (the original enlarges the px in the font string by the bake scale).
  trak is added here, not by rustybuzz, the way HarfBuzz 15 (hb-aat-layout-trak-table.hh) does. Between sizes it interpolates linearly without rounding, outside the first and last entries of the table
  it uses the end values, and it is added only to the advance of the first glyph of a cluster. Not applied to fonts without a STAT table.
  (rustybuzz 0.20 rounds to integer font units, extrapolates outside the table, adds half to x_offset too, and does not look at STAT)
  The Mac system UI font (SFNS, opsz 17 ~ 96, initially 28) matches Chrome at 16px with opsz 17 and trak -40 units. (color emoji keep the CoreText advance as is)
- Per-word shaping: Chrome's canvas (SegmentWord in platform/fonts/plain_text_node.cc) splits text into words and shapes them separately. There is no kerning or ligature across spaces.
  Spaces (U+0020), tabs and ZWSP are one each, and CJK characters and emoji are separate per character. (find_chrome_word_end) The canvas turns tabs, line feeds, form feeds and carriage returns into spaces.
- Mac: glyphs are drawn with CoreText like the original Chrome on Mac. (platform/desktop/coretextglyph.rs) Non-color glyphs are A8 masks with the same settings as Chrome Canvas2D (font smoothing,
  undoing the CoreGraphics gamma, gamma pre-correction by the text color luminance, 1/4 pixel subpixel positions), and color emoji fonts (sbix) read from files are CoreText color drawings. (rasterize_glyph_at)
  The advance of color emoji is multiplied by the ratio CoreText enlarges drawing at small sizes and rounded to integer pixels. (20 at 16px, 16 at 13px, same as Chrome measureText)
